3 miles; 1,000 feet above; 2,000 feet horizontal; 500 feet below.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 10,000 ft MSL 미만 Class E 공역의 기본 VFR 기상최저치는 비행시정 3 SM, 구름 아래 500 ft·위 1,000 ft·수평 2,000 ft이다.
questions.explanation_en: In Class E airspace below 10,000 ft. MSL, the basic VFR weather minimums are in-flight visibility of 3 SM and a distance from clouds of 500 ft. below, 1,000 ft. above, and 2,000 ft. horizontal. Answer (A) is incorrect. The minimum visibility required is 3 SM, not 2,000 ft. Answer (B) is incorrect. In Class E airspace at or above 10,000 ft., not below 10,000 ft., the minimum visibility is 5 SM.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the minimum in-flight visibility and distance from clouds required in VFR conditions above clouds at 13,500 feet MSL (above 1,200 feet AGL) during daylight hours in uncontrolled airspace?

choices.text: 5 miles; 1,000 feet above; 2,000 feet horizontal; 500 feet below.
3 miles; 1,000 feet above; 1 mile horizontal; 1,000 feet below.
5 miles; 1,000 feet above; 1 mile horizontal; 1,000 feet below.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 1,200 ft AGL 초과이면서 10,000 ft MSL 이상인 비관제공역에서 기본 VFR 기상최저치는 비행시정 5 SM, 구름 위·아래 각 1,000 ft, 수평 1 SM이다.
questions.explanation_en: In uncontrolled airspace at more than 1,200 ft. AGL and at or above 10,000 ft. MSL, the basic VFR weather minimums are in-flight visibility of 5 SM and a distance from clouds of 1,000 ft. above or below and 1 SM horizontal. Answer (A) is incorrect. The minimum cloud distances for VFR in uncontrolled airspace above 1,200 ft. AGL and below, not above, 10,000 ft. MSL are 1,000 ft. above, 2,000 ft. horizontal, and 500 ft. below. Answer (B) is incorrect. Visibility minimum is 5 SM, not 3 SM.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A flight is to be conducted in VFR-on-Top conditions at 12,500 feet MSL (above 1,200 feet AGL). What is the in-flight visibility and distance from clouds required for operation during daylight hours in class E airspace?

choices.text: 5 miles; 1,000 feet above; 2,000 feet horizontal; 500 feet below.
5 miles; 1,000 feet above; 1 mile horizontal; 1,000 feet below.
3 miles; 1,000 feet above; 2,000 feet horizontal; 1,000 feet below.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 10,000 ft MSL 이상 Class E 공역의 기본 VFR 기상최저치는 비행시정 5 SM, 구름 위·아래 각 1,000 ft, 수평 1 SM이다.
questions.explanation_en: In Class E airspace at or above 10,000 ft. MSL, the basic VFR weather minimums are in-flight visibility of 5 SM and a distance from clouds of 1,000 ft. above or below and 1 SM horizontal. Answer (A) is incorrect. The distance from cloud requirements listed are for below, not above, 10,000 ft. MSL. Answer (C) is incorrect. The visibility requirement is 5 SM, not 3 SM, and the horizontal separation requirement from clouds is 1 SM, not 2,000 ft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the minimum in-flight visibility and distance from clouds required for an airplane operating less than 1,200 feet AGL during daylight hours in uncontrolled airspace?

choices.text: 3 miles; 1,000 feet above; 2,000 feet horizontal; 500 feet below.
1 mile; 500 feet above; 1,000 feet horizontal; 500 feet below.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 1,200 ft AGL 미만 비관제공역의 주간 기본 VFR 기상최저치는 비행시정 1 SM이며 구름을 피하면 된다(clear of clouds).
questions.explanation_en: In uncontrolled airspace below 1,200 ft. AGL, the basic VFR weather minimums during daylight hours are in-flight visibility of 1 SM and clear of clouds. Answer (A) is incorrect. Three SM visibility, 1,000 ft. above, 500 ft. below, and 2,000 ft. horizontal are the VFR weather minimums for a flight in controlled, not uncontrolled airspace. Answer (C) is incorrect. The distance from clouds is clear of clouds, not 500 ft. above and below and 1,000 ft. horizontal.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the minimum in-flight visibility and distance from clouds required for an airplane operating less than 1,200 feet AGL under special VFR during daylight hours in controlled airspace?

choices.text: 1 mile; 2,000 feet above; 2,000 feet horizontal; 500 feet below.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 1,200 ft AGL 미만 관제공역에서 Special VFR로 운항할 때는 구름을 피하면 되며, 이륙·착륙을 위해 지상시정이 최소 1 SM이어야 한다. 지상시정이 보고되지 않으면 이륙·착륙 중 비행시정이 최소 1 SM이어야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: In controlled airspace below 1,200 ft. AGL when operating an airplane under special VFR, the distance-from-clouds requirement is clear of clouds. No one may take off or land an airplane under special VFR unless ground visibility is at least 1 SM. If ground visibility is not reported, the in-flight visibility during takeoff or landing must be at least 1 SM. Answer (A) is incorrect. Special VFR permits operating clear of clouds. Answer (B) is incorrect. Special VFR permits clear of clouds and a minimum visibility of 1 SM, not 3 SM.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 223 below and in color on page 446.) Hold line markings at the intersection of taxiways and runways consist of four lines (two solid and two dashed) that extend across the width of the taxiway. These lines are

choices.text: white in color and the dashed lines are nearest the runway.
yellow in color and the dashed lines are nearest the runway.
yellow in color and the solid lines are nearest the runway. Figure 223. Airport Sign and Marking.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 유도로/활주로 교차부의 정지위치 표시는 노란색 4개 선(실선 2개, 점선 2개)으로 구성된다. 항공기가 정지해야 하는 쪽에는 실선이 있고, 활주로 쪽에 점선이 위치한다.
questions.explanation_en: Holding position markings for taxiway/ runway intersections consist of four yellow lines -- two solid and two dashed, spaced 6 in. apart and extending across the width of the taxiway or runway. The solid lines are always on the side where the aircraft is to hold (i.e., away from the runway). Thus, the dashed lines are nearest the runway. Answer (A) is incorrect. Hold line markings are always yellow, not white, in color. Answer (C) is incorrect. The solid lines are farthest from, not nearest to, the runway (i.e., on the side where the aircraft is to hold).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 223 above and in color on page 446.) The “runway hold position” sign denotes

choices.text: an entrance to a taxiway from a runway.
an entrance to a runway from a taxiway.
an area protected for an aircraft approaching a runway.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Runway holding position sign은 빨간 배경에 흰색 표기로, 유도로 또는 교차 활주로에서 활주로 진입 지점을 나타낸다. 활주로 진입허가를 받지 못했으면 이 표지와 정지선에서 대기해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Runway holding position signs, consisting of white numbering on a red background, are found adjacent to runway holding position markings that are painted on a taxiway or a runway. These signs and markings indicate the point at which aircraft are expected to hold short of a runway if an ATC clearance to proceed onto that runway has not been received or without making sure of adequate separation at an airport without an operating control tower. Runway holding position signs therefore denote the entrance to a runway from a taxiway or from an intersecting runway. Answer (A) is incorrect. A direction sign, not a runway holding position sign, denotes the entrance to a taxiway from a runway. Answer (C) is incorrect. A runway approach area holding position sign, not a runway holding position sign, denotes an area protected for aircraft approaching or departing a runway.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 224 on page 295 and in color on page 446.) The weather is 600-1. While taxiing, you come across this signage and marking. You

choices.text: should hold short and request clarification of your taxi instructions from ATC.
should expect to continue as the weather is greater than 200-3/4.
can expect to ignore the signage and marking as you are only taxiing to the compass rose.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 기상이 800-2 미만이면 ILS critical area를 보호한다. 이때는 정지선을 넘지 말고 ATC에 유도 지시를 재확인해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: The ILS critical area is protected when the weather is less than 800-2. The proper action is to hold short and contact ATC for clarification of your taxi instructions. Answer (B) is incorrect. You should not expect to continue any time the weather is less than 800-2. The proper action is to hold short and contact ATC for further instructions. Answer (C) is incorrect. Ignoring the signage could cause ILS course distortion to an arriving aircraft that is between the ILS final approach fix and the airport.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 224 above and in color on page 446.) When instructed by ATC to “hold short of a runway (ILS critical area, etc.),” the pilot should stop

choices.text: with the nose gear on the hold line.
so that no part of the aircraft extends beyond the hold line.
so the flight deck area of the aircraft is even with the hold line.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. ATC로부터 활주로 또는 ILS critical area 앞에서 hold short 지시를 받으면 항공기의 어느 부분도 정지위치 표시를 넘지 않도록 정지해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: When instructed by ATC to hold short of a runway (ILS critical area, etc.), you should stop so no part of your aircraft extends beyond the holding position marking. Answer (A) is incorrect. You should stop before, not with the nose gear on, the hold line. Answer (C) is incorrect. You should stop before, not so the flight deck is even with, the hold line.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 228 below and in color on page 446.) The sign shown is an example of

choices.text: an airport directional sign. Figure 228. Airport Sign.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 그림은 mandatory instruction sign의 하나인 runway holding position sign이다. 빨간 배경에 흰 글씨이며 활주로·critical area 진입 지점 또는 진입 금지 구역을 표시한다.
questions.explanation_en: The image depicts a runway holding position sign, which is a type of mandatory instruction sign. These signs have a red background with a white inscription and are used to denote the entrance to a runway or critical area and areas where aircraft are prohibited from entering. Answer (B) is incorrect. Though a runway holding position sign shows the designation of the intersecting runways, the purpose of this type of mandatory instruction sign is to denote the entrance to a runway, not to notify the pilot of the associated runway headings. Answer (C) is incorrect. The sign shown is an example of a mandatory instruction sign, not a direction sign. Direction signs have a yellow background with a black inscription that identifies the designations of the intersecting taxiways leading out of the intersection.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 228 above and in color on page 446.) During landing roll, you see this sign on either side of the runway. This indicates

choices.text: you are near a high-speed exit of runway 04-22.
you are ready for an intersection takeoff from runway 4.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 이 표지는 활주로와 교차하는 유도로 또는 다른 활주로와 교차하는 활주로의 정지위치에 설치된다. 이 경우 교차 활주로는 04와 22이다.
questions.explanation_en: This sign would be located at the holding position on taxiways that intersect a runway or on runways that intersect other runways. In this case, the intersecting runways are 04 and 22. Answer (B) is incorrect. The high-speed exit is also referred to as a long radius exit or turn-off taxiway. The high speed taxiway (up to 60 knots) is designed to expedite aircraft turning off the runway after landing, thus reducing runway occupancy time and is indicated by green and yellow lights on the runway to the left or right of the runway centerline. Answer (C) is incorrect. You have just landed. An intersection takeoff does not begin at intersecting runways.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 227 below and in color on page 446.) The “taxiway ending” marker

choices.text: provides general taxiing direction to named taxiway.
identifies area where aircraft are prohibited. Figure 227. Airport Sign.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Taxiway ending marker는 해당 지점 이후로 유도로가 계속되지 않음을 나타낸다.
questions.explanation_en: The taxiway ending marker indicates that the taxiway does not continue beyond a certain point. Answer (B) is incorrect. The taxiway ending marker indicates that the taxiway does not continue. It does not provide directions or name the taxiway. Answer (C) is incorrect. The taxiway ending marker does not suggest areas where aircraft are prohibited. It only indicates that the taxiway does not continue.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: You have just landed at JFK and the tower tells you to call ground control when clear of the runway. You are considered clear of the runway when

choices.text: the aft end of the aircraft is even with the taxiway location sign.
the flight deck area of the aircraft is even with the hold line.
all parts of the aircraft have crossed the hold line.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 활주로를 이탈하는 항공기는 항공기의 모든 부분이 해당 runway holding position marking을 완전히 통과해야 활주로를 벗어난 것으로 간주된다.
questions.explanation_en: An aircraft exiting a runway is not considered clear of the runway until all parts of the aircraft have crossed the applicable holding position marking. Answer (A) is incorrect. You are clear when the entire aircraft has crossed the hold line, not when the aft end is even with the taxiway location sign. Answer (B) is incorrect. You are clear when the entire aircraft has crossed the hold line, not when the flight deck is even with the hold line.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Upon landing you

choices.text: may stop on the runway until you determine which taxiway you should use.
may stop on the taxiway when your aircraft tail is clear of the boundary line.
should continue on to the ramp without delay without further ATC authorization.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 착륙 후에는 가능한 첫 유도로 또는 ATC가 지시한 유도로로 활주로를 이탈하고, 해당 활주로의 holding position marking을 완전히 지나야 한다. 이후 추가 지상 이동은 ATC 지시 또는 비관제공항에서의 안전 확인에 따라야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: After landing, the pilot should exit the runway at the first available taxiway or on a taxiway as instructed by ATC. The pilot is expected to taxi clear of the landing runway by taxiing beyond the runway holding position markings associated with the landing runway, even if that requires the aircraft to protrude into or across another taxiway or ramp area. Answer (A) is incorrect. The pilot should not stop on the runway after landing to consider taxiway options. Answer (C) is incorrect. The pilot should not taxi beyond the point (s)he has cleared the runway without clearance from ATC or, in the case of a non-towered airport, until (s)he can ensure his/her way is clear and taxiing will not impact any other aircraft, structures, or obstacles along his or her path to the ramp.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When holding short of a runway, what lines do you see?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Hold short marking은 노란색 4개 선(실선 2개, 점선 2개)으로 구성되며 실선은 항상 항공기가 대기해야 하는 쪽에 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The hold short markings consist of four yellow lines, two solid and two dashed, spaced six or twelve inches apart, and extending across the width of the taxiway or runway. The solid lines are always on the side where the aircraft is to hold. Answer (B) is incorrect. The lines are painted yellow, not white. Answer (C) is incorrect. The hold short lines are painted yellow and consist of four lines, not two.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: ILS critical area sign indicates

choices.text: the edge of the ILS critical area.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. ILS critical area sign은 ILS critical area의 경계를 나타낸다. ILS 접근이 사용 중이면 항공기는 이 표지 위치를 완전히 지난 뒤 정지해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: An ILS critical area sign indicates the edge, or boundary, of the ILS critical area. Answer (A) is incorrect. The ILS critical area sign is seen when exiting the runway. It indicates the boundary, or edge, of the ILS critical area. If the ILS approach is in use, aircraft should taxi beyond the sign’s location before stopping. Answer (C) is incorrect. Although the ILS critical area sign indicates the boundary, or edge, of the ILS critical area, it does not indicate an exit boundary. When the ILS is in use, aircraft should taxi beyond the sign’s location before stopping.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 156 below and in color on page 446.) This sign, when seen from the top looking downward by the pilot on the runway, indicates

choices.text: a point at which the pilot should contact ground control without being instructed by the tower.
a point at which the aircraft will be clear of the runway.
the point at which the emergency arresting gear is stretched across the runway. Figure 156. Airport Sign.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Fig. 156은 runway boundary sign이다. 활주로를 빠져나오는 조종사가 볼 수 있도록 포장면의 holding position marking 옆에 설치되며, 항공기가 활주로를 완전히 벗어났는지 판단하는 시각적 기준을 제공한다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 156 is a runway boundary sign. This sign, which faces the runway and is visible to the pilot exiting the runway, is located adjacent to the holding position marking on the pavement. It is intended to provide pilots with another visual cue they can use as a guide in deciding when they are clear of the runway. Answer (A) is incorrect. The pilot should contact ground control when advised by the tower, not after passing the runway boundary sign. Answer (C) is incorrect. Arresting gear that crosses over a runway is identified by solid yellow circles painted on the runway, not by a runway boundary sign.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 156 above and in color on page 446.) When you see this pavement marking from the flight deck, you

choices.text: can taxi past this point at your own risk.
must hold short until “Cleared” to taxi onto or past the runway.
may not cross the line until ATC allows you to “enter” or “cross” by instruction.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 문항은 pavement marking이라고 표현하지만 그림은 runway boundary sign이다. 이는 활주로를 빠져나오는 조종사가 활주로를 완전히 벗어났는지 판단하도록 돕는 시각적 표지이며, 항공기의 모든 부분이 활주로 가장자리를 지나고 holding position marking 너머로 계속 이동할 수 있을 때 clear of runway로 본다.
questions.explanation_en: Though the question refers to a “pavement marking,” the image depicts a runway boundary sign. This sign, which faces the runway and is visible to the pilot exiting the runway, is located adjacent to the holding position marking on the pavement. The runway boundary sign is intended to provide pilots with another visual cue, which they can use as a guide in deciding when they are clear of the runway. After landing, pilots are expected to taxi clear of the runway unless otherwise directed by ATC. An aircraft is considered clear of the runway when all parts of the aircraft are past the runway edge and there are no restrictions to its continued movement beyond the runway holding position markings. Answer (B) is incorrect. The image depicts a runway boundary sign, not a runway holding position marking. After landing, pilots are expected to taxi clear of the runway unless otherwise directed by ATC. The runway boundary sign is intended to provide pilots with another visual cue, which they can use as a guide in deciding when they are clear of the runway. Additionally, in order to preclude misunderstandings in radio communications, ATC will not use the word “cleared” in conjunction with authorization for aircraft to taxi. Answer (C) is incorrect. The image depicts a runway boundary sign, not a runway holding position marking. After landing, pilots are expected to taxi clear of the runway unless otherwise directed by ATC. The runway boundary sign is intended to provide pilots with another visual cue, which they can use as a guide in deciding when they are clear of the runway.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 157 below and in color on page 446.) This is an example of

choices.text: an ILS Critical Area Holding Position Sign.
an ILS Critical Area Boundary Sign.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 157은 ILS critical area boundary sign이다. 포장면의 ILS holding position marking 옆에 설치되며, critical area를 벗어나는 조종사가 ILS critical area를 완전히 벗어났는지 판단하는 시각적 기준을 제공한다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 157 is an ILS critical area boundary sign. This sign is located adjacent to the ILS holding position marking on the pavement and can be seen by pilots leaving the critical area. The sign is intended to provide pilots with another visual cue they can use as a guide in deciding when they are clear of the ILS critical area. Answer (A) is incorrect. An ILS critical area holding position sign has a red, not yellow, background with the inscription “ILS” in white, not a graphic depiction of the ILS pavement holding position marking. Answer (B) is incorrect. A runway boundary sign depicts the pavement holding position marking, i.e., four lines -- two solid and two dashed.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 157 below and in color on page 446.) The current airport weather is 600 and 1 mile. As you taxi, this sign comes into view, you

choices.text: can expect to ignore the sign since you are just taxiing to the compass rose.
should hold short and request clarification of your taxi instructions from ATC.
should expect taxiing past this point since the weather is better than 200 and 3/4 mile. Figure 157. Airport Sign.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 주어진 기상에서는 ILS가 운용 중이라고 보는 것이 타당하다. ILS critical area를 침범하지 말고 ATC에 유도 지시를 재확인해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Given the weather conditions, it is safe to assume that the ILS would, in fact, be operational. You should remain clear of the ILS critical area and request clarification instructions from ATC. Answer (A) is incorrect. Taxiing through the ILS critical area when the ILS is in operation could cause an arriving aircraft to perform a missed approach. When instrument approach operations are being conducted, you should always remain clear of the ILS critical area and ask for clarification from ATC. Answer (C) is incorrect. The weather does not have to be at ILS minimums for the ILS to be in operation. Whenever the weather is below visual approach minimums you should remain clear of the ILS critical area and request clarification instructions from ATC.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 157 above and in color on page 446.) This sign identifies

choices.text: the edge of the ILS critical area.
the exit boundary for the runway protected area.
the area where an aircraft is prohibited from entering.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 이 표지는 ILS critical area의 가장자리를 나타내며 ILS Critical Area Boundary sign과 혼동할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: This sign is the edge of “ILS critical area.” It can be confused with the ILS Critical Area Boundary sign. The other answer choices do not pertain to an ILS. Answer (B) is incorrect. The exit boundary for the runway protected area is a hold line consisting of four yellow lines, two solid and two dashed lines extending across the taxi way. The protected side is the side of the dashed lines. Answer (C) is incorrect. The sign prohibiting aircraft from entry into an area is red with a white circle and a white dash line in the middle.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Holding position signs have

choices.text: white inscriptions on a red background.
red inscriptions on a white background.
yellow inscriptions on a red background.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Holding position sign은 빨간 배경에 흰색 표기로 되어 있으며 활주로 또는 critical area의 진입 지점을 나타낸다.
questions.explanation_en: A holding position sign has a red background with a white inscription and is used to denote an entrance to a runway or critical area. Answer (B) is incorrect. A holding position sign has a white, not red, inscription on a red, not white, background. Answer (C) is incorrect. A holding position sign has a white, not yellow, inscription on a red background.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 129 above and in color on page 445.) What is the runway distance remaining at “A” for a daytime takeoff on runway 9?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fig. 129의 A는 Runway 27 threshold에서 1,000 ft 떨어진 runway aiming point marking이다. Runway 9에서 이륙 중이라면 A 지점에서 남은 활주로는 1,000 ft이다.
questions.explanation_en: “A” on Fig. 129 refers to the runway aiming point marking that is 1,000 ft. from the threshold of runway 27. Since runway 9 is being used for a takeoff, “A” would indicate 1,000 ft. of runway remaining. Answer (B) is incorrect. The 1,500-ft. distance of runway remaining is not marked on an FAA nonprecision runway. Answer (C) is incorrect. The figure of 2,000 ft. is the distance remaining on an ICAO, not an FAA, nonprecision instrument runway where the runway edge lights are amber.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: All runway hold markings consist of
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Runway hold marking은 유도로를 가로지르는 노란색 실선 2개와 점선 2개로 구성된다. 실선 쪽에서는 허가 없이 넘을 수 없고, 점선 쪽에서 활주로를 이탈할 때는 표시를 완전히 통과한 뒤 정지해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Runway hold markings consist of two dashed and two solid yellow lines extending across the taxiway near a runway. The two solid lines will be located on the taxiway (or landing runway for LAHSO operations) side of the taxiway, and the two dashed lines will be located on the runway side of the taxiway. The solid lines indicate that one cannot proceed past those lines without a clearance. The dashed lines indicate that they should be crossed completely before stopping. Answer (A) is incorrect. Markings consisting of two dashed and one solid yellow line is an enhanced taxiway center line. It is one solid line with one dashed line on both sides of the solid line. Answer (C) is incorrect. A marking consisting of one dashed and one solid yellow line is a movement area boundary line.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Airport information signs, used to provide destination or information, have

choices.text: yellow inscriptions on a black background.
white inscriptions on a black background.
black inscriptions on a yellow background.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Destination sign은 노란 배경에 검은 글씨로 공항 내 목적지를 표시한다.
questions.explanation_en: Destination signs have black inscriptions on yellow backgrounds indicating destinations on the airport. Answer (A) is incorrect. Taxiway location signs, not destination signs, have yellow inscriptions on black back-grounds. Answer (B) is incorrect. Runway distance remaining signs, not destination signs, have white inscriptions on black backgrounds.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Identify the runway distance remaining markers.

choices.text: Signs with increments of 1,000 feet distance remaining.
Red markers laterally placed across the runway at 3,000 feet from the end.
Yellow marker laterally placed across the runway with signs on the side denoting distance to end.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Runway distance remaining sign은 활주로 옆에 설치되어 남은 활주로 거리를 1,000 ft 단위로 표시한다. 검은 배경에 흰 숫자이며 야간·저시정 운항을 위해 조명된다.
questions.explanation_en: Runway distance remaining signs are located along the sides of the runway to indicate the remaining runway distance in increments of 1,000 ft. The signs have white numbers on a black background and are lighted for nighttime and low-visibility operations. Answer (B) is incorrect. Distance remaining markers are along the side of, not across, the runway and are black and white, not red. Answer (C) is incorrect. Distance remaining markers are signs along the side of, not across, the runway and are black and white, not yellow.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Taxiway centerline lead-off lights are color-coded to warn pilots that

choices.text: they are within the taxiway end environment or ILS critical area.
they are within the runway environment or run-up danger critical area.
they are within the runway environment or ILS critical area.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Taxiway centerline lead-off light는 활주로 이탈 시 시각 유도를 제공한다. 색상으로 항공기·차량이 활주로 환경 또는 더 제한적인 ILS critical area 안에 있는지 경고한다.
questions.explanation_en: Taxiway centerline lead-off lights provide visual guidance to persons exiting the runway. They are color-coded to warn pilots and vehicle drivers that they are within the runway environment or instrument landing system (ILS) critical area, whichever is more restrictive. Answer (A) is incorrect. Taxiway centerline lead-off lights warn pilots that they are within the runway environment, not the taxiway end environment. Answer (B) is incorrect. Taxiway centerline lead-off lights warn pilots that they are within the ILS critical area, not the run-up danger critical area.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the advantage of HIRL or MIRL on an IFR runway as compared to a VFR runway?

choices.text: Lights are closer together and easily distinguished from surrounding lights.
Amber lights replace white on the last 2,000 feet of runway for a caution zone.
Alternate red and white lights replace the white on the last 3,000 feet of runway for a caution zone.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. HIRL과 MIRL은 밝기 조절이 가능한 활주로 가장자리 등화이다. 가장자리 등은 기본적으로 흰색이며, 계기활주로에서는 마지막 2,000 ft 또는 활주로 길이의 절반 중 짧은 구간에서 황색(amber)으로 바뀌어 착륙 주의구역을 나타낸다.
questions.explanation_en: HIRL (high-intensity runway lights) and MIRL (medium-intensity runway lights) are runway edge light systems that have variable intensity controls. The runway edge lights are white, except that on instrument runways, amber replaces white on the last 2,000 ft. or half the runway length, whichever is less, to form a caution zone for landings. Answer (A) is incorrect. MIRL and HIRL are runway edge light systems and are not spaced closer together on instrument runways. Answer (C) is incorrect. Alternate red and white runway centerline, not runway edge, lights are on the last 3,000 ft. of a runway to the last 1,000 ft. of runway (the last 1,000 ft. of runway centerline lights are marked by red lights).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the purpose of REIL?

choices.text: To provide rapid and positive identification of the approach end of a particular runway.
Identification of the touchdown zone to prevent landing short.
Establish visual descent guidance information during an approach.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. REIL은 특정 활주로의 접근단을 빠르고 명확하게 식별하도록 설치한다. 주변에 다른 등화가 많아 활주로 식별이 어려운 경우 특히 효과적이다.
questions.explanation_en: Runway end identifier lights (REIL) are installed to provide rapid and positive identification of the approach end of a particular runway. REIL is effective for the identification of a runway surrounded by a preponderance of other lighting. Answer (B) is incorrect. The touchdown zone is identified by in-runway lighting of two rows of transverse light bars on either side of the runway centerline from 100 ft. to 3,000 ft. from the landing threshold. Answer (C) is incorrect. A VASI, not REIL, assists in providing visual descent guidance information during an approach.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Identify REIL.

choices.text: Amber lights for the first 2,000 feet of runway.
Green lights at the threshold and red lights at far end of runway.
Synchronized flashing lights laterally at each side of the runway threshold.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. REIL은 활주로 threshold 양쪽에 설치된 한 쌍의 동기식 섬광등으로 특정 활주로 접근단을 빠르고 확실하게 식별하게 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Runway end identifier lights (REIL) are installed to provide rapid and positive identification of the approach end of a particular runway. The system consists of a pair of synchronized flashing lights located laterally on each side of the runway threshold. REIL is effective for the identification of a runway surrounded by a preponderance of other lighting. Answer (A) is incorrect. Amber lights are used on the last, not first, 2,000 ft. of runway edge lights to form a caution zone on instrument runways. Answer (B) is incorrect. Green lights at the threshold mark the runway edge for landing aircraft, and red lights at the far end mark the runway edge to a departing or landing aircraft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 130 on page 301 and in color on page 445.) What is the runway distance remaining at “A” for a nighttime takeoff on runway 9?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Fig. 130의 A는 runway edge light이다. ICAO 비정밀 계기활주로에서는 마지막 2,000 ft 또는 활주로 길이의 절반 중 짧은 구간에서 흰색 대신 황색을 사용한다. 따라서 Runway 9 야간 이륙 중 황색 가장자리 등이 시작되면 남은 활주로는 2,000 ft이다.
questions.explanation_en: “A” on Fig. 130 refers to the runway edge lights, which are white. However, on ICAO nonprecision instrument runways, amber (yellow) replaces white on the last 2,000 ft. or half the runway length, whichever is less. At point “A” on Fig. 130, during a takeoff on runway 9 at night, the start of amber runway edge lights indicates that 2,000 ft. of runway remains. Answer (A) is incorrect. The beginning of yellow runway edge lights on an ICAO nonprecision instrument runway indicates 2,000 ft., not 1,000 ft., of runway remaining. Answer (C) is incorrect. The beginning of yellow runway edge lights on an ICAO nonprecision instrument runway indicates that 2,000 ft., not 2,500 ft., of runway remaining.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 130 above and in color on page 445.) What is the runway distance remaining at “B” for a daytime takeoff on runway 9?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 130의 B는 고정거리표시로, 착륙 threshold로부터의 거리를 약 500 ft 간격으로 약 3,000 ft까지 표시한다. Runway 9에서 주간 이륙 시 처음 만나는 B 표시는 활주로 끝까지 3,000 ft가 남았음을 뜻한다.
questions.explanation_en: “B” on Fig. 130 refers to fixed distance markings, which provide distance indication from the threshold of a landing position runway. The markers are spaced approximately every 500 ft. (150 meters) to a distance of approximately 3,000 ft. For a takeoff on runway 9 during the day, “B” indicates 3,000 ft. to the end of the runway because it is the first distance marker encountered. Answer (A) is incorrect. The marker at 2,000 ft. is the third, not first, distance marker encountered. Answer (B) is incorrect. The marker at 2,500 ft. is the second, not first, distance marker encountered.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 130 above and in color on page 445.) What is the runway distance remaining at “C” for a daytime takeoff on runway 9?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Fig. 130의 C는 약 500 ft 간격의 고정거리표시이다. Runway 9 주간 이륙 시 세 번째로 만나는 표시이므로 활주로 끝까지 2,000 ft가 남았다.
questions.explanation_en: “C” on Fig. 130 refers to fixed distance markings, which are spaced at approximately 500-ft. (150 meters) intervals from the threshold of a landing position runway to approximately 3,000 ft. During a daytime takeoff on runway 9, “C” is the third set of distance markings encountered. The first begins at 3,000 ft., the second is at 2,500 ft., and “C” is at 2,000 ft. from the end of the runway. Answer (A) is incorrect. The marker at 2,500 ft. is the second, not third, distance marker encountered. Answer (C) is incorrect. The marker at 1,500 ft. is the fourth, not third, distance marker encountered.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 130 above and in color on page 445.) What is the runway distance remaining at “D” for a daytime takeoff on runway 9?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Fig. 130의 D는 threshold에서 약 1,000 ft 떨어진 runway aiming point marking이다. Runway 9 이륙 방향에서 D는 남은 활주로 1,000 ft를 의미한다.
questions.explanation_en: “D” on Fig. 130 refers to the runway aiming point marking, which is located approximately 1,000 ft. from the threshold. During a takeoff on runway 9, the marker at “D” on Fig. 130 indicates 1,000 ft. of remaining runway because it is the fifth distance marker encountered. Answer (A) is incorrect. The marker at 500 ft. is the sixth, not fifth, distance marker encountered. Answer (C) is incorrect. The marker at 1,500 ft. is the fourth, not fifth, distance marker encountered.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Identify taxi leadoff lights associated with the centerline lighting system.

choices.text: Alternate green and yellow lights curving from the centerline of the runway to the centerline of the taxiway.
Alternate green and yellow lights curving from the centerline of the runway to the edge of the taxiway.
Alternate green and yellow lights curving from the centerline of the runway to a point on the exit. Figure 131. FAA ICAO Precision Approach

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Taxiway lead-off light는 활주로 중심선에서 출구 유도로까지 이어지며 활주로 이탈을 유도한다. 활주로 중심선부터 runway holding position 또는 ILS critical area까지 녹색과 황색이 번갈아 표시된다.
questions.explanation_en: Taxiway leadoff lights extend from the runway centerline to a point on an exit taxiway to provide visual guidance to persons exiting the runway. These lights alternate green and yellow from the runway centerline to the runway holding position or the ILS critical area, as appropriate. Answer (A) is incorrect. Taxiway turnoff lights extend from the runway centerline to a point on the exit taxiway, which may be beyond the point where the leadoff lights meet the taxiway centerline. Answer (B) is incorrect. Taxiway leadoff lights curve from the centerline of the runway to a point on the centerline, not the edge, of the exit taxiway. Runway Markings and Lighting.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 131 above and in color on page 445.) What is the runway distance remaining at “D” for a daytime takeoff on runway 9?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fig. 131의 D는 활주로 끝 500 ft 지점부터 500 ft 간격으로 표시되는 고정거리표시이다. Runway 9 주간 이륙 시 첫 번째 한 쌍의 단일 표시인 D는 남은 활주로 3,000 ft를 의미한다.
questions.explanation_en: “D” on Fig. 131 refers to fixed distance markings, which begin at the 500-ft. mark from the end of the runway and continue at 500-ft. intervals to the 3,000-ft. mark, depending on the runway length. During a daytime takeoff on runway 9, the marking at “D” on Fig. 131 indicates 3,000 ft. of remaining runway because it is the first pair of single markers on either side of the centerline. Answer (B) is incorrect. The markers at 2,500 ft. are the second, not first, pair of single markers encountered on either side of the centerline. Answer (C) is incorrect. The markers at 1,500 ft. are the second pair of double, not single, markers encountered on either side of the centerline.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 131 above and in color on page 445.) What is the runway distance remaining at “E” for a daytime takeoff on runway 9?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Fig. 131의 E는 500 ft 간격의 고정거리표시로, Runway 9 주간 이륙 시 첫 번째 한 쌍의 이중 표시이므로 남은 활주로 2,000 ft를 의미한다.
questions.explanation_en: “E” on Fig. 131 refers to fixed distance markings, which begin at the 500-ft. mark from the end of the runway, and continue at 500-ft. intervals to the 3,000-ft. mark, depending on the runway length. During a daytime takeoff on runway 9, the marking at “E” on Fig. 131 indicates 2,000 ft. of remaining runway because it is the first pair of double markers on either side of the centerline. Answer (A) is incorrect. The markers at 1,500 ft. are the second, not first, pair of double markers encountered on either side of the centerline. Answer (C) is incorrect. The markers at 2,500 ft. are the second pair of single, not the first pair of double, markers encountered on either side of the centerline.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 131 on page 302 and in color on page 445.) What is the runway distance remaining at “F” for a daytime takeoff on runway 9?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 131의 F는 착륙 threshold에서 1,000 ft 떨어진 runway aiming point marking으로, Runway 9 주간 이륙 시 남은 활주로 1,000 ft를 의미한다.
questions.explanation_en: “F” on Fig. 131 refers to the runway aiming point marking, which is located 1,000 ft. from the landing threshold end of the runway. During a daytime takeoff on runway 9, the marking at “F” on Fig. 131 indicates 1,000 ft. of remaining runway. Answer (A) is incorrect. The markers at 2,000 ft. are the first pair of double markers, not a single bold marker, encountered on either side of the centerline. At night it is marked by the beginning of amber runway edge lights. Answer (B) is incorrect. The markers at 1,500 ft. are the second pair of double markers, not a single bold marker, encountered on either side of the centerline.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 131 on page 302 and in color on page 445.) What is the runway distance remaining at “A” for a nighttime takeoff on runway 9?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Fig. 131의 A는 정밀접근활주로 중심선등이다. 이륙 방향에서 남은 3,000 ft부터 1,000 ft까지 적색과 백색이 교대로 나타나고, 마지막 1,000 ft는 모두 적색이다. A 지점은 남은 3,000 ft로 적·백 교대등이 시작되는 지점이다.
questions.explanation_en: “A” on Fig. 131 refers to runway centerline lights, which are installed on FAA ICAO precision approach runways. They are white up to 3,000 ft. of remaining runway. Runway remaining lighting is centerline lighting in the final 3,000 ft. viewed from the takeoff position. Alternate red and white lights are seen from the 3,000-ft. point to the 1,000-ft. point, and red lights are seen for the final 1,000 ft. At point “A” on Fig. 131, 3,000 ft. remain, and the alternating red and white lights begin. Answer (A) is incorrect. The distance of 2,000 ft. is marked by the beginning of amber runway edge lights. Answer (C) is incorrect. The runway remaining lights begin alternating between red and white at 3,000 ft., not 3,500 ft., of remaining runway.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 131 on page 302 and in color on page 445.) What is the runway distance remaining at “C” for a takeoff on runway 9?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fig. 131의 C는 runway centerline light와 관련된 지점으로, 활주로 끝 1,000 ft 전부터 중심선등이 모두 적색으로 바뀐다. 따라서 C는 남은 활주로 1,000 ft 지점이다.
questions.explanation_en: “C” on Fig. 131 refers to runway centerline lights, which are installed on FAA ICAO precision approach runways. Runway remaining lighting is centerline lighting in the final 3,000 ft. viewed from the takeoff position. Alternate red and white lights are seen from 3,000 ft. to 1,000 ft., and red lights are seen for the last 1,000 ft. of the runway. Point “C” on Fig. 131 is 1,000 ft. from the end of the runway and is the beginning of red runway centerline lights. Answer (B) is incorrect. The start of red runway centerline lights indicates 1,000 ft., not 1,800 ft., of remaining runway. Answer (C) is incorrect. The start of red runway centerline lights indicates 1,000 ft., not 1,500 ft., of remaining runway.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 131 on page 302 and in color on page 445.) What is the runway distance remaining at “B” for a nighttime takeoff on runway 9?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Fig. 131의 B는 runway edge light와 관련된다. 정밀 계기활주로에서는 마지막 2,000 ft 또는 활주로 길이 절반 중 짧은 구간에서 가장자리 등이 흰색에서 황색으로 바뀌므로, B는 남은 활주로 2,000 ft를 의미한다.
questions.explanation_en: “B” on Fig. 131 refers to the runway edge lights, which are white. However, on FAA ICAO precision instrument runways, amber (yellow) replaces white on the last 2,000 ft. or half of the runway length, whichever is less. During a takeoff on runway 9 at night, “B” on Fig. 131 marking the beginning of amber runway edge lights indicates 2,000 ft. of remaining runway. Answer (A) is incorrect. The distance of 1,000 ft. is indicated by the start of red centerline lighting. Answer (C) is incorrect. The beginning of yellow runway edge lights on an instrument runway indicates 2,000 ft., not 2,500 ft., of remaining runway.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 131 on page 302 and in color on page 445.) Identify runway remaining lighting on centerline lighting systems.

choices.text: Amber lights from 3,000 feet to 1,000 feet, then alternate red and white lights to the end.
Alternate red and white lights from 3,000 feet to 1,000 feet, then red lights to the end.
Alternate red and white lights from 3,000 feet to the end of the runway.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Runway remaining centerline lighting은 남은 3,000~1,000 ft 구간에서 적색과 백색이 교대로 보이고, 마지막 1,000 ft는 모두 적색이다. 반대 방향에서는 이 등들이 백색으로 보인다.
questions.explanation_en: Runway remaining lighting on centerline lighting systems alternates red and white lights as seen from 3,000 ft. to 1,000 ft. and has all red lights from 1,000 ft. to the runway end. From the opposite direction, these lights are seen as white lights. Answer (A) is incorrect. Alternate red and white, not amber, lights are from 3,000 ft. to 1,000 ft.; then red lights, not alternate red and white, are to the end. Answer (C) is incorrect. Runway remaining lighting alternates red and white lights from 3,000 ft. to 1,000 ft. and has red lights, not alternate red and white, from 1,000 ft. to the end of the runway.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Runway centerline lights on an instrument runway are all white until the

choices.text: last 2,000 feet to 1,000 feet of the runway length.
lesser of the last 3,000 feet or half of the runway length.
last 3,000 feet of the runway length.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. RCLS는 일부 정밀접근활주로에 설치되어 저시정 착륙을 돕는다. 활주로 중심선을 따라 50 ft 간격으로 설치되며 착륙 threshold에서 볼 때 마지막 3,000 ft 전까지는 백색이다.
questions.explanation_en: Runway Centerline Lighting System (RCLS) consist of runway centerline lights installed on some precision approach runways to facilitate landing under adverse visibility conditions. They are located along the runway centerline and are spaced at 50-foot intervals. When viewed from the landing threshold, the runway centerline lights are white until the last 3,000 feet of the runway. Answer (A) is incorrect. The white lights begin to alternate with red for the next 2,000 feet. Answer (B) is incorrect. The last 1,000 feet of the runway, all centerline lights are red.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is meant by the term FAROS?

choices.text: Activation of the fire and operation system.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 독립형 FAROS는 최종접근 중인 조종사에게 활주로 점유 상태를 자동으로 알려주는 시스템이다. 활주로에 항공기나 차량이 감지되면 PAPI가 점멸해 착륙이 안전하지 않을 수 있음을 경고한다.
questions.explanation_en: Stand-alone Final Approach Runway Occupancy Signal (FAROS) is a fully automated system that provides runway occupancy status to a pilot on final approach to indicate whether it may be unsafe to land. When an aircraft or vehicle is detected on the runway, the Precision Approach Path Indicator (PAPI) will flash or pulse to indicate to the pilot on an approach that the runway is occupied and that it may be unsafe to land. Answer (A) is incorrect. REILs are Runway End Identifier Lights. They consist of a pair of synchronized flashing lights located laterally on each side of the runway threshold. They are not associated with the FAROS. Answer (C) is incorrect. Activation of the fire and operation system is not associated with the FAROS.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: How can a pilot identify a military airport at night?

choices.text: Green, yellow, and white beacon light.
White and red beacon light with dual flash of the white.
Green and white beacon light with dual flash of the white.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 군 비행장은 야간에 녹색과 백색이 번갈아 섬광하며, 녹색 사이에 백색이 두 번 섬광하는 공항 비콘으로 식별한다.
questions.explanation_en: Military airports can be identified at night by an airport beacon. The beacon flashes green and white light with a dual flash of the white between the green flashes. Answer (A) is incorrect. A sequential green, yellow, and white beacon light identifies a lighted civilian, not military, heliport. Answer (B) is incorrect. No type of airfield is marked by a beacon with a red and white light with a dual flash of the white.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: How can a pilot identify a lighted heliport at night?

choices.text: Green, yellow, and white beacon light.
White and red beacon light with dual flash of the white.
Green and white beacon light with dual flash of the white.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 조명된 헬리포트는 야간에 녹색·황색·백색 순으로 섬광하는 공항 비콘으로 식별한다.
questions.explanation_en: Lighted heliports can be identified at night by an airport beacon. The beacon flashes green, yellow, and white light. Answer (B) is incorrect. No type of airfield is marked by a beacon with a white and red light with a dual flash of the white. Answer (C) is incorrect. A green and white beacon light with a dual flash of the white identifies a military airport, not a lighted heliport.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: THL is the acronym for
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. RWSL은 활주로 진입·횡단·이륙·착륙이 안전하지 않은 상황을 조종사와 지상차량 운전자에게 자동으로 알려주는 시스템이다. 감시정보를 처리해 REL, THL, RIL, FAROS를 교통의 위치와 속도에 따라 작동시킨다.
questions.explanation_en: The Runway Status Light System (RWSL) is a fully automated system that provides runway status information to pilots and surface vehicle operators to clearly indicate when it is unsafe to enter, cross, take off from, or land on a runway. The RWSL system processes information from surveillance systems and activates runway entrance lights (REL), takeoff hold lights (THL), runway intersection lights (RIL), and the final approach runway occupancy signal (FAROS) in accordance with the position and velocity of the detected traffic. Answer (B) is incorrect. THL is the acronym for takeoff hold lights, not taxi holding lights. Answer (C) is incorrect. THL is the acronym for takeoff hold lights, not terminal holding lights.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A Runway Status Light (RWSL) System at an airport

choices.text: relies on ASDE-X/Airport Surface Surveillance Capability (ASSC).
allows ATC to override any RWSL false indications.
does not require pilots to tell ATC when executing a go-around.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. RWSL이 설치된 공항에서는 ASDE-X/ASSC 등 FAA 감시시스템과 연동되도록 트랜스폰더를 켜 두어야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Aircraft operating at airports with RWSL systems must keep their transponders on to ensure interaction with FAA surveillance systems such as ASDE-X/Airport Surface Surveillance Capability (ASSC), which provides information to the RWSL system. Answer (B) is incorrect. RWSL is fully automatic and functions independently of the traffic control system operated by ATC. Answer (C) is incorrect. RWSL acts as an independent safety enhancement and does not replace ATC-issued interactions.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The illumination of the “THL” indicates

choices.text: terminal holding procedures are in effect.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. THL(Takeoff Hold Lights)은 활주로가 이륙에 안전하지 않음을 경고한다. 예를 들어 다른 차량이 활주로에 있으면 THL이 점등될 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The THL (Takeoff Hold Lights) system is designed to warn aircrews and vehicle operators that the runway is unsafe for takeoff. Another vehicle on the runway could trigger the illumination of the THL. Answer (A) is incorrect. The THL is illuminated because the runway is unsafe for takeoff, not because a takeoff clearance has not yet been issued. Answer (C) is incorrect. An illuminated THL indicates the runway is unsafe for takeoff, not that terminal holding procedures are in effect.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Takeoff hold lights (THL) are a part of the

choices.text: tower operated runway stop light system.
ground controller operated ramp status holding light system.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. RWSL은 활주로가 진입·횡단·이륙·착륙에 안전하지 않은 상황을 자동 표시하며, 감시정보를 바탕으로 THL을 포함한 여러 등화를 작동시킨다.
questions.explanation_en: The Runway Status Light (RWSL) System is fully automated, providing runway status information to pilots and surface vehicle operators to clearly indicate when it is unsafe to enter, cross takeoff from, or land on a runway. The RWSL system processes information that activates many different lights, including THL. Answer (B) is incorrect. The Runway Status Light System, which includes the THL, is an independent safety enhancement, and ATC has limited control over the system. System lights can be disabled should the RWSL operations impact the efficient movement of air traffic and system light intensity levels can be adjusted. Answer (C) is incorrect. The Runway Status Light System, which includes the THL, is an independent safety enhancement, and ATC has limited control over the system. System lights can be disabled should the RWSL operations impact the efficient movement of air traffic and system light intensity levels can be adjusted.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: REL is the acronym for
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. RWSL은 감시시스템 정보를 이용해 REL, THL, RIL, FAROS를 교통의 위치와 속도에 따라 자동 작동시켜 활주로 사용이 안전하지 않은 상황을 알린다.
questions.explanation_en: The Runway Status Light System (RWSL) is a fully automated system that provides runway status information to pilots and surface vehicle operators to clearly indicate when it is unsafe to enter, cross, take off from, or land on a runway. The RWSL system processes information from surveillance systems and activates runway entrance lights (REL), takeoff hold lights (THL), runway intersection lights (RIL), and the final approach runway occupancy signal (FAROS) in accordance with the position and velocity of the detected traffic. Answer (A) is incorrect. REL is the acronym for runway entrance lights, not runway exit lights. Answer (C) is incorrect. REL is the acronym for runway entrance lights, not ramp entry lights.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Illumination of the “RIL” indicates

choices.text: there is traffic on the intersecting runway.
there is crossing traffic ahead of you, but crossing ahead of you.
that you should expect to see traffic holding short of your runway ahead.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. RIL은 RWSL의 일부로 활주로 중심선 양쪽에 두 줄로 매입 설치된다. 착륙 후 활주 중인 항공기와 교차 활주로의 고속 교통이 교차점에서 ±5초 이내에 만날 가능성이 있으면 점등되고, 그 교통이 교차점을 통과하면 소등된다.
questions.explanation_en: The Runway Intersection Lights (RIL) are part of the Runway Status Light (RWSL) System. The RIL are flush mounted, in-pavement light fixtures, in a double row aligned on either side of the runway center-line lighting. The RIL will illuminate for an aircraft that has landed and is rolling out when there is high-speed traffic on the intersecting runway that is within ±5 seconds of meeting at the intersection. Once that traffic passes through the intersection, the RIL extinguish. Answer (A) is incorrect. Once the traffic passes the intersection, the RIL will extinguish. Answer (C) is incorrect. You should be holding and see an aircraft crossing the intersection.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: “REL” is a system of
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. REL은 RWSL의 일부인 단방향 매입식 적색등이다. 활주로에 고속 교통이 있거나 활성 구역 안 최종접근 항공기가 있을 때 점등되며, 조종사는 적색 REL을 보면 hold line에서 정지하거나 계속 정지한 채 ATC에 연락해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: The Runway Entrance Lights (REL) are part of the Runway Status Light (RWSL) System. The REL are flush mounted, in-pavement, unidirectional light fixtures that are directly visible to pilots and surface vehicle operators. When activated, the red lights indicate that there is high-speed traffic on the runway or an aircraft on final approach within the activation area. Whenever a pilot observes the red lights of the REL, that pilot will stop at the hold line or remain stopped and contact ATC. Answer (A) is incorrect. The runway edge lights are white except on instrument runways where yellow replaces white on the last 2,000 feet or half the runway length, whichever is less, to form a caution zone for landings. Answer (B) is incorrect. Taxiway edge lights are blue.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Runway Status Lights (REL) are
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. REL은 Runway Entrance Lights의 약어이며 RWSL 자체의 약어가 아니다. RWSL은 감시정보로 REL 등을 자동 작동시키는 독립적 안전보조 시스템이며 ATC 허가를 대신하거나 전달하지 않는다.
questions.explanation_en: NOTE: This is an FAA sample question. REL is not the acronym for Runway Status Lights (RWSL). The Runway Status Light (RWSL) system is fully automated and provides runway status information to pilots and surface vehicle operators to indicate when it is unsafe to occupy a runway. The RWSL system processes information from surveillance systems and activates the runway entrance lights (REL). When activated, the REL indicate there is high speed traffic on or approaching the runway. The RWSL is an independent safety enhancement that does not substitute for or convey an ATC clearance. Answer (B) is incorrect. The Runway Status Light system, which activates the runway entrance lights (REL), is an automated system, yet the system can be disabled and enabled by the ATC Manager if the system is impacting movement negatively or is unsafely operating. Answer (C) is incorrect. The Runway Status Light system itself can be activated or deactivated by ATC. However, when activated, it functions independently and without ATC control.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is “RIL” the acronym for?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. RIL은 RWSL의 일부로, 착륙 후 활주 중인 항공기와 교차 활주로의 고속 교통이 교차점에서 약 ±5초 이내에 만날 수 있을 때 점등되고 해당 교통이 지나가면 소등된다.
questions.explanation_en: The Runway Intersection Lights (RIL) are part of the Runway Status Light (RWSL) System. The RIL are flush mounted, in-pavement light fixtures, in a double row aligned on either side of the runway center-line lighting. The RIL will illuminate for an aircraft that has landed and is rolling out when there is high speed traffic on the intersecting runway that is ±5 seconds of meeting at the intersection. Once that traffic passes through the intersection, the RIL extinguish. Answer (A) is incorrect. There is no reference for a Repeating Identification Light. Answer (C) is incorrect. There are no runway identification lights. Runway identification would be either a sign for taxiing aircraft or the number of the runway painted on the end of the runway for approaching and departing runways.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Airport touchdown zone lighting (TDZL) has

choices.text: two rows of transverse light bars disposed symmetrically about the runway centerline.
alternate white and green centerline lights extending from 75 feet from the threshold through the touchdown zone.
flush centerline lights spaced at 50-foot intervals extending through the touchdown zone.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. TDZL은 일부 정밀접근활주로에 설치되어 저시정 착륙 시 touchdown zone을 표시한다. 활주로 중심선 양쪽에 대칭으로 두 줄의 횡방향 light bar를 두며, threshold 100 ft 지점부터 3,000 ft 또는 활주로 중간점 중 짧은 곳까지 연장된다.
questions.explanation_en: Touchdown zone lighting (TDZL) is installed on some precision approach runways to indicate the touchdown zone when landing under adverse visibility conditions. It consists of two rows of transverse light bars disposed symmetrically about the runway centerline in the runway touchdown zone. The system starts 100 ft. from the landing threshold and extends to 3,000 ft. from the threshold or the midpoint of the runway, whichever is less. Answer (B) is incorrect. Runway centerline lights, not TDZL, extend from 75 ft. from the threshold through the touchdown zone and are white, not alternating white and green. Answer (C) is incorrect. Flush centerline lights spaced at 50-ft. intervals extending the length of the runway, including the touchdown zone, are runway centerline lighting, not TDZL.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the advantage of a three-bar VASI?

choices.text: Pilots have a choice of glide angles.
A normal glide angle is afforded both high and low flight deck aircraft.
The three-bar VASI is much more visible and can be used at a greater height.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Three-bar VASI는 두 개의 시각 글라이드패스를 제공한다. 가까운 bar와 중간 bar가 보통 3°의 낮은 경로를 만들고, 중간 bar와 먼 bar가 약 0.25° 더 높은 경로를 만든다. 높은 경로는 flight deck이 높은 항공기의 충분한 threshold crossing height 확보용이다.
questions.explanation_en: The three-bar VASI provides two visual glide paths. The lower glide path is provided by the near and middle bars and is normally set at 3°, while the upper glide path, provided by the middle and far bars, is normally 1/4° higher. This higher glide path is intended for use only by high flight deck aircraft to provide a sufficient threshold crossing height. Answer (A) is incorrect. The three-bar VASI provides a glide slope for high flight deck aircraft, not a choice of glide angles for pilots. Answer (C) is incorrect. Both the two-and three-bar VASI are visible from 3 to 5 mi. during the day and up to 20 mi. or more at night, and the three-bar VASI does not provide use at a greater height.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The higher glide slope of the three-bar VASI is intended for use by
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Three-bar VASI의 높은 글라이드패스는 flight deck이 높은 항공기가 충분한 threshold crossing height를 확보하도록 사용한다.
questions.explanation_en: The three-bar VASI provides two visual glide paths. The higher glide path is intended for use only by high-flight deck aircraft to provide a sufficient threshold crossing height. Answer (A) is incorrect. The higher glide slope of a three-bar VASI is for use only by high-flight deck aircraft, which may or may not be high-performance aircraft. Answer (B) is incorrect. The higher glide slope of a three-bar VASI is for use only by high-flight deck aircraft, not specifically for use by helicopters.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A pilot of a high-performance airplane should be aware that flying a steeper-than-normal VASI glide slope angle may result in

choices.text: landing short of the runway threshold.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. VASI는 보통 3°이지만 지형·장애물 여유를 위해 최대 약 4.5°로 설정될 수 있다. 고성능 항공기가 3.5°를 초과하는 VASI 각을 사용하면 착륙 및 rollout에 필요한 활주로 길이가 증가할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Although VASI normally provides glide path angles of 3°, some locations may be as high as 4.5° to give proper clearance. Pilots of high-performance aircraft are cautioned that use of VASI angles in excess of 3.5° may cause an increase in runway length required for landing and rollout. Answer (A) is incorrect. Flying a steeper-than-normal VASI may result in an increased landing rollout, not a hard landing, in a high-performance airplane. Answer (C) is incorrect. A landing short of the runway threshold results from flying a lower-than-normal, not higher, VASI glide slope angle.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What are the indications of the pulsating VASI?

choices.text: High - pulsing white, on glide path - green, low - pulsing red.
High - pulsing white, on glide path - steady white, slightly below glide slope - steady red, low - pulsing red.
High - pulsing white, on course and on glide path - steady white, off course but on glide path - pulsing white and red, low - pulsing red.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Pulsating VASI는 최종접근구역에서 2색으로 수직 경로만 알려준다. 글라이드패스 위는 점멸 백색, 정상 경로는 고정 백색, 약간 아래는 고정 적색, 아래는 점멸 적색이다. 횡방향 유도는 활주로 또는 활주로 등화로 판단한다.
questions.explanation_en: The pulsating VASI provides a two-color visual glide path indication in the final approach area. It provides only a glide path indication while lateral course guidance is provided by the runway or runway lights. Above glide path is pulsating white. On glide path is steady white. Slightly below glide path is steady red. Below glide path is pulsating red. Also, the answer should refer to “pulsating,” not “pulsing.” Answer (A) is incorrect. The on glide path indication of a pulsating VASI is either a pulsating red and white or steady white, not green, light. Answer (C) is incorrect. The pulsating VASI provides only glide path indications, not lateral, or course, indications.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What does the pulsating VASI consist of?

choices.text: Three-light system, two pulsing and one steady.
Two-light projectors, one pulsing and one steady.
One-light projector, pulsing white when above glide slope or red when more than slightly below glide slope, steady white when on glide slope, steady red for slightly below glide path.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Pulsating VASI는 보통 하나의 투사장치로 2색 글라이드패스 정보를 제공한다. 경로 아래는 점멸 적색, 위는 점멸 백색, 정상은 고정 백색, 약간 아래는 고정 적색이다.
questions.explanation_en: Pulsating VASIs normally consist of a single light unit projecting a two-color visual glide path indication in the final approach area of the runway. The below glide path indication is normally pulsating red, and the above glide path is pulsating white. The on glide path indication is a steady white light. The slightly below glide path is a steady red. The answer should refer to “pulsating,” not “pulsing.” Answer (A) is incorrect. The pulsating VASI is a two-, not three-, light system, with two pulsating and two, not one, steady. Answer (B) is incorrect. The pulsating VASI is a single, not double, light projecting unit.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What does the Precision Approach Path Indicator (PAPI) consist of?

choices.text: Row of four lights parallel to the runway; red, white, and green.
Row of four lights perpendicular to the runway; red and white.
One light projector with two colors; red and white.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. PAPI는 활주로에 직각인 한 줄에 2개 또는 4개의 등화장치를 설치하며 보통 활주로 왼쪽에 있다. 각 등은 적색 또는 백색으로 보이고, 4등식에서 적색 2개·백색 2개이면 정상 글라이드패스이다.
questions.explanation_en: The PAPI uses lights similar to the two-and three-bar VASI but installed in a single row of either two or four light units perpendicular to the runway. The row of lights is normally installed on the left side of the runway. Each light unit appears as either red or white. When two are red and two are white, you are on the glide path. Answer (A) is incorrect. PAPI has a row of four lights perpendicular, not parallel, to the runway and projects red and white, not green, light. Answer (C) is incorrect. PAPI consists of a row of four, not one, light projectors emitting red or white light.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What are the indications of Precision Approach Path Indicator (PAPI)?

choices.text: High - white, on glide path - red and white; low - red.
High - white, on glide path - green; low - red.
High - white and green, on glide path - green; low - red.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. PAPI 4등식은 전부 백색이면 높음(약 3.5° 초과), 적1/백3은 약간 높음(약 3.2°), 적2/백2는 정상(3°), 적3/백1은 약간 낮음(약 2.8°), 전부 적색이면 낮음(약 2.5° 미만)을 뜻한다.
questions.explanation_en: PAPI can indicate five possible glide path indications. All white light indicates “high” or more than 3.5° glide path. One red and three white indicate a slightly high (3.2°) glide path. Two red and two white indicate on the glide path (3°). Three red and one white indicate a slightly low (2.8°) glide path. Four red lights indicate below (less than 2.5°) the glide path. Answer (B) is incorrect. The on glide path indication of PAPI is both red and white, not green, lights. Answer (C) is incorrect. Above the glide path indication of PAPI is all white (green is not a color indication of PAPI), on glide path is two red and two white, not green, and below glide path is all red.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What best describes the Precision Approach Path Indicator (PAPI) system?

choices.text: One light projection unit with two colors: red and white.
Row of four lights perpendicular to the runway: red and white.
Row of four lights parallel to the runway: red and white.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. PAPI는 보통 활주로 왼쪽에 2개 또는 4개의 등화장치를 한 줄로 설치한다. 4등식에서 백2·적2는 정상 경로, 백색이 3개 이상이면 높음, 적색이 3개 이상이면 낮음을 뜻한다.
questions.explanation_en: The PAPI uses light units similar to the VASI but are installed in a single row of either two or four light units. The row of light units is normally installed on the left side of the runway. The glide path indications are red and white lights where two whites and two reds indicate that the aircraft is on the glide path. Three or more white lights indicates too high and three or more red lights indicate too low. Answer (A) is incorrect. One light projection unit with two colors, red and white, is a pulsating system (PVASI). Answer (C) is incorrect. The row of four lights are perpendicular to the runway, not parallel to the runway.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: How often are NOTAMs broadcast to pilots on a scheduled basis?

choices.text: 15 minutes before and 15 minutes after the hour.
Between weather broadcasts on the hour.
Hourly, appended to the weather broadcast.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. NOTAM(D)은 시간별 기상방송에 첨부되어 자동 전파된다. NOTAM(L)은 지역적으로 배포·관리되며 시간별 기상보고에 붙지 않고, FDC NOTAM은 한 번 전송된 뒤 발간되거나 취소될 때까지 FSS에 보관된다.
questions.explanation_en: NOTAMs (D) are broadcast to pilots automatically, appended to the hourly weather broadcast. NOTAM (L) information is not attached to the hourly weather reports but is distributed locally and maintained at each FSS for facilities in its area only. FDC NOTAMs are transmitted only once and are kept on file at the FSS until published or canceled. Answer (A) is incorrect. NOTAMs (D) are appended to the hourly weather report, not broadcasted 15 min. before and after the hour. Answer (B) is incorrect. NOTAMs (D) are appended to the hourly weather broadcast, not a separate broadcast between weather reports.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What are FDC NOTAMs?

choices.text: Conditions of facilities en route that may cause delays.
Time critical aeronautical information of a temporary nature from distant centers.
Regulatory amendments to published IAPs and charts not yet available in normally published charts.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. FDC NOTAM은 규제 성격의 NOTAM으로 비행 제한을 설정하거나 차트·공표 계기접근절차를 수정할 때 발행한다.
questions.explanation_en: FDC (Flight Data Center) NOTAMs are regulatory in nature and issued to establish restrictions to flight or amend charts or published instrument approach procedures. FDC NOTAMs are published as needed and indexed in the Notice to Airmen Publication. Answer (A) is incorrect. NOTAM (D) contains information on navigational facilities en route that may cause delays. NOTAMs (D) are appended to the hourly weather reports and are available from any FSS for the duration of their validity or until published. Answer (B) is incorrect. Time critical aeronautical information of a temporary nature from distant centers will be included in a NOTAM (D), or distant. NOTAMs (D) are appended to the hourly weather reports and are available from any FSS for the duration of their validity or until published.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: NOTAMs (D) are used to disseminate what type of information?

choices.text: Temporary flight restrictions, changes to sectional aeronautical charts, and changes to instrument approach procedures.
Taxi closures, personnel and equipment near or crossing runways, airport lighting aids that do not affect instrument approach criteria, and airport rotating beacon outages.
Time critical information of a permanent nature that is not yet available in normally published charts.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. NOTAM(D)은 지역 및 원거리 정보를 전파하며, 지역 정보에는 유도로 폐쇄, 활주로 인근 인원·장비, 계기접근 기준에 영향을 주지 않는 공항등화 고장, 회전비콘 고장 등이 포함된다.
questions.explanation_en: NOTAMs (D) disseminate various local and distant information. At the local level, NOTAMs (D) disseminate information such as taxiway closures, personnel and equipment near or crossing runways, airport lighting aids that do not affect instrument approach criteria, and airport rotating beacon outages. Answer (A) is incorrect. Temporary flight restrictions and charting changes between regular printing cycles are disseminated in FDC NOTAMs. Answer (C) is incorrect. Time critical information of a permanent nature that is not yet available in normally published charts is disseminated by an FDC NOTAM.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What type of information is disseminated by NOTAMs (D)?

choices.text: Status of navigation aids, ILSs, radar service available, and other information essential to planning.
Information specific to military airports that are part of the NAS.
Temporary flight restrictions, changes in status in navigational aids, and updates on equipment such as VASI.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 원거리 NOTAM(D)은 NAS의 항행시설과 Chart Supplement에 등재된 공용 공항·수상비행장·헬리포트에 대해 발행되며, 항행시설/ILS 상태, 이용 가능한 레이더 서비스 등 비행계획에 중요한 정보를 포함한다.
questions.explanation_en: NOTAMs (D) disseminate various local and distant information. Distant NOTAMs are disseminated for all navigational facilities that are part of the National Airspace System (NAS) and for all public-use airports, seaplane bases, and heliports listed in the Chart Supplement. They include the status of navigation aids, ILSs, radar service available, and other information essential to planning. Answer (B) is incorrect. Military NOTAMs, not NOTAMs (D), are issued for military airports in the National Airspace System (NAS). Answer (C) is incorrect. Temporary flight restrictions are normally disseminated in FDC NOTAMs.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What information is contained in the Notices to Airmen Publication (NTAP)?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. NTAP에는 장기간 유효할 것으로 예상되는 NOTAM(D)이 수록된다.
questions.explanation_en: The NTAP contains NOTAMs (D) that are expected to remain in effect for an extended period. Answer (B) is incorrect. Military NOTAMs are not published in the NTAP. Answer (C) is incorrect. FDC NOTAMs are no longer published in the NTAP, and pointer NOTAMs are issued by a Flight Service Station to highlight or point out another NOTAM and are not published in the NTAP.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Land and Hold Short Operations (LAHSO) include landing and holding short

choices.text: of some designated point on the runway.
only of an intersecting runway or taxiway.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. LAHSO에는 교차 활주로, 교차 유도로 또는 그 밖의 지정된 활주로 지점 앞에서 착륙 후 정지하는 절차가 포함된다.
questions.explanation_en: LAHSO include landing and holding short of an intersecting runway, an intersecting taxiway, or some other designated point on a runway other than an intersecting runway or taxiway. Answer (A) is incorrect. LAHSO include landing and holding short of an intersecting runway or some other designated point on a runway, not only an intersecting taxiway. Answer (C) is incorrect. LAHSO include landing and holding short of some designated point on a runway, not only an intersecting runway or taxiway.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A Land and Hold Short Operations (LAHSO) clearance that the pilot accepts

choices.text: does not preclude a rejected landing.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. LAHSO 허가를 수락하면 다른 ATC 허가와 마찬가지로 수정 허가를 받거나 비상상황이 발생하지 않는 한 따라야 한다. 단, LAHSO 허가는 rejected landing을 금지하지 않는다.
questions.explanation_en: A LAHSO clearance, once accepted, must be adhered to, just as any other ATC clearance, unless an amended clearance is obtained or an emergency occurs. A LAHSO clearance does not preclude a rejected landing. Answer (A) is incorrect. A LAHSO clearance must be adhered to unless an amended clearance is obtained or an emergency occurs. Additionally, a LAHSO clearance does not preclude a rejected landing. Answer (C) is incorrect. A LAHSO clearance does not preclude a rejected landing.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: In conducting Land and Hold Short Operations (LAHSO), the pilot should have readily available

choices.text: the published Available Landing Distance (ALD), landing performance of the aircraft, and slope of all LAHSO combinations at the destination airport.
the published runway length and slope for all LAHSO combinations at the airport of intended landing.
the landing performance of the aircraft, published Available Landing Distance (ALD) for all LAHSO combinations at the airport of intended landing, plus the forecast winds.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. LAHSO를 수행하려면 목적공항의 관련 정보를 숙지하고 각 LAHSO 활주로 조합의 공표 ALD(Available Landing Distance)와 활주로 경사 정보를 즉시 확인할 수 있어야 한다. 또한 항공기 착륙성능을 알아야 배정된 ALD가 안전한 LAHSO에 충분한지 판단할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: To conduct LAHSO, you should become familiar with all available information concerning LAHSO at the destination airport. You should have readily available the published ALD and runway slope information for all LAHSO runway combinations at each airport of intended landing. Additionally, knowledge about landing performance of your airplane permits you to readily determine that the ALD for the assigned runway is sufficient for safe LAHSO. Answer (B) is incorrect. To conduct LAHSO, you should have the available landing distance (ALD), not the published runway length. Answer (C) is incorrect. To conduct LAHSO, a pilot would want to have the current, not forecast, winds to assist in determining if the landing performance would be sufficient for safe LAHSO.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The airport markings, signage, and lighting associated with Land and Hold Short Operations (LAHSO) consist of

choices.text: yellow hold-short markings, red and white signage, and in-pavement lights.
red and white signage, yellow hold-short markings, and at some airports, in-pavement lights.
red and black signage, in-pavement lights, and yellow hold-short markings.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. LAHSO에서는 상황인식이 매우 중요하다. 관련 공항 표식·표지·등화를 정확히 알아야 하며, 대표적으로 노란 hold-short 표시, 적·백색 표지, 일부 공항의 포장면 매입등이 사용된다.
questions.explanation_en: Situational awareness is vital to the success of LAHSO. Situational awareness includes a thorough understanding of the airport markings, signage, and lighting associated with LAHSO. These visual aids consist of yellow hold-short markings, red and white signage, and, at some airports, in-pavement lighting. Answer (A) is incorrect. Not all airports will have in-pavement lighting. Answer (C) is incorrect. The signage is red and white, not red and black, and not all airports will have in-pavement lighting.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Bird strikes in flight will be reported to the

choices.text: nearest state or federal wildlife office on company letterhead.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. FAA는 조종사, 공항운영·정비·ATC 관계자, 엔진 제작사 등 야생동물 충돌을 알고 있는 누구나 NWSD에 보고하도록 강력히 권고한다. 보고에는 FAA Bird/Other Wildlife Strike Report Form 5200-7을 사용할 수 있으며 ADO, FSDO, FSS 또는 AIM에서 양식을 얻을 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The FAA strongly encourages pilots, airport operations, aircraft maintenance personnel, Air Traffic Control personnel, engine manufacturers, or anyone else who has knowledge of a strike to report it to the National Wildlife Strike Database (NWSD). Anyone reporting a strike can print the FAA’s Bird/Other Wildlife Strike Report Form 5200-7. Paper copies of Form 5200-7 may be obtained from the appropriate Airports District Offices (ADO), Flight Standards District Offices (FSDO), and Flight Service Stations (FSS) or from the Aeronautical Information Manual (AIM). Answer (A) is incorrect. The federal wildlife office does not investigate or record aviation wildlife strikes. Answer (C) is incorrect. The FSS would be able to supply you with the appropriate form to fill out, but they do not investigate or record wildlife strikes.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: How are random RNAV routes below FL 390 defined on the IFR flight plan?

choices.text: Define route waypoints using degree-distance fixes based on appropriate navigational aids for the route and altitude at 250 NM intervals.
List the initial and final fix with at least one waypoint each 200 NM.

Review and enter appropriate arrival and departure transition fixes or navigation aids for the altitude being flown. Define the random route waypoints by using degree-distance fixes based on navigation aids appropriate for the altitude being flown.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. FL 390 미만에서 임의 RNAV 항로를 IFR 비행계획으로 제출할 때 Route of Flight에는 해당 항로와 고도에 적합한 항행시설을 기준으로 degree-distance fix를 사용해 waypoint를 정의해야 한다.
