questions.explanation_en: When filing an IFR flight plan for a proposed random RNAV route below FL 390, in block 8, Route of Flight, you must define the route waypoints by using degree-distance fixes based on navigational aids which are appropriate for the route and altitude. This question requires how a random route is to be defined on an IFR flight plan, not how the flight is to be planned. Answer (A) is incorrect. The distances should be within 200 NM, not 250 NM. Answer (B) is incorrect. The route must contain a minimum of one route waypoint for each ARTCC through whose area the RNAV route will be flown. These waypoints must be located within 200 NM of the preceding center’s boundary, not every 200 NM.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: How should an off-airway direct flight be defined on an IFR flight plan?

choices.text: The initial fix, the true course, and the final fix.
All radio fixes over which the flight will pass.
The initial fix, all radio fixes which the pilot wishes to be compulsory reporting points, and the final fix.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 항로 밖 direct IFR 비행의 전부 또는 일부는 통과할 radio fix를 비행계획에 기재해 정의해야 하며, ATC가 달리 통보하지 않는 한 이 fix들은 강제보고점이 된다.
questions.explanation_en: All or any portion of an off-airway direct flight must be defined on an IFR flight plan by indicating the radio fixes over which the flight will pass. These fixes automatically become compulsory reporting points for the flight, unless advised otherwise by ATC. Answer (A) is incorrect. True course is not an item that is reported on an IFR flight plan. The initial fix and the final fix are listed as radio fixes that define the start and finish points of a flight. Answer (C) is incorrect. Initial and final fixes are required to define random RNAV, not direct flight, routes. All radio fixes that define the route of a direct flight automatically become compulsory reporting points, not only those the pilot desires.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: How should the route of flight be defined on an IFR flight plan?

choices.text: A simplified route via airways or jet routes with transitions.
A route via airways or jet routes with VOR’s and fixes used.
A route via airways or jet routes with only the compulsory reporting points.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. IFR 비행계획의 항로는 정확하고 완전하게 기재해야 한다. 항로 정의를 단순화하고 ATC 처리를 돕기 위해 가능한 경우 transition이 포함된 airway 또는 jet route로 제출하는 것이 권장된다.
questions.explanation_en: It is vitally important that the route of flight be defined accurately and completely on an IFR flight plan. To simplify definition of the route and to facilitate ATC, pilots are requested to file via airways or jet routes with transitions. Answer (B) is incorrect. To simplify the route, all VORs and fixes are not used to define a route on an IFR flight plan. Answer (C) is incorrect. Compulsory reporting points may not define the transitions between airways or jet routes.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: How should an IFR flight plan be closed at the completion of the flight at a controlled airport?

choices.text: The tower will automatically close the flight plan when the aircraft lands.
The pilot must close the flight plan with the nearest FSS or other FAA facility upon landing.
The pilot must request the tower to relay the instructions to the nearest FSS after landing.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 관제탑이 운영되는 공항에 착륙하면 IFR 비행계획은 관제탑이 자동으로 종료하므로 조종사가 별도 조치를 할 필요가 없다.
questions.explanation_en: The tower will automatically close an IFR flight plan after landing, and no action is required from the pilot. Answer (B) is incorrect. A pilot is responsible for ensuring that the IFR flight plan is canceled only when landing at a non-towered airport. Answer (C) is incorrect. There is no need to ask the tower to relay instructions to the nearest FSS. The flight plan will be canceled automatically.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 500A on page 319.) If more than one cruising altitude is intended, what information should be entered in item 15, “Level,” of the flight plan?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 둘 이상의 순항고도를 계획했다면 비행계획에는 첫 번째 구간에서 사용할 초기 순항고도를 기재한다.
questions.explanation_en: If more than one cruising altitude is intended, enter the planned cruising level for the first (initial) portion of the route to be flown. Answer (B) is incorrect. The initial, not highest, altitude should be filed on your IFR flight plan. Answer (C) is incorrect. The initial, not lowest, altitude should be filed on your IFR flight plan.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 500A on page 319.) What information should be entered in item 15, “Level,” for an IFR flight?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. IFR 비행에서 순항고도를 여러 개 사용할 예정이면 첫 구간의 계획 순항고도를 비행계획에 기재한다.
questions.explanation_en: Enter the planned cruising level for the first (initial) portion of the route to be flown if more than one cruising altitude is intended for an IFR flight. Answer (B) is incorrect. The initial, not highest, altitude should be filed on your IFR flight plan. Answer (C) is incorrect. The initial, not lowest, altitude should be filed on your IFR flight plan.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 500A on page 319.) What information should be entered into item 16, “Destination Aerodrome,” for an IFR flight?

choices.text: The destination airport identifier code and name of the FBO where the airplane will be parked.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. ICAO 비행계획서 Item 16 Destination Aerodrome에는 목적공항의 ICAO 4문자 위치식별부호를 기입한다.
questions.explanation_en: In item 16, “Destination Aerodrome,” of the flight plan form (Fig. 500A), enter the ICAO four-letter location identifier. Answer (A) is incorrect. The name of the FBO is not required. Answer (C) is incorrect. The ICAO four-letter indicator should be entered, not the city and state.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 500A on page 319.) What information should be entered in item 19, “Endurance,” for an IFR flight?

choices.text: The estimated time en route plus 30 minutes.
The estimated time en route plus 45 minutes.
The amount of usable fuel on board expressed in time.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. ICAO 비행계획서 Item 19 Endurance에는 출발 시 사용 가능한 연료를 비행 가능 시간의 시·분으로 기재한다.
questions.explanation_en: Item 19, “Endurance,” of the flight plan requires the amount of usable fuel in the airplane at the time of departure. It should be expressed in hours and minutes of flying time. Answer (A) is incorrect. The VFR fuel requirement for day flight is the estimated time en route plus 30 min. Answer (B) is incorrect. The IFR fuel requirement is the estimated time en route plus 45 min.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 500A on page 319.) What information should be entered in item 19, “Endurance,” for an IFR flight?

choices.text: The actual time en route expressed in hours and minutes.
The estimated time en route expressed in hours and minutes.
The total amount of usable fuel onboard expressed in hours and minutes.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 비행계획의 Endurance는 출발 시점의 usable fuel로 가능한 비행시간을 시간과 분으로 표시한다.
questions.explanation_en: Item 19, “Endurance,” of the flight plan requires the amount of usable fuel in the airplane at the time of departure. It should be expressed in hours and minutes of flying time. Answer (A) is incorrect. Item 19 requires the amount of fuel on board at the time of departure expressed in time. Answer (B) is incorrect. Item 19 requires the amount of fuel on board at the time of departure expressed in time.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 500A on page 319.) What information should be entered in item 16, “Destination Aerodrome,” for an IFR flight with an intended stopover of 30 minutes?

choices.text: The ICAO four-letter indicator of the airport of first intended landing.
The ICAO four-letter indicator of the destination airport.
The ICAO four-letter indicator of the airport where the aircraft is based.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 비행계획 Item 16에는 1시간을 초과하는 stopover가 없는 경우 해당 비행의 최종 예정 착륙공항 ICAO 4문자 식별부호를 기재한다.
questions.explanation_en: Item 16 of the flight plan form (Fig. 500A) requires the ICAO four-letter indicator of the airport of last intended landing for that flight, as long as no stopover exceeds 1 hr. Answer (A) is incorrect. The first intended landing, i.e., the end of the first leg of the flight, is included in the route of flight (item 15). Answer (C) is incorrect. The ICAO four-letter indicator of the airport where the airplane is based is not entered on the ICAO flight plan form.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the suggested time interval for filing and requesting an IFR flight plan?

choices.text: File at least 30 minutes prior to departure and request the clearance not more than 10 minutes prior to taxi.
File at least 30 minutes prior to departure and request the clearance at least 10 minutes prior to taxi.
File at least 1 hour prior to departure and request the clearance at least 10 minutes prior to taxi.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 출발허가 지연을 피하려면 IFR 비행계획은 예상 출발시각 최소 30분 전에 제출하는 것이 좋다. Pretaxi clearance 공항에서는 taxi 약 10분 전 이내에 clearance delivery 또는 ground control에 연락할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Pilots should file IFR flight plans at least 30 min. prior to estimated time of departure to prevent possible delays in receiving a departure clearance from ATC. Certain airports have established pretaxi clearance programs through which pilots of IFR airplanes may contact clearance delivery or ground control not more than 10 min. prior to taxi time. Answer (B) is incorrect. A pilot can request the clearance not more than 10 min., not at least 10 min., prior to taxi. Answer (C) is incorrect. Pilots should file at least 30 min., not 1 hr., prior to departure and request the clearance not more than 10 min., not at least 10 min., prior to taxi.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is one limitation when filing a random RNAV route on an IFR flight plan?

choices.text: The waypoints must be located within 200 NM of each other.
The entire route must be within radar environment.
The waypoints may only be defined by degree-distance fixes based on appropriate navigational aids.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Random RNAV route는 전체 항로가 radar environment 안에 있을 때만 승인될 수 있다. ATC가 비행을 감시하지만 항법 책임은 조종사에게 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Random RNAV routes can be approved only when the entire route is in a radar environment. ATC will monitor each random RNAV flight, but navigation on the route is the responsibility of the pilot. Answer (A) is incorrect. VOR/VORTAC (H) facilities, not waypoints, must be within 200 NM of each other when operating above FL 450 to define a direct, not random RNAV, route. Answer (C) is incorrect. Random RNAV waypoints may be defined by degree-distance fixes based on appropriate navigational aids or by latitude-longitude coordinate navigation, independent of VOR/TACAN references, operating at and above FL 390 in the conterminous U.S.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Under what condition may a pilot file an IFR flight plan containing a special or privately owned IAP?

choices.text: Upon signing a waiver of responsibility.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 특별 또는 사설 IAP가 있는 목적지로 비행할 때는 절차 소유자의 사전 승인을 받아야 한다. 이런 절차는 특별 승무원 자격·훈련이 필요할 수 있고 사설 항행시설을 기반으로 할 수도 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Pilots planning flights to locations served by a special or privately owned IAP should obtain advance approval from the owner of the procedure. These IAPs may require special crew training qualifications or other special considerations to execute the approach. Approval by the owner is necessary because special procedures are for the exclusive use of the owner, and these approaches may be based on privately owned navigational aids. Answer (A) is incorrect. ATC is not required to question pilots to determine whether they have the owner’s permission to use the procedure. Answer (C) is incorrect. A pilot is responsible for the safe operation of the airplane. To sign a waiver of responsibility is contrary to the pilot’s responsibilities.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Under what condition may a pilot cancel an IFR flight plan prior to completing the flight?

choices.text: Anytime it appears the clearance will cause a deviation from Federal Aviation Regulations.
Anytime within controlled airspace by contacting ARTCC.
Only if in VFR conditions in other than Class A airspace.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Class A 밖에서 VFR 기상상태로 운항 중이면 언제든 'Cancel my IFR flight plan'이라고 말해 IFR을 취소할 수 있다. ATC가 수락한 뒤에는 적절한 통신주파수, VFR 트랜스폰더 코드, VFR 고도로 전환한다.
questions.explanation_en: An IFR flight plan may be canceled at any time the flight is operating in VFR conditions outside Class A airspace by the pilot’s stating, “Cancel my IFR flight plan.” Once accepted by ATC, a pilot should change to the appropriate communications frequency, VFR transponder code, and VFR altitude. Answer (A) is incorrect. Anytime a clearance appears to deviate from a Federal Aviation Regulation, the pilot should request clarification from ATC and an amended clearance. Answer (B) is incorrect. All aircraft in Class A airspace (above FL 180) or when operating in IMC must be operating under an IFR flight plan.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: In what way are SIDs depicted in plan view?

choices.text: “Vectors” provided for navigational guidance or “Pilot NAV” with courses the pilot is responsible to follow.
“Vectors” and “Pilot NAV” for pilots to use at their discretion.
Combined textual and graphic form which are mandatory routes and instructions.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. SID는 기본적으로 Vector 방식과 Pilot NAV 방식이 있다. Vector 방식은 ATC가 filed/assigned route나 SID fix까지 레이더 유도를 제공하고, Pilot NAV는 조종사가 SID 항로 항법을 주로 책임진다.
questions.explanation_en: SID procedures will be depicted in one of two basic forms. “Vectors” are established where ATC will provide radar navigational guidance to a filed/assigned route or to a fix depicted on the SID. “Pilot NAV” indicates where the pilot is primarily responsible for navigation on the SID route. These may contain vector instructions which pilots are expected to comply with until notified to resume normal navigation on the filed/assigned route or SID procedure. Answer (B) is incorrect. SIDs are departure procedures and must be followed as depicted, not at the pilot’s discretion. If a pilot does not wish to use a SID, then (s)he must notify ATC. Answer (C) is incorrect. While SIDs are published in textual and graphic form, they are mandatory only if the SID was given as part of a clearance.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the difference between an obstacle departure procedure (ODP) and a standard instrument departure (SID)?

choices.text: An ODP provides obstacle clearance protection but does not include ATC-related climb requirements for traffic separation.
An ODP typically provides for traffic separation in busy terminal areas, but a SID provides both obstacle clearance and aircraft separation.
An ODP provides both obstacle and aircraft separation, but a SID is designed for ATC to provide aircraft separation on departure routes.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. ODP는 장애물 회피만을 목적으로 하며 ATC 교통 관련 상승요건은 포함하지 않는다. 가능한 한 부담이 적은 경로로 항로구조에 연결되도록 설계한다.
questions.explanation_en: Obstacle departure procedures are only used for obstruction clearance and do not include ATC-related climb requirements. The primary emphasis of ODP design is to use the least onerous route of flight to the en route structure while attempting to accommodate typical departure routes. Answer (B) is incorrect. ODP does not use ATC for traffic separation. It is only used for obstruction clearance. Answer (C) is incorrect. ODP only provides obstacle clearance and not aircraft separation.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a STAR?

choices.text: Provide separation between IFR and VFR traffic.
Decrease traffic congestion at certain airports.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. STAR는 특정 공항으로 도착하는 IFR 교통을 위해 설정된 ATC coded arrival route이며, clearance 전달 절차를 단순화하는 것이 목적이다.
questions.explanation_en: A STAR is an ATC coded IFR arrival route established for use by arriving IFR traffic at certain airports. Its purpose is to simplify clearance delivery procedures. Answer (A) is incorrect. Separation between IFR and VFR traffic is provided by Class B or TRSA radar service, not a STAR. Answer (C) is incorrect. A STAR is used to simplify clearance delivery procedures, thus decreasing radio frequency, not traffic, congestion at certain airports.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When does ATC issue a STAR?

choices.text: Only when ATC deems it appropriate.
Only upon request of the pilot.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. STAR가 공표된 목적지로 가는 IFR 항공기에는 ATC가 적절하다고 판단하면 STAR가 포함된 허가를 발부할 수 있다. 조종사는 최소한 해당 STAR의 textual description을 소지해야 하며 수락 또는 거부할 책임이 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Pilots of IFR airplanes destined to locations for which STARs have been published may be issued a clearance containing a STAR whenever ATC deems it appropriate. A pilot must have at least a textual description in his or her possession. It is the responsibility of each pilot to accept or refuse an issued STAR. Answer (B) is incorrect. Any type of IFR flight can be issued a STAR. High priority flights will normally be handled in an expeditious manner by ATC. Answer (C) is incorrect. A STAR is a clearance delivery procedure that is issued by ATC. A pilot has the responsibility to accept or refuse that clearance. A pilot can list a STAR in the flight plan, but ATC will issue one only if appropriate.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 269 below.) The flight is filed Senic One Departure, Daggett transition. Before reaching MOXIE intersection, ATC clears you to turn left heading 030 and proceed direct LAHAB intersection. After the turn, you realize you cannot cross LAHAB at 15,000 feet. What should you do if you are in IMC?

choices.text: Enter holding at LAHAB on the 185 degree radial until reaching 15,000 feet.
Advise Departure Control you cannot make the clearance and request radar vectors.
Turn toward the Long Beach airport temporarily and continue the climb until you can cross LAHAB at 15,000 feet. Figure 269. SENIC ONE Departure

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. SID 요건을 충족할 수 없다고 판단되면 Departure Control에 알리고 radar vectors를 요청해야 한다. ATC는 교통분리와 장애물 여유를 확보하는 항로·고도로 재지정한다.
questions.explanation_en: If you realize you are unable to meet the requirements of a SID, you should advise Departure Control and request radar vectors. ATC will redirect you on a route and altitude that will give proper traffic separation and obstacle clearance. Answer (A) is incorrect. Once cleared on a SID, ATC will expect you to continue on the published route without deviation. Answer (C) is incorrect. The described procedure is not authorized by the SID. (RNAV) (SENIC1.SENIC).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the normal procedure for IFR departures at locations with pretaxi clearance programs?

choices.text: Pilots request IFR clearance when ready to taxi. The pilot will receive taxi instruction with clearance.
Pilots request IFR clearance when ready to taxi. Pilots will receive taxi clearance, then receive IFR clearance while taxiing or on runup.
Pilots request IFR clearance 10 minutes or less prior to taxi, then request taxi clearance from ground control.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Pretaxi clearance는 IFR 항공기가 taxi 시작 전에 IFR clearance를 받을 수 있게 한다. 참여는 의무가 아니며, 참여 시 taxi 약 10분 전 이내에 IFR clearance를 요청한 뒤 ground control에 taxi clearance를 요청한다.
questions.explanation_en: Pretaxi clearance programs allow pilots of departing IFR airplanes to receive their IFR clearances before they start taxiing for takeoff. Pilot participation is not mandatory. Participating pilots should request IFR clearance 10 min. or less prior to taxi, then request taxi clearance from ground control. Answer (A) is incorrect. At a location with a pretaxi clearance program, the pilot will first receive the IFR clearance, then taxi instructions. The pilot should request the IFR clearance 10 min. or less prior to taxi time. Answer (B) is incorrect. At a location with a pretaxi clearance program, the pilot will first be given the IFR clearance, then the taxi clearance. The pilot should request the IFR clearance 10 min. or less prior to taxi time.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What minimum information does an abbreviated departure clearance “cleared as filed” include?

choices.text: Clearance limit, transponder code, and DP, if appropriate.
Destination airport, en route altitude, transponder code, and DP, if appropriate.
Clearance limit and en route altitude.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Abbreviated IFR departure clearance에는 최소한 목적공항이 포함되며, en route altitude, transponder code, DP 및 필요한 추가 지시도 포함된다.
questions.explanation_en: The minimum information in an abbreviated IFR departure clearance will include the destination airport. The en route altitude, transponder code and departure procedure (DP), as well as any additional instruction will also be included. Answer (A) is incorrect. This option does not specify the destination airport, which is included in an abbreviated departure clearance. Answer (C) is incorrect. This option does not specify the destination airport or a DP. The destination airport is always included in an abbreviated departure clearance. DPs are also included whenever they are appropriate.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What action should the pilot take when “gate hold” procedures are in effect?

choices.text: Contact ground control prior to starting engines for sequencing.
Taxi into position and hold prior to requesting clearance.
Start engines, perform pretakeoff check, and request clearance prior to leaving the parking area.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Gate hold가 시행되거나 출발지연이 15분을 초과할 것으로 예상되면 엔진 시동 전에 ground control 또는 clearance delivery에 연락해야 한다. 초기 호출 순서에 따라 출발 순서가 보통 유지된다.
questions.explanation_en: Pilots should contact ground control or clearance delivery prior to starting engines as gate hold procedures will be in effect whenever departure delays exceed or are anticipated to exceed 15 min. Pilots should monitor the ground control or clearance delivery frequency for engine startup advisories or new proposed start time if the delay changes. The sequence for departure will normally be maintained in accordance with the initial call-up. Answer (B) is incorrect. “Taxi into position” means that the pilot is on the active runway and ready for takeoff. This is not a position where ATC would issue an IFR clearance. Answer (C) is incorrect. Pilots should contact ground control for sequencing before, not after, starting engines.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Aircraft are expected to

choices.text: depart no earlier than 5 minutes before and no later than 5 minutes after the EDCT.
depart no earlier than 5 minutes before and no later than 15 minutes after the EDCT.
depart no earlier than 15 minutes before and no later than 15 minutes after the EDCT.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. EDCT는 교통관리 프로그램 대상 항공기에 지정되는 runway release time이며, 항공기는 EDCT 5분 전보다 일찍 또는 5분 후보다 늦게 출발해서는 안 된다.
questions.explanation_en: The Expect Departure Clearance Time (EDCT) is the runway release time assigned to an aircraft included in traffic management programs. Aircraft are expected to depart no earlier than 5 minutes before and no later than 5 minutes after the EDCT. Answer (B) is incorrect. Aircraft are expected to depart no earlier than 5 minutes before and no later than 5, not 15, minutes after the EDCT. Answer (C) is incorrect. Aircraft are expected to depart no earlier than 5, not 15, minutes before and no later than 5, not 15, minutes after the EDCT.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When should transponders be operated on the ground while taxiing?

choices.text: Only when ATC specifically requests your transponder to be activated.
Any time when the airport is operating under IFR.
All the time when at an airport with ASDE-X.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. ASDE-X가 있는 공항에서 지상 이동 중에는 고도보고 기능을 포함해 트랜스폰더를 계속 송신 상태로 유지해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: If operating at an airport with Airport Surface Detection Equipment - Model X (ASDE-X), transponders should be transmitting continuously with altitude reporting while moving on the airport surface. ASDE-X is a multi-sensor surface surveillance system the FAA is acquiring for airports in the U.S. Answer (A) is incorrect. If you are operating at an airport with ASDE-X, your transponder should be transmitting continuously with altitude reporting while moving on the airport surface, not only when ATC specifically requests your transponder to be activated. Answer (B) is incorrect. If you are operating at an airport with ASDE-X, your transponder should be transmitting continuously with altitude reporting while moving on the airport surface, not only when the airport is operating under IFR.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the purpose of the term “hold for release” when included in an IFR clearance?

choices.text: A procedure for delaying departure for traffic volume, weather, or need to issue further instructions.
When an IFR clearance is received by telephone, the pilot will have time to prepare for takeoff prior to being released.
Gate hold procedures are in effect and the pilot receives an estimate of the time the flight will be released.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 'Hold for release'는 기상·교통량 등 교통관리 사유로 출발을 지연시키는 지시이다. release time을 받거나 추가 ATC 지시를 받을 때까지 출발할 수 없다.
questions.explanation_en: ATC may issue “hold for release” instructions in a clearance to delay an airplane’s departure for traffic management reasons (i.e., weather, traffic volume, etc.). The pilot may not depart until (s)he receives a release time or is given additional instructions by ATC. Answer (B) is incorrect. When a pilot receives an IFR clearance via telephone, it is normally because (s)he is departing from an uncontrolled airport. In this case, ATC issues a clearance void time, not a hold for release. Answer (C) is incorrect. Gate hold procedures are in effect whenever departure delays exceed (or are expected to exceed) 15 min. This procedure is not a way for ATC to delay an airplane’s departure.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What special consideration is given for turbine-powered aircraft when “gate hold” procedures are in effect?

choices.text: They are given preference for departure over other aircraft.
They are expected to be ready for takeoff when they reach the runway or warmup block.
They are expected to be ready for takeoff prior to taxi and will receive takeoff clearance prior to taxi.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Gate hold 절차가 시행 중일 때 ATC는 터빈항공기가 활주로 또는 warmup block에 도착하면 이륙 준비가 된 것으로 간주한다.
questions.explanation_en: When gate hold procedures are in effect, ATC will consider that pilots of turbine-powered aircraft are ready for takeoff when they reach the runway or warmup block. Answer (A) is incorrect. When gate hold procedures are in effect, sequencing of all airplanes is based on the initial call-up to ground control or clearance delivery. Answer (C) is incorrect. A pilot of any airplane should be ready to taxi, not take off, prior to taxi, and takeoff clearance is received prior to takeoff, not taxi.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Pilots should state their position on the airport when calling the tower for takeoff

choices.text: from a runway intersection, only at night.
from a runway intersection, only during instrument conditions.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 공항 처리능력 향상과 taxi 거리·출발지연 감소를 위해 ATC는 intersection takeoff를 제안하거나 조종사 요청을 승인할 수 있다. 교차점에서 이륙을 요청할 때는 공항 내 현재 위치를 함께 알려야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: In order to enhance airport capacities, reduce taxiing distances, minimize departure delays, and provide for more efficient movement of air traffic, controllers may initiate intersection takeoffs as well as approve them when the pilot requests. A pilot should state his or her position on the airport when calling the tower for takeoff from a runway intersection. Answer (B) is incorrect. A pilot should state his or her position on the airport when calling the tower for takeoff from a runway intersection at all times. Answer (C) is incorrect. A pilot should state his or her position on the airport when calling the tower for takeoff from a runway intersection under all, not just instrument, conditions.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 243 on page 325 and Figure 244 on page 326.) At Fort Lauderdale, HS 5 probably points out a potential operational risk of an airplane

choices.text: mistaking taxiway B for runway 09L and making the takeoff roll on the taxiway.
landing runway 09L and taxiing on C.
landing runway 27R and clearing taxiway B2, which crosses runway 13.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Airport hot spot은 충돌 또는 runway incursion 위험 이력이 있거나 잠재위험이 있어 조종사·운전자의 각별한 주의가 필요한 movement area 지점이다. Fort Lauderdale HS 5는 taxiway를 활주로로 오인해 출발할 위험이 있는 지점이다.
questions.explanation_en: An airport hot spot is a location on an airport movement area with a history of potential risk of collision or runway incursion, and where heightened attention by pilots and drivers is necessary. See the hot spot description to the right of Fort Lauderdale, FL airport, HS 5. This gives the description of the hazard that is present, taxiway departure risk. If a pilot is not careful, a departure could be done on taxiway B instead of Rwy 09L. Answer (B) is incorrect. Taxiway C is near the very beginning of Rwy 09L. Landing on Rwy 09L and then taxiing on taxiway C would be improbable. Answer (C) is incorrect. Taxiway B2 does not cross runway 13. There is no hot spot circle near taxiway B2 or runway 13.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 243 on page 325 and Figure 244 on page 326.) At Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International, HS 1 probably points out a potential incursion risk of an airplane

choices.text: taxiing across runway 09L at taxiway Bravo for a runway 31 departure.
taxiing onto runway 09L instead of runway 13 as instructed for takeoff.
landing on runway 13 and clearing at taxiway Bravo and crossing runway 30.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Airport hot spot은 충돌 또는 runway incursion 위험이 높은 movement area 지점이다. Fort Lauderdale HS 1은 Rwy 13과 09L 부근으로, 허가받은 Rwy 13 대신 09L로 잘못 진입해 이륙할 위험이 있다.
questions.explanation_en: An airport hot spot is a location on an airport movement area with a history of potential risk of collision or runway incursion, and where heightened attention by pilots and drivers is necessary. See the hot spot description to the right of Fort Lauderdale, FL airport, HS 1. It lists the hot spot as “Twy E at Rwy 09L-27R.” Fig. 244 shows HS 1 near the intersection of Rwy 13 and 09L. This could be an area of potential incursion risk for a pilot to taxi onto Runway 09L for takeoff instead of Runway 13, the runway the pilot was cleared to take off on. Answer (A) is incorrect. HS 1 is not indicating that taxiway Bravo is a hot spot as there is no hot spot circle on a Bravo taxiway. Answer (C) is incorrect. There is not a runway 30 to cross.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When taxiing on an airport with ASDE-X, you should

choices.text: operate the transponder only when the airport is under IFR or at night during your taxi.
operate the transponder with altitude reporting all of the time during taxiing.
be ready to activate the transponder upon ATC request while taxiing.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. ASDE-X가 설치된 공항에서는 지상 이동 중 트랜스폰더와 altitude reporting을 계속 송신해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: If operating at an airport with Airport Surface Detection Equipment - Model X (ASDE-X), transponders should be transmitting continuously with altitude reporting while moving on the airport surface. ASDE-X is a multi-sensor surface surveillance system the FAA is acquiring for airports in the United States. Answer (A) is incorrect. When taxiing on an airport with ASDE-X, you should operate the transponder with altitude reporting all the time during taxiing, not only when the airport is under IFR or at night. Answer (C) is incorrect. When taxiing on an airport with ASDE-X, you should operate the transponder with altitude reporting all the time during taxiing, not just upon ATC request.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Hot Spots are depicted on airport diagrams as

choices.text: squares or rectangles around “HS and a number.”
circles or polygons around “HS and a number.”
triangles or blocks filled with “HS” and a number.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Airport surface hot spot은 충돌 또는 runway incursion의 과거 이력이나 잠재 위험이 있는 movement area 지점이며, 공항도에는 원 또는 다각형으로 표시하고 HS 1, HS 2 등으로 식별한다.
questions.explanation_en: An airport surface Hot Spot is a location on an airport movement area with a history or potential risk of collision or runway incursion. Heightened attention by pilots and drivers is necessary. Hot Spots are depicted on airport diagrams as open circles or polygons and designated as “HS 1,” “HS 2,” etc. Answer (A) is incorrect. Hot Spots are depicted on airport diagrams as open circles or polygons, not squares or rectangles, and designated as “HS 1,” “HS 2,” etc. Answer (C) is incorrect. Hot Spots are depicted on airport diagrams as open circles or polygons, not triangles or blocks, and designated as “HS 1,” “HS 2,” etc.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: An airport movement area is

choices.text: an area requiring permission from ATC to move an aircraft.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Movement area는 항공기의 taxi/hover taxi/air taxi/이륙/착륙에 사용되는 활주로·유도로 및 기타 구역이며 ramp와 parking area는 제외한다. 관제탑이 운영되면 진입 전 ATC의 명시적 승인이 필요하다.
questions.explanation_en: A movement area is defined as the runways, taxiways, and other areas of an airport and heliport which are utilized for taxiing or hover taxiing, air taxiing, takeoff and landing of aircraft, exclusive of loading ramps and parking areas. At those airports and heliports with an operating control tower, specific approval for entry onto the movement area must be obtained from ATC. Answer (A) is incorrect. An ATC control zone (CTR or controlled traffic region) is a volume of controlled airspace, normally around an airport, which extends from the surface to a specified upper limit and is established to protect air traffic operating to and from that airport. A movement area does not include the airspace above it. Answer (C) is incorrect. A movement area is exclusive of ramps and aprons.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Under what condition does a pilot receive a “void time” specified in the clearance?

choices.text: When “gate hold” procedures are in effect.
If the clearance is received prior to starting engines.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 비관제공항에서 IFR clearance에 void time이 주어질 수 있다. 그 시각 전에 출발하지 않으면 clearance는 무효가 되며, 지상에 남아 있으면 가능한 한 빨리, 통상 최대 30분 이내에 ATC에 의도를 알려야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: A pilot will receive a “void time” in an IFR clearance when operating from an uncontrolled airport. If the flight has not departed prior to the void time, the clearance is void. The pilot who is still on the ground at the void time must advise ATC of his or her intentions as soon as possible, normally within a maximum of 30 min. Answer (B) is incorrect. Gate hold procedures are in effect whenever departure delays exceed or are anticipated to exceed 15 min. Pilots should contact ground control or clearance delivery prior to starting engines to receive departure clearance and engine startup advisories. Answer (C) is incorrect. Clearances can be issued before starting the airplane’s engine(s). Only when operating from an uncontrolled airport will the clearance contain a “void time.”

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 241 on page 329 and Figure 242 on page 330.) At Long Beach (LGB), HS 2 probably points out a potential incursion hazard of an airplane

choices.text: landing on runway 25R and taxiing on K3.
taxiing across runway 34L at taxiway G.
landing on runway 25R and clearing at taxiway B, which crosses runway 30.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Airport hot spot은 충돌 또는 runway incursion 위험이 있어 특별한 주의가 필요한 지점이다. Long Beach HS 2는 Rwy 12-30, Rwy 07L-25R, Taxiway B/K가 관련되며, Rwy 25R 착륙 후 Taxiway B로 이탈하면 Rwy 30을 횡단하게 되는 위험지점이다.
questions.explanation_en: An airport hot spot is defined as a location on an airport movement area with a history of potential risk of collision or runway incursion, and where heightened attention by pilots and drivers is necessary. Refer to the first page of Fig. 241 and the column to the right of Long Beach, CA, Long Beach (Daugherty Fld) (LGB). Look at HS 2. This hot spot refers to Rwy 12-30 and Rwy 07L-25R, taxiway B and taxiway K. Landing long on Rwy 25R would have the aircraft exit the runway at taxiway B. Taxiway B crosses Rwy 30. The hot spot is taxiway B with the circle around it. Answer (A) is incorrect. Taxiway K3 has no hot-spot circle around that area and it runs into taxiway K. There are on hot spots in those areas. Answer (B) is incorrect. The hot spot for Rwy 34L is taxiway F as indicated by the circle around runway 34 and taxiway F.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 241 on page 329 and Figure 242 on page 330.) At Long Beach (LGB), HS 5 probably points out a potential operational risk of an airplane

choices.text: landing runway 7R and mistakenly crossing runway 34L while taxiing on taxiway F.
landing runway 25R and mistakenly turning onto runway 34R instead of taxiway K.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Long Beach HS 5는 Taxiway F와 Runway 34L 접근단 부근의 hot spot으로, 부주의하면 Taxiway F로 taxi하면서 Runway 34L을 횡단할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: An airport hot spot is defined as a location on an airport movement area with a history of potential risk of collision or runway incursion, and where heightened attention by pilots and drivers is necessary. Refer to the hot-spot description to the right of Long Beach (LGB) airport, HS 5. The hazard is located at taxiway F and the approach end of runway 34L. If a pilot is not careful, (s)he may taxi on taxiway F and cross runway 34L. Answer (B) is incorrect. If landing on runway 25R, there is no taxiway K to exit on. Answer (C) is incorrect. If a pilot landed long on runway 7R, (s)he may cross runway 12, but there is no hot-spot circle in that area and no HS 5 label near that runway.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 241 on page 329 and Figure 242 on page 330.) You land on Runway 12 at LGB and plan to exit the runway to the right on Taxiway J. What potential risk should you be aware of on the airport diagram?

choices.text: Convergence of taxiways D and J.
Convergence of taxiways C and J.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fig. 242에서 Taxiway J와 D의 교차점이 Runway 12와 매우 가까우며, 이 지점이 각별한 주의가 필요한 HS 4로 표시된다.
questions.explanation_en: On Fig. 242, notice that the intersection of taxiways J and D is very close to runway 12. This area has been highlighted as HS 4 (hot spot) where heightened attention by pilots is necessary. Answer (B) is incorrect. The convergence of taxiways C and J would not present a hazard since you plan to exit west by turning right onto taxiway J. Answer (C) is incorrect. The convergence of runways 16R-34L and 07R-25L would not present a hazard as you will turn onto taxiway J prior to reaching their intersection.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 242 on page 330.) ATC instructs you to taxi to runway 12 via taxiway K, cross runway 34R, and hold short of runway 30. You know

choices.text: to taxi on K from the terminal ramp, cross 34R, and then hold short of runway 30.
you must call prior to crossing runway 34R.
to taxi to runway 12 via taxiway G and D after clearing runway 34R.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 관제탑 운영시간에는 활주로 taxi, 이륙, 착륙 및 모든 활주로 횡단 전에 clearance가 필요하다. ATC는 활주로 횡단에 명시적 허가를 발부하고, hold-short 지시는 반드시 read back해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Clearance must be obtained prior to taxiing on a runway, taking off, or landing during the hours an Airport Traffic Control Tower is in operation. A clearance must be obtained prior to crossing any runway. ATC will issue an explicit clearance for all runway crossings. ATC will not use the word “cleared” in conjunction with authorization for aircraft to taxi. All hold-short instructions must be read back to ATC. Answer (B) is incorrect. ATC gave an explicit clearance for crossing runway 34R, therefore you do not need to call ATC prior to crossing runway 34R. Answer (C) is incorrect. ATC gave instructions to taxi to runway 12 via taxiway K, not via taxiway G and D.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 242 on page 330.) You received these ATC taxi instructions: “Taxi to Runway 30 via Lima and hold short of Runway 25L.” Your airplane is on the ramp by the terminal and NWS on the east side of the airport. Your taxi route

choices.text: requires crossing of Runway 25L at Lima.
requires crossing Runway 34R en route to the assigned runway.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. ATC가 Runway 25L 앞에서 hold short를 지시했더라도 Runway 30으로 가는 taxi route는 결국 Taxiway Lima에서 Runway 25L을 횡단하게 된다.
questions.explanation_en: While ATC has instructed you to hold short of Runway 25L, your taxi route to Runway 30 will eventually require you to cross Runway 25L at taxiway Lima. Answer (B) is incorrect. Your taxi route will keep you west of Runway 34R at all times, but hot spot 4 (HS 4) is east of Runway 34R. Answer (C) is incorrect. Your taxi route requires you to cross Runway 25L, not Runway 34R, en route to Runway 30.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 242 on page 330 and Figure 241 on page 332.) As you rolled out long on Runway 30 after landing at Long Beach (LGB), you slowed and turned left on very wide pavement and now see Taxiway D signs on both sides of your pavement. You notice your heading is about 250°. Tower is urging you to turn left on D, cross 16R/34L, then taxi to G and hold short of Runway 30. You now know you

choices.text: exited onto Runway 25R and transited HS 2.
exited at Taxiway J and transited HS 4.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Runway 25R은 폭 150 ft이며 출발단 부근에서 Runway 30과 교차한다. Runway 30에서 25R로 좌회전하면 먼저 비스듬히 교차하는 Taxiway D를 보게 되고, Taxiway D로 진입해 Runway 16R/34L을 횡단하면 HS 2를 통과하게 된다.
questions.explanation_en: Runway 25R, which is 150 feet wide, intersects Runway 30 near the departure end. If you turned left onto Runway 25R from Runway 30, you would initially see the intersection of Taxiway D, which crosses the runway at an angle. Before the intersection, both sides of the runway would be marked with direction signs featuring a black “D” on a yellow background. Turning left onto Taxiway D and crossing Runway 16R/34L would require you to transit hot spot 2 (HS 2). Answer (B) is incorrect. If you had exited on Taxiway G, ATC would not have instructed you to turn left onto Taxiway D and cross Runway 16R/34L. Answer (C) is incorrect. Exiting at Taxiway J near hot spot 4 (HS 4) would require exiting near the midpoint of Runway 30, not near the end, as would be the case after a long rollout.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: An ATC “instruction”

choices.text: is the same as an ATC “clearance.”
is a directive issued by ATC for the purpose of requiring a pilot to take a specific action.
must be “read back” in full to the controller and confirmed before becoming effective.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. ATC instruction은 조종사에게 특정 행동을 요구하는 지시로, 'Turn left heading 250', 'Go around', 'Clear the runway' 등이 해당한다.
questions.explanation_en: An ATC instruction is a directive issued by ATC for the purpose of requiring a pilot to take a specific action, e.g., “Turn left, heading 250,” “Go around,” “Clear the runway,” etc. Answer (A) is incorrect. An ATC clearance is an authorization by ATC for an aircraft to proceed under specified traffic conditions within controlled airspace. An instruction is more specific; e.g., “Turn left heading 250.” Answer (C) is incorrect. Although instructions should be (and some are required to be) read back to the controller, they are effective immediately.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the pilot’s responsibility for clearance or instruction readback?

choices.text: Except for SIDs, read back altitude assignments, altitude restrictions, and vectors.
If the clearance or instruction is understood, an acknowledgment is sufficient.
Read back the entire clearance or instruction to confirm the message is understood.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 고도 배정·고도 제한·vector가 포함된 ATC clearance나 instruction은 상호 확인을 위해 받은 순서대로 read back하는 것이 원칙이다. 차트에 이미 공표된 SID 고도는 controller가 직접 말하지 않은 한 다시 읽을 필요가 없다.
questions.explanation_en: Pilots should read back the parts of ATC clearances and instructions containing altitude assignments or vectors as a means of mutual verification. Altitudes, altitude restrictions, and vectors should be read back in the same sequence as they are given in the clearance or instruction. Altitudes contained in charted procedures, such as SIDs, should not be read back unless they are specifically stated by the controller. Answer (B) is incorrect. The best way to know that the clearance or instruction is understood is to read back the “numbers” as a double-check between the pilot and ATC. This practice reduces the kinds of communication errors that occur when a number is either misheard or incorrect. Answer (C) is incorrect. The pilot’s responsibility is to read back the clearances and instructions containing altitude assignments, altitude restrictions, and vectors, not the entire clearance or instruction.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What action should a pilot take when a clearance is received from ATC that appears to be contrary to a regulation?

choices.text: Read the clearance back in its entirety.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. PIC는 항공기 운항에 직접 책임을 지는 최종 권한자이다. ATC clearance가 규정 위반을 초래하거나 안전을 위협한다고 판단되면 조종사가 ATC에 clarification을 요청해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: 14 CFR 91.3(a) states: “The pilot in command of an aircraft is directly responsible for, and is the final authority as to, the operation of that aircraft.” If ATC issues a clearance that would cause a pilot to deviate from a rule or regulation or, in the pilot’s opinion, would place the airplane in jeopardy, it is the pilot’s responsibility to request a clarification from ATC. Answer (A) is incorrect. Reading the clearance back in its entirety does not inform ATC of the possible conflict to a regulation. A pilot should actively seek clarification if there is any doubt. Answer (C) is incorrect. Not accepting a clearance is not the proper procedure to use when, in a pilot’s opinion, it would conflict with a regulation. First, a pilot should receive a clarification from ATC, then ask for an amended clearance, if necessary.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What action should a pilot take if within 3 minutes of a clearance limit and further clearance has not been received?

choices.text: Assume lost communications and continue as planned.
Plan to hold at cruising speed until further clearance is received.
Start a speed reduction to holding speed in preparation for holding.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Clearance limit까지 3분 이내인데 그 fix 이후의 clearance를 받지 못했다면 holding에 대비해 fix를 최대 holding speed 이하로 통과하도록 감속을 시작해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: When an airplane is within 3 min. from a clearance limit and a clearance beyond the fix has not been received, the pilot is expected to start a speed reduction so the airplane will initially cross the fix at or below the maximum holding speed in preparation for holding. Answer (A) is incorrect. If two-way communications are lost, the pilot is required to hold at the clearance limit in a standard pattern on the course that was used to approach the fix. If an expected further clearance time was received, (s)he should plan on leaving the fix at that time. If none was given and the fix is an IAP, (s)he should plan his or her arrival as close as possible to the estimated time of arrival. Answer (B) is incorrect. Cruising speed may be greater than maximum holding speed. For all propeller-driven airplanes (including turboprop), the maximum holding speed is 175 KIAS. For turbojet airplanes, the maximum holding airspeed is 200 KIAS from minimum holding altitude through 6,000 ft.; 230 KIAS from above 6,000 ft. through 14,000 ft.; and 265 KIAS above 14,000 ft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What report should the pilot make at a clearance limit?

choices.text: Time and altitude/flight level arriving or leaving.
Time, altitude/flight level, and expected holding speed.
Time, altitude/flight level, expected holding speed, and inbound leg length.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Clearance limit에 도착한 시각과 고도/flight level을 ATC에 보고하고, clearance limit을 떠날 때도 보고해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: The pilot should report to ATC the time and altitude/flight level at which the airplane reaches the clearance limit, and (s)he should report leaving the clearance limit. Answer (B) is incorrect. ATC does not need the expected holding speed reported since it will be at or below the maximum holding airspeed. Answer (C) is incorrect. Inbound leg lengths are set by time or DME distance. At or below 14,000 ft. MSL, there is a 1-min. inbound leg. Above 14,000 ft. MSL, the inbound leg is 1 1/2 min.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: As you call for taxi instructions, the key words to understand are
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. ATC taxi instruction에는 공항 내 목적지, taxi route, 필요한 hold-short 지시 및 활주로 횡단 clearance가 포함된다. 핵심 표현은 'hold short of'와 'cross'이며 관련 지시는 정확히 read back해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: When giving taxi instructions, ATC will specify the destination on the airport, issue a taxi route, and state any hold-short instructions or runway crossing clearances if the taxi route will cross a runway. A clearance must be obtained prior to crossing any runway, and pilots should always read back any instruction to hold short of or cross a specific runway. Therefore, the key words to understand are “hold short of” and “cross.” Answer (A) is incorrect. In order to preclude misunderstandings in radio communications, ATC will not use the word “cleared” in conjunction with authorization for aircraft to taxi. Answer (C) is incorrect. The key words to understand are “hold short of” and “cross,” not “taxi to” and “expedite.”

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: You must

choices.text: read back runway hold-short instructions only if you are unsure of their meaning.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. ATC는 모든 runway hold-short instruction에 대해 조종사의 read-back을 받아야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: ATC is required to obtain a read-back from the pilot of all runway hold-short instructions. Answer (A) is incorrect. Acknowledging hold-short instructions is not enough. You are required to read back all runway hold-short instructions. Answer (B) is incorrect. You must read back all hold-short instructions, whether you are sure or unsure of their meaning.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When ATC clears you onto or across a runway,

choices.text: scan the full runway and the runway approach corridor prior to entering the runway.
proceed as quickly as possible to help with traffic flow.
call ATC as soon as you are in position or clear of the runway for further instructions.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 활주로에 진입할 때는 활주로가 active인지와 관계없이 전 길이를 확인하고 final 접근·landing rollout 항공기와 장주의 downwind/base 양쪽을 살펴야 한다. 'clear left, clear right, clear to cross' 식 확인이 좋은 습관이다.
questions.explanation_en: Whenever a pilot is going to enter a runway, whether that runway is active or not, (s)he should be vigilant when doing so. The pilot should scan the full length of the runway and look for aircraft on final approach or landing roll-out. (S)he should also check both right and left corners of the downwind and base legs of the pattern. It is good practice to check and call out, “clear left, clear right, and clear to cross.” Answer (B) is incorrect. Taxiing as quickly as possible leads to incidents or accidents. It is not recommended. Answer (C) is incorrect. When in position, you should only call ATC if takeoff clearance is not received within a reasonable amount of time after clearance to line up and wait. Contacting ATC when clear of the runway is not necessary, unless further instructions have not been received.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When ATC issues a clearance to descend “at pilot’s discretion,” the pilot

choices.text: can descend when the pilot wishes.
can climb back to the original altitude, if needed.
must maintain a descent rate of 2,000 ft/min.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 'Descend at pilot's discretion'을 받으면 조종사는 원하는 시점과 강하율로 강하하고 중간 어느 고도에서도 level off할 수 있지만, 한 번 이탈한 고도로 다시 올라갈 수는 없다.
questions.explanation_en: When a pilot receives the clearance to descend “at pilot’s discretion,” the pilot may descend at any time and any rate and may level off at any altitude during the descent. However, the pilot may not return to any vacated altitude. Answer (B) is incorrect. Once the descent is started, the pilot cannot return to the vacated altitude. Answer (C) is incorrect. The pilot can descend at any rate (s)he wishes.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What action should a pilot take if asked by ARTCC to “VERIFY 9,000” and the flight is actually maintaining 8,000?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. ATC가 특정 고도를 verify하라고 하면 실제 그 고도를 유지 중인지 확인해 보고해야 한다. 예를 들어 'VERIFY 9,000'을 받았지만 실제 8,000 ft 유지 중이면 'maintaining 8,000'이라고 보고한다.
questions.explanation_en: At times a controller will ask a pilot to verify that (s)he is at a particular altitude. The pilot should confirm that (s)he is at the altitude stated by the controller, or (s)he should inform the controller of the actual altitude being maintained, if different. If asked by ARTCC to “VERIFY 9,000” and the flight is actually maintaining 8,000, the pilot should report maintaining 8,000. Answer (A) is incorrect. A pilot should not take action to change his or her actual altitude to the altitude stated in the controller’s verification request unless the controller specifically authorizes a change. Answer (B) is incorrect. A pilot should not take action to change his or her actual altitude to the altitude stated in the controller’s verification request unless the controller specifically authorizes a change.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Where are position reports required on an IFR flight on airways or routes?

choices.text: Over all designated compulsory reporting points.
Only where specifically requested by ARTCC.
When requested to change altitude or advise of weather conditions.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 정확한 position report는 교통관제 안전에 중요하다. IFR 항로의 compulsory reporting point에서는 식별부호, 위치, 시각, 고도/FL, 비행계획 종류, 다음 보고점 ETA와 명칭, 그 다음 보고점 명칭, 관련 remarks를 보고한다. 강제보고점은 항로도에서 실선 삼각형으로 표시된다.
questions.explanation_en: The safety and effectiveness of traffic control depends to a large extent on accurate position reporting. A position report for an IFR flight along airways or routes is required over all designated compulsory reporting points along the route being flown. Position reports should include the following: identification, position, time, altitude/flight level, type of flight plan, ETA and name of next reporting point, the name only of the next succeeding reporting point along the route, and pertinent remarks. Compulsory reporting points are indicated on en route charts by a solid triangle. Answer (B) is incorrect. The “on request” reporting point is indicated on en route charts by an open, not solid, triangle. Reports passing an “on request” reporting point are necessary only when requested by ARTCC. Answer (C) is incorrect. Pilots on IFR flight plans must always report when changing altitude and are expected to report weather conditions which have not been forecast or any hazardous conditions.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which reports are required when operating IFR in radar environment?

choices.text: Position reports, vacating an altitude, unable to climb 500 ft/min, and time and altitude reaching a holding fix or point to which cleared.

Position reports, vacating an altitude, unable to climb 500 ft/min, time and altitude reaching a holding fix or point to which cleared, and a change in average true airspeed exceeding 5 percent or 10 knots.

Vacating an altitude, unable to climb 500 ft/min, time and altitude reaching a holding fix or point to which cleared, a change in average true airspeed exceeding 5 percent or 10 knots, and leaving any assigned holding fix or point.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. ATC가 'RADAR CONTACT'라고 통보하면 지정 보고점의 정기 position report는 중단한다. 다만 고도 이탈, 500 fpm 이상 상승·강하 불가, holding fix 도착 시각·고도, TAS 5% 또는 10 kt 초과 변화, holding fix 이탈, missed approach 등은 항상 보고해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: When informed by ATC that his or her airplane is in “RADAR CONTACT,” the pilot should discontinue position reports over designated reporting points. A pilot will report at all times vacating an altitude, inability to climb/descend at a rate of at least 500 fpm, time and altitude upon reaching a holding fix or point to which cleared, a change in average true airspeed exceeding 5% or 10 kt., leaving any assigned holding fix or point, and a missed approach. Answer (A) is incorrect. Position reports are not required in a radar environment. A pilot must also report a change in average TAS (exceeding 5% or 10 kt.), leaving any assigned holding fix or point, and a missed approach. Answer (B) is incorrect. Position reports are not required in a radar environment. A pilot must also report when leaving any assigned holding fix or point and when the approach has been missed.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which of the following reports should always be reported to ATC?

choices.text: Preferred runway choice to limit taxi time.
When true airspeed (TAS) varies by 10 percent or 5 knots, whichever is less.
When leaving an assigned holding fix.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 지정된 holding fix 또는 point를 떠날 때는 ATC 요청이 없어도 보고해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: A report should be made to ATC without a specific request when leaving any assigned holding fix or point. Answer (A) is incorrect. Reporting your preferred takeoff runway is not required, but you can make a request for a runway other than the one in use. Answer (B) is incorrect. Reporting is required for variations in average true airspeed exceeding 5% or 10 kt., not 10% or 5 kt.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When a speed adjustment is necessary to maintain separation, what minimum speed may ATC request of a turbine-powered aircraft operating below 10,000 feet?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 레이더 관제 중 ATC의 속도조정은 필요한 간격 확보를 위한 것이며 IAS 기준 10 kt 단위로 지시한다. 10,000 ft MSL 미만의 터빈항공기에는 최소 210 kt를 요청할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: ATC will issue speed adjustments to pilots of radar-controlled aircraft to achieve or maintain required or desired spacing. ATC will express all speed adjustments in knots based on indicated airspeed in 10-kt. increments. ATC may request a minimum speed of 210 kt. of a turbine-powered airplane operating below 10,000 ft. MSL. Answer (A) is incorrect. The maximum airspeed of any airplane operating below 2,500 ft. AGL within 4 NM of the primary airport in Class C or Class D airspace, in a VFR-designated corridor through Class B airspace, or in airspace underlying Class B airspace is 200 kt. Answer (C) is incorrect. The maximum airspeed of any airplane operating below 10,000 ft. MSL and within Class B airspace is 250 kt.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When a speed adjustment is necessary to maintain separation, what minimum speed may ATC request of a turbine-powered aircraft departing an airport?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 출발하는 터빈항공기에 ATC가 요청할 수 있는 최소 속도는 230 kt이다.
questions.explanation_en: ATC will issue speed adjustments to pilots of radar-controlled airplanes to achieve or maintain required or desired spacing. ATC will express all speed adjustments in knots based on indicated airspeed in 10-kt. increments. For departing turbine-powered aircraft, the minimum speed that ATC may request is 230 kt. Answer (A) is incorrect. An applicable airspeed for any ATC operation is not 188 kt. All airspeeds used by ATC/Federal Aviation Regulations are expressed in 10-kt. increments. Answer (B) is incorrect. The minimum airspeed that ATC can request of a turbine-powered airplane operating below 10,000 ft. MSL, excluding departing airplanes, is 210 kt.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: If ATC requests a speed adjustment that is not within the operating limits of the aircraft, what action must the pilot take?

choices.text: Maintain an airspeed within the operating limitations as close to the requested speed as possible.
Attempt to use the requested speed as long as possible, then request a reasonable airspeed from ATC.
Advise ATC of the airspeed that will be used.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 속도조정이 항공기 운용한계를 벗어나면 조종사는 이를 거부할 권한이 있으며 실제 사용할 속도를 ATC에 알려야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: The pilot retains the authority to reject the application of speed adjustment by ATC. If the speed adjustment is not within the operating limits of the airplane, the pilot is expected to advise ATC of the airspeed that will be used. Answer (A) is incorrect. While a pilot should maintain at least the minimum safe airspeed for any particular operation, a pilot is expected to advise ATC of the airspeed being used when it differs from ATC’s requested speed adjustment. Answer (B) is incorrect. A pilot who uses an airspeed that is not within the operating limits of the airplane not only is in violation of Federal Aviation Regulations but also is risking the safety of all on board the airplane. A pilot must operate the airplane in a safe manner and advise ATC of the airspeed that will be used.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: An airplane operating in cruise at 10,000 feet, 200 knots calibrated with an OAT of 68°F has a true airspeed of
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. E6B에서 68°F는 20°C이다. Pressure altitude 10과 20°C를 맞춘 뒤 계산하면 해당 조건의 속도는 약 244 kt가 된다.
questions.explanation_en: Using an E6B flight computer, find the temperature conversion scale and covert 68°F to Celsius. 68°F equates to 20°C. Line up 10 in the pressure altitude window with the temperature scale above, at 20°C. Find 20 on the outer scale of the inner wheel. Across from 20 is the second hash mark past the 24. This represents 244 knots. Answer (A) is incorrect. An airspeed of 16 knots higher, or 216 knots, would require a calibrated airspeed of almost 178 knots. Answer (B) is incorrect. An airspeed of 33 knots higher, or 233 knots, would require a calibrated airspeed of almost 192 knots.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Under what conditions may a pilot on an IFR flight plan comply with authorization to maintain “VFR-on-Top”?

choices.text: Maintain IFR flight plan but comply with visual flight rules while in VFR conditions.
Maintain VFR altitudes, cloud clearances, and comply with applicable instrument flight rules.
Maintain IFR altitudes, VFR cloud clearances, and comply with applicable instrument flight rules.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. IFR 비행계획으로 VFR 기상에서 비행 중인 조종사는 배정고도 대신 VFR-on-top을 요청할 수 있다. 승인되면 VFR 순항고도와 VFR 구름거리·시정을 유지하면서도 IFR 최저고도, 위치보고, 통신, 항로 및 ATC clearance 준수 등 IFR 규칙을 계속 따라야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: A pilot on an IFR flight plan operating in VFR weather conditions may request VFR-on-top instead of an assigned altitude. When ATC authorizes maintenance of VFR-on-top, pilots on IFR flight plans must maintain VFR altitudes, maintain VFR cloud clearances and visibilities, and comply with applicable instrument flight rules. These rules include minimum IFR altitudes, position reporting, radio communications, courses to be flown, and adherence to ATC clearances. Answer (A) is incorrect. Not only will a pilot remain on the IFR flight plan and comply with VFR altitudes, visibility, and cloud clearances, (s)he must also comply with applicable IFR rules, e.g., position reporting, minimum IFR altitudes. Answer (C) is incorrect. While operating on a VFR-on-top clearance, a pilot must maintain VFR, not IFR, altitudes.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What cloud clearance must be complied with when authorized to maintain “VFR-on-Top”?

choices.text: May maintain VFR clearance above, below, or between layers.
Must maintain VFR clearance above or below.
May maintain VFR clearance above or below, but not between layers.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. VFR-on-top은 구름층 위에서만 비행하라는 뜻이 아니다. 기상조건이 허용하면 층 위·아래·층 사이 또는 기상장애가 없는 구역에서 운항할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: ATC authorization to maintain VFR-on-top is not intended to restrict pilots so that they must operate only above a layer. Instead, it permits operation above, below, or between layers, or in areas where there is no meteorological obscuration. Answer (B) is incorrect. An authorization to maintain VFR-on-top allows a pilot to maintain VFR clearance not only above or below, but also between layers. Answer (C) is incorrect. An authorization to maintain VFR-on-top allows a pilot to maintain VFR clearance above, below, and between layers.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: In what airspace will ATC not authorize “VFR-on-Top”?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. ATC는 Class A 공역에서 VFR 또는 VFR-on-top을 허가하지 않는다. Class A는 FL 180부터 FL 600까지이다.
questions.explanation_en: ATC will not authorize VFR or VFR-on-top operations in Class A airspace. Class A airspace extends from FL 180 up to, and including, FL 600. Answer (A) is incorrect. While there may be some restrictions due to separation, a pilot can operate VFR-on-top in Class C airspace. Answer (B) is incorrect. While there may be some restrictions due to separation, a pilot can operate VFR-on-top in Class B airspace.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What separation or service by ATC is afforded pilots authorized “VFR-on-Top”?

choices.text: The same afforded all IFR flights.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. IFR 비행계획 항공기 사이에는 원칙적으로 분리가 제공되지만, Class B/C 밖에서 VFR-on-top 중인 경우에는 예외가 될 수 있다. 이때 ATC는 traffic advisory를 제공할 수 있으나 see-and-avoid 책임은 조종사에게 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Separation will be provided between all aircraft operating on IFR flight plans except during VFR-on-top operations outside Class B or Class C airspace. Under these conditions, ATC may issue traffic advisories, but it is the responsibility of the pilot to be vigilant in order to see and avoid other aircraft. Answer (A) is incorrect. Separation will be provided for all IFR flights except those operating with a VFR-on-top clearance. In that case, only traffic advisories may be provided. Answer (B) is incorrect. When radar is employed for separation of aircraft at the same altitude, a minimum of 3 mi. separation is provided between airplanes operating within 40 mi. of the radar antenna site, and 5 mi. between aircraft operating beyond 40 mi. from the antenna site.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Under what condition should a pilot on IFR advise ATC of minimum fuel status?

choices.text: When the fuel supply becomes less than that required for IFR.
If the remaining fuel suggests a need for traffic or landing priority.
If the remaining fuel precludes any undue delay.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 목적지 도착 시 추가 지연을 감당하기 어려울 정도로 연료가 줄면 ATC에 'minimum fuel' 상태를 알려야 한다. 이는 비상선언이 아니라 추가 지연 시 비상상황으로 발전할 수 있음을 알리는 advisory이다.
questions.explanation_en: A pilot should advise ATC of minimum fuel status when the remaining fuel supply has reached a state which precludes any undue delay upon reaching destination. A pilot must be aware that this is not an emergency situation but an advisory that indicates an emergency situation is possible should any undue delay occur. Answer (A) is incorrect. A pilot must ensure the minimum amount of fuel is on board the airplane for the planned IFR flight and alternatives, if needed, during the flight planning phase. Answer (B) is incorrect. If the remaining fuel suggests a need for traffic or landing priority, the pilot should declare an emergency, not minimum fuel status, due to low fuel and report fuel remaining in minutes.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What minimum condition is suggested for declaring an emergency?

choices.text: Anytime the pilot is doubtful of a condition that could adversely affect flight safety.
When fuel endurance or weather will require an en route or landing priority.
When distress conditions such as fire, mechanical failure, or structural damage occurs.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Emergency는 distress 또는 urgency 상태를 포함한다. 화재·기계고장·구조손상은 distress가 될 수 있고, 위치·연료지속시간·기상 등 비행안전에 영향을 주는 사항에 의문이 생긴 것만으로도 최소 urgency 상태가 될 수 있으므로 상황이 악화되기 전에 비상을 선언해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: An emergency is defined as either a distress or an urgency condition. A distress condition can be a fire, mechanical failure, or structural damage. An airplane is in at least an urgency condition when the pilot becomes doubtful about position, fuel endurance, weather, or any other condition that could adversely affect flight safety. A pilot should declare an emergency under any of these circumstances, not after the situation has developed into a distress condition. Answer (B) is incorrect. If fuel endurance or weather will require an en route or landing priority, the situation has progressed beyond an urgency condition and is now a distress condition. Answer (C) is incorrect. Distress condition implies a serious and/or imminent danger requiring immediate assistance. This situation is the step after an urgency condition, which is one that has the potential to become a distress condition.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: You should advise ATC of minimum fuel status when your fuel supply has reached a state where, upon reaching your destination, you cannot accept any undue delay.

choices.text: This will ensure your priority handling by ATC.
ATC will consider this action as if you had declared an emergency.
If your remaining usable fuel supply suggests the need for traffic priority to ensure a safe landing, declare an emergency due to low fuel and report fuel remaining in minutes.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 'Minimum fuel' 통보 자체는 비상이 아니며 traffic priority를 의미하지 않는다. 안전한 착륙을 위해 우선권이 필요할 정도로 usable fuel이 부족하면 low fuel emergency를 선언하고 남은 연료를 분 단위로 보고해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Advising ATC of minimum fuel status is not considered an emergency, nor does it imply a need for traffic priority. However, if the remaining usable fuel supply suggests the need for traffic priority to ensure a safe landing, you should declare an emergency due to low fuel and report fuel remaining in minutes. Answer (A) is incorrect. A minimum fuel advisory does not imply a need for traffic priority, only that you cannot accept any undue delay. Answer (B) is incorrect. Declaring minimum fuel is not an emergency situation but merely an advisory that indicates an emergency situation is possible should any undue delay occur.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What does the term “minimum fuel” imply to ATC?

choices.text: Traffic priority is needed to the destination airport.
Emergency handling is required to the nearest suitable airport.
Upon reaching the destination, the aircraft can accept little or no delay.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. ATC는 minimum fuel 보고를 추가 지연 시 비상상황이 될 수 있다는 advisory로 취급하며, 이 보고 자체로 traffic priority가 생기지는 않는다.
questions.explanation_en: When a pilot advises ATC of a minimum fuel status, ATC will handle this report as an advisory that indicates an emergency situation is possible should an undue delay occur. A minimum fuel advisory does not imply a need for traffic priority. Answer (A) is incorrect. A pilot should declare an emergency due to low fuel and report fuel remaining in minutes if traffic priority is needed to the destination airport. Answer (B) is incorrect. Emergency handling to the nearest suitable airport is required in a distress or urgent type of emergency.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which range of codes should a pilot avoid switching through when changing transponder codes?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 일반적인 코드 변경 시 7500·7600·7700을 실수로 선택하지 않도록 주의해야 한다. 7500은 unlawful interference/hijack, 7600은 radio failure, 7700은 general emergency, 7777은 military interceptor operation에 사용된다.
questions.explanation_en: When making routine code changes, pilots should avoid inadvertent selection of codes 7500, 7600, or 7700, which can cause momentary false alarms at automated ground facilities. This applies to nondiscrete code 7500 and all discrete codes in the 7600 and 7700 series. Remember that 7500 is for hijack, 7600 for lost radio communications, 7700 for general emergency, and 7777 for military interceptor operations. Answer (A) is incorrect. Codes 0000 through 1000 are acceptable codes that may be used during normal operations. Answer (B) is incorrect. The 7200 series can be used during normal operations, while 7500 should be avoided except in the case of a hijack.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the hijack code?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Transponder code 7500은 항공기가 납치되거나 강제로 다른 목적지로 향하고 있음을 뜻한다. 조종사의 사전 통보 없이 ATC가 임의로 배정하지 않으며, 선택 시 모든 radar ATC 시설에 특별 비상표시가 작동한다.
questions.explanation_en: Transponder code 7500 means: “I am being hijacked/forced to a new destination.” Code 7500 will never be assigned by ATC without prior notification from the pilot that his or her airplane is being subjected to unlawful interference. Code 7500 will trigger special emergency indicators in all radar ATC facilities. Answer (A) is incorrect. Code 7200 is used for normal operating procedures. Answer (C) is incorrect. Under no circumstances should a pilot of a civil airplane operate the transponder on Code 7777. This code is reserved for military interceptor operations.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: It is the responsibility of the pilot and crew to report a near midair collision as a result of proximity of at least

choices.text: 50 feet or less to another aircraft.
500 feet or less to another aircraft.
1,000 feet or less to another aircraft.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Near midair collision은 다른 항공기와 500 ft 미만까지 접근해 충돌 가능성이 발생한 사건을 말한다. 실제 NMAC 여부 판단과 보고 개시는 조종사/승무원의 책임이다.
questions.explanation_en: A near midair collision is defined as an incident associated with the operation of an airplane in which a possibility of collision occurs as a result of proximity of less than 500 ft. to another airplane. It is the responsibility of the pilot and/or flight crew to determine whether a near midair collision did actually occur and to initiate a near midair collision report. Answer (A) is incorrect. A near midair collision is reported if the possibility of a collision occurs as a result of proximity of less than 500 ft., not 50 ft., to another airplane. Answer (C) is incorrect. Proximity of greater than 500 ft. is not considered a near midair collision and would not be reported as such.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Under what condition does ATC issue safety alerts?

choices.text: When collision with another aircraft is imminent.
If the aircraft altitude is noted to be in close proximity to the surface or an obstacle.
When weather conditions are extreme and wind shear or large hail is in the vicinity.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. ATC는 관제 중인 항공기가 지형·장애물·다른 항공기에 위험하게 근접했다고 판단하면 safety alert를 발령한다. 지형/장애물 근접에는 terrain or obstruction alert, 다른 항공기 근접에는 aircraft conflict alert가 사용된다.
questions.explanation_en: ATC will issue a safety alert when an airplane under its control is at an altitude which, in ATC’s judgment, places the aircraft in unsafe proximity to terrain, obstructions, or another aircraft. A terrain or obstruction alert is issued to an airplane that is at an altitude believed to place the aircraft in unsafe proximity to terrain or obstructions. An aircraft conflict alert is issued when an airplane under a controller’s direction is at an altitude believed to place the aircraft in unsafe proximity to another airplane not under that controller’s direction. Answer (A) is incorrect. A safety alert is issued to a pilot if ATC believes that his or her airplane is at an altitude which will place it in unsafe proximity to another airplane, not that a collision is imminent. Answer (C) is incorrect. When weather conditions are extreme and wind shear or large hail is in the vicinity, a convective SIGMET, not a safety alert, is broadcast.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim

subunit.title: Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS)

questions.question: TCAS I provides

choices.text: recommended maneuvers to avoid conflicting traffic.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. TCAS I은 침입 항공기를 눈으로 찾는 데 도움이 되는 proximity/traffic 경고만 제공하며, 직접적인 회피기동 권고는 제공하지 않는다.
tags: Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS)
questions.explanation_en: TCAS I provides only a proximity warning to assist the pilot in the visual acquisition of intruder aircraft. No recommended avoidance maneuvers are provided or authorized as a direct result of a TCAS I warning. Answer (A) is incorrect. TCAS II, not TCAS I, provides traffic and resolution advisories. TCAS I provides only a proximity warning. Answer (C) is incorrect. TCAS II, not TCAS I, provides recommended maneuvers to avoid conflicting traffic and resolution advisories. TCAS I provides only a proximity warning.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim

subunit.title: Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS)

questions.question: TCAS II provides

choices.text: maneuvers in all directions to avoid the conflicting traffic.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. TCAS II는 Traffic Advisory와 Resolution Advisory를 제공하며, RA는 충돌 회피를 위해 수직방향의 상승 또는 강하 기동을 권고한다.
tags: Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS)
questions.explanation_en: TCAS II provides traffic and resolution advisories. Resolution advisories provide recommended maneuvers in a vertical direction (climb or descend only) to avoid conflicting traffic. Answer (B) is incorrect. TCAS I, not TCAS II, provides only a proximity warning. TCAS II provides traffic and resolution advisories. Answer (C) is incorrect. TCAS II provides recommended maneuvers only in a vertical direction, not in all directions, to avoid conflicting traffic.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim

subunit.title: Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS)

questions.question: Each pilot who deviates from an ATC clearance in response to a TCAS advisory is expected to notify ATC and

choices.text: maintain the course and altitude resulting from the deviation, as ATC has radar contact.
expeditiously return to the ATC clearance in effect prior to the advisory, after the conflict is resolved.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. TCAS II RA에 따라 ATC clearance에서 이탈했다면 가능한 한 빨리 ATC에 알리고, 충돌 위험이 해소되면 신속히 현재 ATC clearance로 복귀해야 한다.
tags: Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS)
