questions.explanation_en: Fig. 114A provides an en route low-altitude chart. In the bottom portion, locate POM VORTAC (center). The flag with the X indicates a minimum crossing altitude (MCA). Since no MCA is given southwest bound on V210, the minimum en route altitude (MEA) is also the MCA. The MEA is to the right of the POM VORTAC symbol with an arrow pointing southwest, which is 5,300 ft. Answer (A) is incorrect. The MEA from MEANT INT to CALBE INT when southwest bound on V210, not the MCA at POM VORTAC, is 10,700 ft. Answer (B) is incorrect. The MCA on V210 northeast, not southwest, bound, is 10,300 ft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 185A below, and Figure 185 on page 395.) The maximum gross weight that an L1011 can be operated on RWY 01L/19R at McCarran Intl is
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fig. 185A의 McCarran Intl. Airport Remarks에 따르면 L-1011의 RWY 01L/19R 최대 gross weight는 496,000 lb이다.
questions.explanation_en: The bottom portion of Fig. 185A is the Chart Supplement excerpt for McCarran Intl. (LAS). Locate the Airport Remarks on Fig. 185 and go down six lines. The maximum gross weight that an L-1011 can be operated on RWY 01L/19R is 496,000 lb. Answer (B) is incorrect. This is the maximum gross weight for an MD-11, not an L-1011, to operate on RWY 01L/19R. Answer (C) is incorrect. This is the maximum gross weight for a DC-10, not an L-1011, to operate on RWY 01L/19R. om Chart Supplement.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 185A below, and Legend 12 on page 397.) McCarran Intl (LAS) is a Part 139 airport. What minimum number of aircraft rescue and fire fighting vehicles and type and amount of fire fighting agents should the airport have?

choices.text: Three vehicles and 500 pounds of dry chemical (DC) or Halon 1211 or 450 pounds DC and 6,000 gallons of water.
Two vehicles and 600 pounds dry chemical (DC) or Halon 1211 or 500 pounds of DC plus 4,000 gallons of water.
Three vehicles and 500 pounds of dry chemical (DC) or Halon 1211 or 450 pounds DC plus 3,000 gallons of water. Figure 185A. Excerpt fr

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fig. 185A에서 LAS의 ARFF Index는 E이다. 해당 기준상 최소 차량 3대와 500 lb DC 또는 HALON 1211, 혹은 450 lb DC와 6,000 gal 물 등 규정된 소화제가 필요하다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 185A is the Chart Supplement excerpt for LAS. First, look for the aircraft rescue and fire-fighting (ARFF) index on the second line, which is ARFF Index E. Next, Legend 12 is a Chart Supplement legend. Look at the table above item 16. Find the airport index E to determine that the minimum number of vehicles is three and that the airport is required to have at least 500 lb. of dry chemical (DC) or HALON 1211, or 450 lb. DC and 6,000 gal. of water (H2O). Answer (B) is incorrect. LAS is required to have at least three, not two, vehicles. Answer (C) is incorrect. LAS is required to have at least 6,000 gal., not 3,000 gal., of water. om Chart Supplement.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 315 below, and Figure 185A on page 399.) The threshold of RWY 07L at McCarran Intl is displaced

choices.text: 1,659 feet, due to a pole. Figure 315. Airpo

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Fig. 185A의 RWY 07L 정보에 따르면 hangar 때문에 threshold가 2,138 ft displaced되어 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Refer to Fig. 185A. Locate the fifth line down from the top, which begins with RWY 07L. Move to the right of that line, which states that the threshold is displaced 2,138 ft. due to a hangar. Answer (A) is incorrect. RWY 19L, not 07L, threshold is displaced 878 ft. due to a pole. Answer (C) is incorrect. RWY 07L threshold is displaced 2,138 ft., not 1,659 ft., due to a hangar, not a pole. rt Diagram (LAS).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 329 on page 401, Figure 201 on page 402, and Figure 201A on page 403.) What type of weather information would normally be expected to be available from the Weather Data Source at Ogden-Hinckley?

choices.text: Cloud height, weather, obstructions to vision, temperature, dewpoint, altimeter, surface winds, and any pertinent remarks.
Cloud bases/tops, obstructions to vision, altimeter, winds, precipitation, and the intensity of the precipitation.
Cloud height, obstructions to vision, temperature, dewpoint, altimeter, wind data, and density altitude.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Ogden-Hinckley Chart Supplement의 Weather Data Sources에는 ASOS가 표시된다. ASOS는 운고, 시정장애, 기온, 이슬점, altimeter, 바람자료 및 density altitude 등을 보고한다.
questions.explanation_en: Figs. 201 and 201A are the Chart Supplement excerpts for Ogden-Hinckley. Move down to locate the line “Weather Data Sources,” which indicates ASOS. An Automated Surface Observation System (ASOS) reports cloud height, obstructions to vision, temperature, dew point, altimeter, wind data, and density altitude. Answer (A) is incorrect. The weather data source listed in Fig. 201 is ASOS, which also provides density altitude information. Answer (B) is incorrect. Cloud top information is normally supplied by PIREPs.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 210 on page 470.) The route between FIS (near Key West) and MTH, which is labeled B646, is an example of a
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. FIS에서 MTH로 이어지는 B646은 얇은 짙은 갈색 선으로 표시된 LF/MF oceanic route이다.
questions.explanation_en: The route labeled B646 from FIS to MTH is a thin, dark brown line that indicates a LF/MF oceanic route. Answer (A) is incorrect. A LF/MF airway would be indicated by a wider brown line, not a thin brown line. Answer (C) is incorrect. A MTR is indicated by a thin, light brown line such as IR-53 to the south of B646.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 210 on page 470 and Figure 211 on page 471.) The Miami Flight Service Station has

choices.text: Remote Communications Outlet (RCO) northeast of MIA which operates on 122.3.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fig. 210의 Dolphin VORTAC 통신 박스 오른쪽 위 검은 원 안의 H는 HIWAS(Hazardous Inflight Weather Advisory Service)를 뜻한다.
questions.explanation_en: The Dolphin VORTAC communication box is shown on Fig. 210. The black circle with an “H” in the upper right corner indicates Hazardous Inflight Weather Advisory Service (HIWAS). Answer (B) is incorrect. The RCO northeast of MIA VORTAC operates on 126.7, not 122.3. Answer (C) is incorrect. ASOS/AWOS is indicated by a letter A in a black circle.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 100 on page 451.) (Refer to spot 8.) Where is the VOR changeover point on V571 between Navasota (TNV) and Humble (IAH)?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fig. 100에서 V571의 changeover point를 보면 IAH VORTAC까지 거리는 24 NM이다.
questions.explanation_en: Refer to Fig. 100. To the left of spot 8, locate V571, then find the changeover point symbol with the number pointing to the applicable VORTAC. The number at the top is the distance to IAH VORTAC, 24 nautical miles. Answer (B) is incorrect. The numbers on the changeover symbol point to the applicable VORTAC; 18 is the distance to the TNV VORTAC. Answer (C) is incorrect. The halfway point is only used if no changeover point is otherwise specified.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 259 on page 405.) What effect on approach minimums, if any, does an inoperative MALSR have for an aircraft with an approach speed of 120 knots at IAH?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Fig. 259의 ILS/LOC RWY 33R에서 Category B 항공기의 기본 visibility는 RVR 2,400 ft이다. MALSR가 불능이면 표에 따라 visibility를 증가시켜 3/4 SM, 즉 RVR 4,000 ft가 된다.
questions.explanation_en: This is where the FAA probably wants to test your resource management skills, as some figures are left out that would assist in getting this answer correct. Refer to Legend 26, the U.S. Terminal Procedures Inoperative Components or Visual Aids Table, on page 361. Item (1) is used for ILS, PAR, LPV, and GLS approaches. In item (1) of the table, notice that all approach categories are affected; then move right to determine that the visibility minimum is increased 1/4 SM, or an RVR of 1,600 ft. (This can be found in Legend 28 on page 363.) Refer to the ILS or LOC RWY 33R IAP in Fig. 259 and locate the minimums section. An approach speed of 120 kt. is for a Category B (91-120) airplane, and the visibility minimum is an RVR of 1/2 SM, or an RVR of 2,400 ft. With the MALSR inoperative, the approach minimum increases the visibility to 3/4 SM, or an RVR of 4,000 ft. Answer (A) is incorrect. With an inoperative MALSR, there is no change to the MDA but an increase of 1/4 SM to the required visibility. Answer (C) is incorrect. Adding 1/2 SM to the RVR would make the RVR visibility 1 SM, or 5,000 feet.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 259 on page 405.) Which approach lighting is available for Rwy 33R?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 259 heading section의 두 번째 줄 두 번째 박스는 RWY 33R에 MALSR(중강도 접근등과 runway alignment indicator lights)가 설치되어 있음을 나타낸다.
questions.explanation_en: The second box on the second line of the heading section of Fig. 259 indicates RWY 33R is serviced by a medium-intensity approach lighting system with runway alignment indicator lights. Answer (A) is incorrect. Medium-intensity runway lights (MIRL) are runway edge, not approach, light systems. Answer (B) is incorrect. Touchdown zone (TDZ) and centerline lights (CL) are in-runway lights, not approach lights.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 273 below.) The touchdown zone elevation of the ILS RWY 25L approach at Phoenix Sky Harbor Intl is
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fig. 273 heading section 첫 줄 세 번째 박스에서 RWY 25L의 TDZE는 1,126 ft이다.
questions.explanation_en: The third box on the first line of the heading section of Fig. 273 indicates the touchdown zone elevation (TDZE) for RWY 25L is 1,126 feet. Answer (B) is incorrect. The airport elevation, not the touchdown zone elevation, is 1,135 feet. Answer (C) is incorrect. The touchdown zone elevation for RWY 25L is 1,126 feet, not 1,458 feet. OC RWY 25L (PHX).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 321 below.) The highest terrain shown in the planview section of the RNAV GPS-D approach to Eagle County Regional is
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. IAP planview에서 가장 높은 지형고도는 굵은 큰 점으로 표시된다. Eagle County Regional RNAV(GPS)-D 접근의 최고 지형고도는 14,007 ft이다.
questions.explanation_en: The highest spot elevation (terrain) shown in the planview section of an IAP chart is indicated by a large bold dot. The highest terrain shown in the planview section of the RNAV (GPS)-D IAP to Eagle County Regional is 14,007 ft., which is located in the lower right corner. Answer (A) is incorrect. The elevation of 11,320 ft. is that of the terrain located in the middle of the chart and is not the highest terrain in the entire planview section. Answer (C) is incorrect. The elevation of 15,100 ft. is the minimum safe altitude (MSA) within 25 NM of NEPRY. This altitude ensures obstacle clearance, but it is not the height of the highest terrain. GPS) –D (EGE).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 374 on page 409.) You are inbound to DEN from Dallas/Fort Worth (DFW), Center gives you a vector and a frequency for Denver Approach Control, but you miss-copy the frequency. You determine you probably were assigned

choices.text: 119.3 and should expect a tower frequency of 124.3.
120.35 and should expect a tower frequency of 132.35.
120.35 and should expect a tower frequency of 124.3.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 남쪽에서 Denver Intl로 접근할 때 approach control 주파수는 120.35이고, Denver Tower 주파수는 124.3이다.
questions.explanation_en: You are approaching from the south. As indicated on the Denver INTL instrument approach plate, under DENVER APP CON, the frequency above (SOUTH) is the frequency 120.35 for approach control, if you are flying from the south to the airport. In the block to the right of the approach control frequencies is DENVER TOWER frequency 124.3. Answer (A) is incorrect. The approach control frequency 119.3 is for aircraft flying north to the airport. Answer (B) is incorrect. The tower frequency is 124.3, not 132.35.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 311 below.) What is the lowest visibility that may exist at ACY prior to the final approach segment to continue the ILS RWY 13 approach?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 해당 Instrument Approach Plate의 straight-in ILS S-ILS 13 최소치 중 더 낮은 visibility는 RVR 1,800 ft이다.
questions.explanation_en: The Instrument Approach Plate specifies two sets of minimums for the Straight-in ILS approach listed to the right of S-ILS 13. The lowest of those two visibilities is 18 (1800 RVR). Answer (A) is incorrect. Visibility of 2 miles is indicated for a circling approach for a category D aircraft. Answer (C) is incorrect. On this plate, there is no 50 located anywhere in the profile view of this approach. OC RWY 13 (ACY).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 311 on page 410.) What is the lowest visibility that may exist at ACY prior to final approach segment to continue the S-LOC RWY 13 approach when the MALSR is inoperative (CAT D)?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Fig. 311 접근판의 note에 따르면 MALSR가 불능이면 S-LOC 13 Category D visibility를 RVR 5,000 ft로 증가시켜야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: The notes in the upper left corner of the instrument approach plate in Fig. 311 indicate that “For inoperative MALSR, increase S-LOC 13 Cat D visibility to RVR 5000.” Answer (A) is incorrect. There is no information referring to RVR 1,800. Cat E for the S-LOC would increase to RVR 6,000. Cat E would be increased to RVR 4,000 for the S-ILS. Answer (C) is incorrect. There is no information referring to 2 miles RVR. The notes in the upper left corner of the instrument approach plate in Fig. 311 indicate that “For inoperative MALSR, increase S-LOC 13 Cat D visibility to RVR 5000.”

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: What functions are provided by ILS?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. ILS는 기능적으로 ① localizer·glide slope의 유도정보, ② marker beacon·DME의 거리정보, ③ approach light·runway light의 시각정보로 나눌 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The ILS system may be divided functionally into the following three parts: 1. Guidance information -- localizer, glide slope 2. Range information -- marker beacon, DME 3. Visual information -- approach lights, runway lights Answer (A) is incorrect. Azimuth and distance information are provided by a TACAN. Answer (B) is incorrect. A localizer/DME approach provides azimuth and range information.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Within what frequency range does the localizer transmitter of the ILS operate?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. ILS localizer 주파수 범위는 108.10~111.95 MHz이다.
questions.explanation_en: The frequencies assigned for localizer transmission are from 108.10 to 111.95 MHz. Answer (A) is incorrect. Communications frequencies are above 117.95 MHz. Answer (C) is incorrect. The frequency band in which VORs operate is 108.10 to 117.95 MHz.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Which component associated with the ILS is identified by the first two letters of the localizer identification group?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Outer compass locator는 localizer 식별부호의 첫 두 글자로 식별한다.
questions.explanation_en: The outer compass locator is identified by the first two letters of the coded localizer identification group. Answer (A) is incorrect. Marker beacons are not identified by letters; only compass locators are so identified. Answer (B) is incorrect. A middle compass locator is identified by the last two letters of the localizer identification group, not the first two letters.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Which component associated with the ILS is identified by the last two letters of the localizer group?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Compass locator는 두 글자 식별부호를 송신한다. Outer locator는 localizer 식별부호의 앞 두 글자, middle locator는 뒤 두 글자를 사용한다.
questions.explanation_en: Compass locators transmit two-letter identification groups. The outer locator transmits the first two letters of the localizer identification group, and the middle locator transmits the last two letters of the localizer identification group. Thus, the middle compass locator is identified by the last two letters of the localizer identification group. Answer (A) is incorrect. A simple marker beacon is not identified by letters; only compass locators are so identified. Answer (C) is incorrect. An outer compass locator is identified by the first two letters of the localizer identification group, not the last two letters.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: What aural and visual indications should be observed over an ILS inner marker?

choices.text: Continuous dots at the rate of six per second.
Continuous dashes at the rate of two per second.
Alternate dots and dashes at the rate of two per second.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Inner marker는 Category II ILS 접근에서 middle marker와 threshold 사이, glide slope상의 지정 DH 지점을 나타낸다. 초당 6회의 연속 dot과 흰색 marker beacon light로 식별한다.
questions.explanation_en: The inner marker indicates a point at which an airplane is at a designated decision height on the glide slope between the middle marker and the landing threshold during a Category II ILS approach. It is identified with continuous dots keyed at the rate of six dots per second and a white marker beacon. Answer (B) is incorrect. Continuous dashes at the rate of two per second indicate the ILS outer marker, not inner marker. Answer (C) is incorrect. Alternate dots and dashes at the rate of two per second indicate the ILS middle marker, not inner marker.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: If installed, what aural and visual indications should be observed over the ILS back course marker?

choices.text: A series of two dot combinations and a white marker beacon light.
Continuous dashes at the rate of one per second and a white marker beacon light.
A series of two dash combinations and a white marker beacon light.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Back Course Marker가 설치된 경우 back course FAF를 나타낸다. 3000 Hz로 변조되고 두 개의 dot 조합 신호와 흰색 marker beacon light로 식별한다.
questions.explanation_en: The back course marker (BCM), where installed, indicates the back course final approach fix. The BCM is modulated at 3000 Hz and identified with two dots at a rate of 72 to 75 two-dot combinations per min. and a white marker beacon light. Answer (B) is incorrect. This is a nonsense indication. This description most closely resembles an ILS outer marker, which has continuous dashes at the rate of two per second. Answer (C) is incorrect. This is not a marker indication of any type. This description most closely resembles an ILS middle marker, which is identified by alternate dot/dash combinations at the rate of two per second.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: What aural and visual indications should be observed over an ILS middle marker?

choices.text: Continuous dots at the rate of six per second identified as a high-pitched tone.
Continuous dashes at the rate of two per second identified as a low-pitched tone.
Alternate dots and dashes at the rate of two per second identified as an intermediate tone.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Middle marker는 landing threshold에서 약 3,500 ft 지점을 나타내며, 중간 음높이로 초당 약 2회의 dot-dash 교대음이 들린다.
questions.explanation_en: The middle marker indicates a position approximately 3,500 ft. from the landing threshold and has an aural signal of alternating dots and dashes at two per second at an intermediate tone. Answer (A) is incorrect. Continuous dots at the rate of six per second indicate an ILS inner marker. Answer (B) is incorrect. Continuous dashes at the rate of two per second indicate an ILS outer marker.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: What aural and visual indications should be observed over an ILS outer marker?

choices.text: Continuous dots at the rate of six per second.
Continuous dashes at the rate of two per second.
Alternate dots and dashes at the rate of two per second.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. ILS outer marker는 초당 2회의 연속 dash 신호로 식별한다.
questions.explanation_en: An ILS outer marker is identified by continuous dashes at the rate of two per second. Answer (A) is incorrect. Continuous dots at the rate of six per second indicate an ILS inner marker. Answer (C) is incorrect. Alternating dots and dashes at the rate of two per second indicate an ILS middle marker.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: The lowest ILS Category II minimums are
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 가장 낮은 Category II 운항에서 PIC 최소치는 DH 100 ft와 RVR 1,200 ft이다.
questions.explanation_en: The pilot-in-command minimums for the lowest Category II minimums are a DH of 100 ft. and an RVR of 1,200 ft. Answer (A) is incorrect. A DH of 50 ft. is for Category III operations, not Category II. Answer (C) is incorrect. A DH of 150 ft. is for a pilot’s initial Category II authorization (for the initial 6-month period) only and is not the lowest DH for Category II operations.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: If the middle marker for a Category I ILS approach is inoperative,

choices.text: the RVR required to begin the approach is increased by 20%.
the DA/DH is increased by 50 feet.
the inoperative middle marker has no effect on straight-in minimums.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Category I ILS 접근에서는 middle marker가 필수 장비가 아니며, middle marker가 없어도 접근최저치가 변하지 않는다.
questions.explanation_en: Category I ILS approaches do not require a middle marker. The approach minimums are not affected by its absence. Answer (A) is incorrect. A middle marker is not required for Category I ILS approaches. The approach minimums as they pertain to RVR are not affected by its absence. Answer (B) is incorrect. A middle marker is not required for Category I ILS approaches. The approach minimums as they pertain to DA/DH are not affected by its absence.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Legend 72 on page 413.) The rate of descent for a 3.5° angle of descent glideslope is
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Instrument approach chart의 rate of climb/descent table에서 3.5°와 120 kt를 교차하면 필요한 강하율은 약 745 ft/min이다.
questions.explanation_en: Reference the rate of climb/descent table in the instrument approach chart legend (Legend 72). Match “3.5” in the left most column with “120” in the upper most row to determine a rate of descent of 745 ft/min. Answer (A) is incorrect. The rate of descent at 105 knots groundspeed when flying a 3.5° glideslope would calculate to be only 650 ft/min, not 745 ft/min. Answer (B) is incorrect. The speed value is given as an airspeed. To calculate the required rate of descent, it is necessary to use groundspeed, not airspeed.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: What is the lowest Category IIIA minimum?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 가장 낮은 Category IIIA 허가는 DH 없이 운항하며 RVR은 최소 700 ft이다.
questions.explanation_en: The lowest Category IIIA authorization is for no DH and an RVR of not less than 700 ft. Answer (A) is incorrect. A DH of 50 ft. is for some Category III operations, and an RVR of 1,200 ft. is for Category II operations. Answer (B) is incorrect. An RVR of 1,000 ft. does not exist for any category approach.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: How does the SDF differ from an ILS LOC?

choices.text: SDF -- offset from runway plus 4°, ILS -- aligned with runway.
SDF -- 15° usable off course indications, ILS -- 35°.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. ILS localizer course width는 약 3°~6°이고, SDF는 6° 또는 12°이다.
questions.explanation_en: The course width for an ILS localizer is from 3° to 6°, whereas the SDF is either 6° or 12° wide. Answer (B) is incorrect. An SDF may not be aligned with the centerline of the runway. Answer (C) is incorrect. The usable off-course indications are limited to 35° for both types of approaches.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: In addition to the localizer, glideslope, marker beacons, approach lighting, and HIRL, which ground components are required to be operative for a Category II instrument approach to a DH below 150 feet AGL?

choices.text: Radar, VOR, DME, runway exit lights, and RVR.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Administrator가 달리 승인하지 않는 한 Category II 운항에 필요한 지상 구성요소는 모두 설치되어 있고 작동해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Unless otherwise authorized by the Administrator, no person may operate a civil aircraft in a Category II operation unless each ground component required for the operation is installed and operating. Answer (A) is incorrect. Radar and DME are not required ground based components for Category II ILS operations. Answer (B) is incorrect. Runway end identifier lights (REIL) are used to provide rapid identification of the approach end of a runway and are not a required ground component for Category II ILS operations.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Which ground components are required to be operative for a Category II approach in addition to LOC, glideslope, marker beacons, and approach lights?

choices.text: Radar, VOR, DME, taxiway lead-off lights and RVR.
All of the required ground components.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Category II 접근의 세부 요건은 사용 장비와 활주로 지상시설에 따라 달라질 수 있으며, 실제 승인사항은 운영자의 OpSpec, Mspec 또는 LOA에서 확인한다.
questions.explanation_en: The specific requirements for conducting Category II approach operations are detailed in U.S. Department of Transportation Order 8400.13D, which acknowledges that different levels of operation may be authorized based on the equipment used by a specific operator and the ground equipment available at specific runways. Specific requirements can be found in an operator’s OpSpec, Mspec, or LOA. Answer (A) is incorrect. There is no requirement for DME or radar equipment in Category II approach operations. Answer (C) is incorrect. There is no requirement for Runway End Identifier Lights for Category II approach operations.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Which ground components are required to be operative for a Category II approach in addition to LOC, glide slope, marker beacons, and approach lights?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Category II ILS에는 LOC, glide slope, marker beacon, approach lights, HIRL, TDZL, RCLS, RVR 등 필요한 지상 구성요소가 작동해야 한다. 일부가 불능이면 DH 및/또는 visibility 증가가 필요할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Category II ILS operations require these ground components to be operative: LOC, glide slope, marker beacons, approach lights, high-intensity runway lights (HIRL), touchdown zone lights (TDZL), runway centerline lighting system (RCLS), and runway visual range (RVR). If any of these is inoperative, an increase in DH and/or visibility may be required. Answer (A) is incorrect. Radar is not a required Category II ILS ground component. Answer (B) is incorrect. Runway end identifier lights (REIL) are used to provide rapid identification of the approach end of a runway. They are not a required ground component for Category II ILS.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: How does the LDA differ from an ILS LOC?

choices.text: LDA -- offset from runway plus 3°, ILS -- aligned with runway.
LDA -- 15° usable off course indications, ILS -- 35°.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. LDA는 localizer와 비슷한 정확도와 유용성을 가지지만 완전한 ILS의 일부는 아니다. 활주로와 반드시 일치할 필요가 없으며 course와 활주로의 정렬 차가 30° 이내이면 straight-in minimum이 공표될 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The localizer-type directional aid (LDA) is of comparable utility and accuracy to a localizer but is not part of a complete ILS. The LDA does not have to be aligned with the runway. The straight-in minimum may be published if alignment does not exceed 30° between the course and the runway. ILS localizers are aligned with the runway. Answer (A) is incorrect. An SDF, not LDA, is fixed at either 6° or 12° wide. Answer (C) is incorrect. The usable off-course indications are limited to 35° for both types of approaches within 10 NM.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: What facilities may be substituted for an inoperative middle marker during a Category I ILS approach?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Middle marker 대신 compass locator 또는 PAR을 사용할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: A compass locator or precision radar (PAR) may be substituted for the middle marker. Answer (A) is incorrect. Surveillance radar (ASR) can be substituted for the outer marker, not the middle marker. Answer (C) is incorrect. Surveillance radar (ASR) can be substituted for the outer marker, not the middle marker.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Which “rule-of-thumb” may be used to approximate the rate of descent required for a 3° glidepath?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 3° glide slope에서 필요한 대략적인 강하율(ft/min)은 groundspeed(kt)에 5를 곱해 구할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: As a general rule, you can calculate the approximate rate of descent required for a 3° glide slope by multiplying your groundspeed (in knots) by 5. Answer (B) is incorrect. Eight times the groundspeed would be used to calculate the rate of descent required for a 4.5°, not a 3°, glide slope. Answer (C) is incorrect. Ten times the groundspeed would be used to calculate the rate of descent required for a 6°, not a 3°, glide slope.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: When is the course deviation indicator (CDI) considered to have a full-scale deflection?

choices.text: When the CDI deflects from full-scale left to full-scale right, or vice versa.
When the CDI deflects from the center of the scale to full-scale left or right.
When the CDI deflects from half-scale left to half-scale right, or vice versa.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. CDI full-scale deflection은 바늘이 중앙에서 완전히 왼쪽 또는 오른쪽 끝까지 편위된 상태를 뜻한다.
questions.explanation_en: A full-scale CDI deflection occurs when the CDI moves full left or right, i.e., is fully deflected to one side or the other. Answer (A) is incorrect. When the CDI deflects full-scale left to full-scale right (or vice versa), you have two full-scale deflections. Answer (C) is incorrect. A deflection from half-scale left to half-scale right (or vice versa) is two half-scale deflections, not a full-scale deflection.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: When simultaneous approaches are in progress, how does each pilot receive radar advisories?

choices.text: One pilot on tower frequency and the other on approach control frequency.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Simultaneous approach가 진행 중이면 radar advisory는 tower frequency에서 제공된다.
questions.explanation_en: Whenever simultaneous approaches are in progress, radar advisories will be provided on the tower frequency. Answer (B) is incorrect. Pilots will be advised to monitor the tower, not approach control, frequency to receive radar advisories and instructions. Answer (C) is incorrect. Both pilots will receive radar advisories on the tower frequency.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: When simultaneous ILS approaches are in progress, which of the following should approach control be advised of immediately?

choices.text: Any inoperative or malfunctioning aircraft receivers.
If a simultaneous ILS approach is desired.
If radar monitoring is desired to confirm lateral separation.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Simultaneous ILS approach가 진행 중이라는 통보를 받았을 때 수신기가 고장·불능이거나 simultaneous approach를 원하지 않으면 즉시 approach control에 알려야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: When advised that simultaneous ILS approaches are in progress, pilots shall advise approach control immediately if receivers are malfunctioning or inoperative or if simultaneous approach is not desired. Answer (B) is incorrect. Simultaneous approaches are issued at any time according to ATC needs, and it is not the responsibility of the pilot to request such an approach. Answer (C) is incorrect. Radar monitoring is always provided during simultaneous approaches.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Precision runway monitoring requires

choices.text: pilot responsibility to monitor 2 simultaneous radios.
pilot responsibility to monitor 2 ILS receivers.
detailed performance during the “decision region”: 1/3 dot localizer and 1/2 dot glideslope.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. PRM 접근에서는 primary frequency와 monitor frequency 두 개를 모두 감시해야 하며, 이는 한 주파수가 막혀 호출을 놓치는 것을 방지한다.
questions.explanation_en: The PRM requires pilots to monitor both the primary and the monitor frequencies. This system prevents missed calls due to a blocked frequency. Answer (B) is incorrect. The pilot is responsible for monitoring two communication frequencies, not two ILS receivers. Answer (C) is incorrect. The pilot is responsible to monitor two communication frequencies during a PRM approach. There is no additional responsibility for performance in the “decision region.”

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Precision Runway Monitoring (PRM) is

choices.text: an airborne RADAR system for monitoring approaches to two runways.
a RADAR system for monitoring approaches to closely spaced parallel runways.
a high update rate RADAR system for monitoring multiple aircraft ILS approaches to a single runway.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. PRM은 좁은 간격의 평행활주로 접근을 높은 갱신율로 정밀 감시하는 radar system으로, closely spaced parallel runway에 대한 simultaneous independent approach를 가능하게 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Precision Runway Monitoring (PRM) is a RADAR system with a high update rate that closely monitors approaches to closely spaced parallel runways. PRM is certified to produce simultaneous independent approaches to closely spaced parallel runways. Answer (A) is incorrect. Precision Runway Monitoring (PRM) is not an airborne RADAR system; it is a ground-based RADAR system with a high update rate that closely monitors approaches to closely spaced parallel runways. Answer (C) is incorrect. Precision Runway Monitoring (PRM) is not for monitoring multiple aircraft ILS approaches to a single runway. Precision Runway Monitoring (PRM) is a RADAR system with a high update rate that closely monitors approaches to two closely spaced parallel runways.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Utilizing PRM may require

choices.text: specialized training and monitoring 2 ILS frequencies.
tracking parameters within decision region to 1/3 dot localizer and 1/2 dot glide slope displayed.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. PRM 접근 중 조종사는 primary와 monitor 두 통신주파수를 모두 감시할 책임이 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The pilot is responsible to monitor two communication frequencies during a PRM approach: the primary and the monitor frequency. Answer (B) is incorrect. There is no requirement to monitor two ILS frequencies. The pilot must instead monitor two communication frequencies: the primary and the monitor. Answer (C) is incorrect. The PRM requires a pilot to monitor two specific communication frequencies. There is no requirement for tracking parameters in the decision region as this answer option suggests.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: How can the pilot determine, for an ILS runway equipped with MALSR, that there may be a penetration of the obstacle identification surfaces (OIS), and care should be taken in the visual segment to avoid any obstacles?

choices.text: The runway has a visual approach slope indicator (VASI).
The published visibility for the ILS is no lower than 3/4 SM.
The approach chart has a visual descent point (VDP) published.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. OIS(Obstacle Identification Surface)를 장애물이 침범한 경우 ILS 접근에 공표할 수 있는 visibility는 3/4 SM보다 낮을 수 없다.
questions.explanation_en: If there is penetration of the obstacle identification surfaces (OIS), the published visibility for the ILS approach can be no lower than 3/4 SM. Answer (A) is incorrect. If there is penetration of the obstacle identification surfaces for a particular approach, the way to determine that is to refer to the visibility minimums for the approach. A VASI-equipped runway is not an indication of the penetration of obstacle identification surfaces. Answer (C) is incorrect. If there is penetration of the obstacle identification surfaces for a particular approach, the way to determine that is to refer to the visibility minimums for the approach. An approach chart that has a published visual descent point is not an indication of the penetration of obstacle identification surfaces.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Pilots are responsible for knowing

choices.text: if the RNP missed approach is normal or reduced.
if the RNP registration is completed.
if they can conduct an RNP approach with an arc at a designated airspeed.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. RF(radius-to-fix) 곡선구간이 포함된 RNP 접근을 해당 속도로 수행할 능력이 있는지는 조종사가 확인해야 한다. 모든 항공기가 RF arc를 비행할 수 있는 것은 아니며, 절차 설계에는 항공기 속도·바람·bank angle이 고려된다.
questions.explanation_en: Pilots are responsible for knowing if they can conduct an RNP approach with an arc at a designated airspeed. Some RNP approaches have a curved path, also called a radius-to-a-fix (RF) leg. Since not all aircraft have the capability to fly these arcs, pilots are responsible for knowing if they can conduct an RNP approach with an arc or not. Aircraft speeds, winds, and bank angles have been taken into consideration in the development of the procedures. Answer (A) is incorrect. Missed approach procedures for the RNP are developed and based on standard approach speeds and a 200 ft./NM climb gradient. Any deviation from those standards will be indicated on the approach procedure, and the operator should ensure (s)he can comply with any published restrictions prior to conducting the operations. Answer (B) is incorrect. Special aircraft and aircrew authorization required procedures, like the RNP instrument approach procedures, are to be conducted by aircrews meeting special training requirements in aircraft that meet the specified performance and functional requirements.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 330 below.) TNA 90 is a CAT C aircraft and has received a clearance to fly the LOC RWY 19L, sidestep to RWY 19R. What are the minimums?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Category C 항공기의 SIDESTEP RWY 19R minimum은 approach plate profile view에 340 - 1 1/2로 공표되어 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The sidestep minimums for SIDESTEP RWY 19R for category C aircraft is listed in the Profile View of the approach plate. It is 340 - 1 1/2. Answer (B) is incorrect. Category A and B is 340/50. Answer (C) is incorrect. The Height Above Touchdown is 332, not the Minimum Descent Altitude. OC RWY 19L (SFO).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: When cleared to execute a published side-step maneuver, at what point is the pilot expected to commence this maneuver?

choices.text: At the MDA published or a circling approach.
As soon as possible after the runway environment is in sight.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Side-step 접근에서는 활주로 또는 runway environment가 보이는 즉시 가능한 한 빨리 side-step maneuver를 시작해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Pilots are expected to commence the side-step maneuver as soon as possible after the runway or runway environment is in sight. Answer (A) is incorrect. The side-step maneuver can only and should be performed as soon as possible after the runway or runway environment is in sight. Answer (B) is incorrect. The side-step maneuver can only and should be performed as soon as possible after the runway or runway environment is in sight.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: When cleared to execute a published sidestep maneuver for a specific approach and landing on the parallel runway, at what point is the pilot expected to commence this maneuver?

choices.text: At the published minimum altitude for a circling approach.
As soon as possible after the runway or runway environment is in sight.
At the localizer MDA minimums and when the runway is in sight.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Runway environment를 확보한 뒤 가능한 한 신속히 side-step maneuver를 시작하는 것이 원칙이다.
questions.explanation_en: Pilots are expected to commence the side-step maneuver as soon as possible after the runway or runway environment is in sight. Answer (A) is incorrect. The side-step maneuver can only and should be performed as soon as possible after the runway or runway environment is in sight, which may be below the published minimum altitude for a circling approach. Answer (C) is incorrect. The side-step maneuver should be performed as soon as possible after the runway or runway environment is in sight, which should be before the localizer MDA minimums.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Which is a valid localizer transmitter frequency?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Localizer transmitter는 108.10~111.95 MHz 범위의 odd tenth 주파수에서 50 kHz 간격으로 운용된다. 예를 들어 108.3은 표시상 108.30 MHz이다.
questions.explanation_en: The localizer transmitter operates between 108.10 MHz and 111.95 MHz, on odd tenths, with 50 kHz spacing between each frequency. The frequency 108.3 would be 108.30 on the radio display. Answer (A) is incorrect. The frequency of 109.2 MHz is an even tenth number frequency. A valid localizer frequency has an odd tenth number frequency. Answer (C) is incorrect. The frequency of 117.6 MHz is outside the operational frequency range of 108.10 to 111.95 MHz.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: The Glidepath Qualification Surface (GQS) limits the height of obstructions between

choices.text: the Final Approach Point and the Missed Approach Point.
any Initial Approach Point and the Final Approach Fix.
Decision Altitude and the Runway Threshold.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 장애물이 GQS(Glidepath Qualification Surface)를 초과하면 positive vertical guidance 접근을 승인할 수 없다. GQS는 DA와 runway threshold 사이의 장애물 높이를 제한한다.
questions.explanation_en: When obstructions exceed the height of the GQS, an approach procedure with positive vertical guidance is not authorized. The GQS limits the height of obstructions between the Decision Altitude (DA) and the Runway Threshold (RWT). Answer (A) is incorrect. Between the Final Approach Point and the Missed Approach Point is the descent phase of the approach and is a higher altitude than that of the Decision Altitude and the Runway Threshold. The extremely low altitude at the Decision Altitude and the Runway Threshold requires strict height limits of any obstructions. Answer (B) is incorrect. Any Initial Approach Fix and the Final Approach Fix are at an altitude that most obstructions are cleared.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 290 on page 419.) Where is the final approach fix for the simultaneous close parallel ILS PRM RWY 26 approach at PHL?

choices.text: FOSOM at 2,000 feet MSL and on course.
HOLEY descending to 2,000 feet MSL and established on course.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 정밀접근의 FAF는 profile view에서 번개 모양 기호로 표시되며 glide slope intercept 지점에 있다. 이 문제의 FAF 고도는 2,000 ft이다.
questions.explanation_en: The final approach fix (FAF) is indicated by the lightning bolt on this precision approach. The FAF altitude is indicated as 2,000 feet at the glideslope intercept. This is indicated by the lightning bolt symbol in the Profile view of the approach plate. Answer (A) is incorrect. FOSOM is labeled in the overhead view as an Initial Approach Fix (IAF) and is not the FAF. Answer (B) is incorrect. HOLEY is labeled in the overhead view as an Initial Approach Fix (IAF) and is not the FAF.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 279 below, and Figure 310 on page 421.) What is the required minimum reported weather to initiate the ILS RWY 9L approach at PHL in your CAT C turbine-powered airplane (no MEL items)?

choices.text: Ceiling at least 200 feet and RVR 2400.
Ceiling 300 feet minimum. Figure 279. ILS or LO

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 200 ft ceiling과 RVR 2400으로도 접근은 가능하지만, 접근판의 이중 별표 조건에 따라 필요한 최저 visibility는 RVR 1800이다.
questions.explanation_en: Although a 200-foot ceiling and a Runway Visual Range (RVR) of 2400 is enough to fly the approach, the minimum necessary weather is 1800 RVR as noted by the double asterisks (**) in the upper left corner of the approach plate. Answer (B) is incorrect. While this weather is good enough to conduct the approach, the minimum specified weather is a ceiling of at least 200 feet and RVR 1800 with autopilot, flight director, or heads-up display to decision altitude. Answer (C) is incorrect. Nowhere on the IAP is there listed a minimum altitude of 300 feet. C RWY 32R (ORD).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 279 below.) Where does the final approach segment begin on the ILS RWY 32R at ORD?

choices.text: MUNDY ORD, 4000 feet MSL. Figure 279. ILS or LO

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Final approach segment는 FAF에서 시작해 MAP에서 끝난다. 정밀접근의 FAF는 profile view의 번개 기호로 표시되고 glide slope intercept 지점에 위치한다.
questions.explanation_en: The final approach segment begins at the final approach fix (FAF) and ends at the missed approach point (MAP). For a precision approach, the FAF is depicted by a lightning bolt on the profile view of the approach procedure chart and is located at the glide slope intercept. Answer (B) is incorrect. INDDY is the start of the final approach segment for the LOC approach. Answer (C) is incorrect. MUNDY is the initial approach fix for the ILS or LOC procedure. C RWY 32R (ORD).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 292 below.) With no equipment inoperative (no MEL items) in your autopilot and flight director equipped airplane, you know you must have

choices.text: at least 2400 RVR to fly the approach.
a reported RVR of 1800 to fly the approach.
at least 2400 RVR to land. Figure 292. ILS or L

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 접근판 note의 'RVR 1800 authorized with use of FD or AP or HUD to DA'는 FD, autopilot 또는 HUD를 DA까지 사용하면 RVR 1,800 ft 운항이 허용된다는 뜻이다.
questions.explanation_en: There is a note at the top of the approach plate that reads: “. . . **RVR 1800 authorized with use of FD or AP or HUD to DA.” This indicates the use of 1,800 feet RVR is authorized when using a Flight Director (FD), an Autopilot (AP), or a Heads Up Display (HUD) to Decision Altitude (DA). Answer (A) is incorrect. The landing minimum for runway visual range is 2,400 RVR and not a minimum to fly the approach. Answer (C) is incorrect. The landing minimum for an aircraft without the use of a FD, AP, or HUD is 2,400 RVR. OC RWY 13 (LGA).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: A large or turbine-powered airplane approaching to land on a runway served by an ILS (if the airplane is ILS equipped)

choices.text: may completely ignore the ILS procedures and profiles.
shall fly that airplane at an altitude at or above the glide slope between the final approach fix and the DH/DA.
may fly any approach path if the airplane remains in VFR day conditions from the beginning of civil twilight to the end of civil twilight.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 장애물·지형 여유를 확보하려면 조종사는 가능한 한 glide slope를 정확히 유지해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: The pilot must make every effort to remain on the glide slope to assure obstacle (terrain) clearance is maintained. Answer (A) is incorrect. There have been airplane crashes on VFR days where the pilot did not remain at or above the glide slope. The glide slope assures that obstacles and terrain clearance is maintained. Answer (C) is incorrect. There are two approach paths to follow on an ILS approach, the localizer and the glide slope. It is irrelevant what time of day, VFR or IFR conditions, the pilot must remain at or above the glide slope and on the localizer during an ILS approach to assure obstacle and terrain clearance is maintained.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Which is a valid localizer transmitter frequency?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Localizer transmitter는 108.10~111.95 MHz에서 odd tenth, 50 kHz 간격으로 운용되며 111.3은 111.30 MHz로 표시된다.
questions.explanation_en: The localizer transmitter operates between 108.10 MHz and 111.95 MHz, on odd tenths, with 50 kHz spacing between each frequency. The frequency 111.3 would be 111.30 on the radio display. Answer (B) is incorrect. The frequency of 113.25 MHz is outside the operational frequency range of 108.10 MHz to 111.95 MHz. Answer (C) is incorrect. The frequency of 109.4 MHz is an even tenth number frequency. A valid localizer frequency has an odd tenth number frequency.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Aircraft navigating by GPS are considered, on the flight plan, to be
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. GPS로 항법하는 항공기는 RNAV 장비 항공기로 간주되므로 비행계획에 적절한 equipment suffix를 기재해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Aircraft navigating by GPS are considered to be RNAV-equipped aircraft; thus, the appropriate equipment suffix must be included on the flight plan. Answer (B) is incorrect. Aircraft navigating by GPS are considered to be RNAV, not astrotracker, equipped. Answer (C) is incorrect. Aircraft navigating by GPS are considered to be RNAV, not FMS/EFIS, equipped.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: The GPS Approach Overlay Program permits pilots to use GPS avionics when IFR for flying existing instrument approach procedures, except
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. GPS Approach Overlay Program은 SDF, LOC, LDA를 제외한 기존 IAP를 IFR에서 GPS avionics로 비행할 수 있게 한다.
questions.explanation_en: The GPS Approach Overlay Program permits pilots to use GPS avionics under IFR for flying existing IAPs, except SDF, LOC, and LDA procedures. Answer (A) is incorrect. The GPS Approach Overlay Program permits pilots to use GPS avionics under IFR for flying existing IAPs except SDF procedures. Answer (B) is incorrect. The GPS Approach Overlay Program permits pilots to use GPS avionics under IFR for flying existing IAPs except LOC, not TACAN, procedures.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Authorization to conduct any GPS operation under IFR requires that

choices.text: the equipment be approved in accordance with TSO C-115a.
the pilot must review appropriate weather, aircraft flight manual (AFM), and operation of the particular receiver.
procedures must be established for use in the event that the loss of RAIM capability is predicted to occur.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. IFR GPS 운항 승인을 위해서는 RAIM 상실이 예측될 때의 절차가 마련되어 있어야 한다. RAIM 상실이 예상되면 다른 승인 장비 사용, 출발 지연 또는 비행 취소 등의 조치를 해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Authorization to conduct any GPS operation under IFR requires, among others, that procedures be established for use in the event that the loss of RAIM capability is predicted to occur. In situations in which this event is encountered, the pilot must rely on other approved equipment, delay departure, or cancel the flight. Answer (A) is incorrect. To conduct any GPS operation under IFR, the equipment must be approved in accordance with TSO C-129 or equivalent. TSO C-115a does not meet the requirements of TSO C-129. Answer (B) is incorrect. Before conducting any GPS operation under IFR, the pilot must be thoroughly familiar with, not just review, the GPS equipment installed, the GPS operation manual, and the aircraft flight manual. Additionally, prior to any GPS IFR operation, the pilot must review the appropriate NOTAMs, not only the weather.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Without Receiver Autonomous Integrity Monitoring (RAIM) capability, the accuracy of the GPS derived

choices.text: altitude information should not be relied upon to determine aircraft altitude.
velocity information should be relied upon to determine aircraft groundspeed.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. RAIM은 위성이 잘못된 정보를 제공하는지 integrity를 감시한다. RAIM이 없으면 GPS가 산출한 고도는 수직오차가 클 수 있어 항공기 고도 결정에 신뢰해서는 안 된다.
questions.explanation_en: RAIM is used to determine if a satellite is providing corrupted information. Without RAIM capability, the accuracy of the GPS-derived altitude information should not be relied upon to determine aircraft altitude since the vertical error can be quite large. Answer (B) is incorrect. RAIM is used to determine if a satellite is providing corrupted information. Without RAIM, the GPS position should NOT be relied upon since the position solution can be greatly affected. Answer (C) is incorrect. RAIM is used to determine if a satellite is providing corrupted information.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Overriding an automatically selected sensitivity during a GPS approach will

choices.text: require flying point-to-point on the approach to comply with the published approach procedure.
have no effect if the approach is flown manually.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Approach mode가 armed된 상태에서 FAWP 2 NM 이내에 들어가면 approach mode가 active로 전환되어 RAIM과 CDI sensitivity가 접근용으로 강화된다. 접근 중 자동 선택된 sensitivity를 수동 override하면 approach mode annunciation이 취소된다.
questions.explanation_en: When within 2 NM of the final approach waypoint with the approach mode armed, the approach mode will switch to active, which results in RAIM changing to approach sensitivity and a change in CDI sensitivity. Overriding an automatically selected sensitivity during an approach will cancel the approach mode annunciation. Answer (B) is incorrect. Flying point-to-point on the approach does NOT ensure compliance with the published approach procedure. Answer (C) is incorrect. Manually setting CDI sensitivity does not automatically change RAIM sensitivity on some GPS receivers.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: If a visual descent point (VDP) is published on a GPS approach, it

choices.text: will not be included in the sequence of waypoints.
will be coded in the waypoint sequence and identified using ATD.
must be included in the normal waypoints.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. GPS 접근에 VDP가 공표되어 있어도 waypoint sequence에는 포함되지 않는다. 시각강하 시작은 조종사가 일반적인 visual piloting technique으로 판단한다.
questions.explanation_en: If a visual descent point (VDP) is published on a GPS approach, it will not be included in the sequence of waypoints. Pilots are expected to use normal piloting techniques for beginning the visual descent. Answer (B) is incorrect. A VDP will NOT be included in the waypoint sequence. Answer (C) is incorrect. If a VDP is published on a GPS approach, it will NOT be included in the normal waypoint sequence.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Authorization to conduct any GPS operation under IFR requires that

choices.text: the pilot review appropriate weather, aircraft flight manual (AFM), and operation of the particular GPS receiver.
air carrier and commercial operators must meet the appropriate provisions of their approved operations specifications.
the equipment be approved in accordance with TSO C-115a.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. IFR GPS 운항을 하는 air carrier와 commercial operator는 승인된 Operations Specifications의 해당 요건을 충족해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Authorization to conduct any GPS operation under IFR requires that, among others, air carriers and commercial operators meet the appropriate provisions of their approved operations specifications. Answer (A) is incorrect. Before conducting any GPS operation under IFR, the pilot must be thoroughly familiar with, not just review, the GPS equipment installed, the GPS operation manual, and the aircraft flight manual. Additionally, prior to any GPS IFR operation, the pilot must review the appropriate NOTAMs, not only the weather. Answer (C) is incorrect. To conduct any GPS operation under IFR, the equipment must be approved in accordance with TSO C-129 or equivalent. TSO C-115a does not meet the requirements of TSO C-129.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: A pilot employed by an air carrier and/or commercial operator may conduct GPS/WAAS instrument approaches

choices.text: if they are not prohibited by the FAA-approved aircraft flight manual and the flight manual supplement.
only if approved in their air carrier/commercial operator operations specifications.
only if the pilot was evaluated on GPS/WAAS approach procedures during their most recent proficiency check.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Air carrier 또는 commercial operation에서 GPS/WAAS 계기접근을 사용하려면 승인된 Operations Specifications의 관련 요건을 충족해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: In order to use GPS/WAAS instrument approaches, pilots employed by an air carrier or in commercial operations must meet the appropriate provisions of their approved operations specifications. Answer (A) is incorrect. Although the aircraft flight manual can prohibit specific activities via placards or approved maneuver lists, pilots employed by an air carrier or in commercial operations can legally conduct GPS/WAAS instrument approaches provided they meet the appropriate provisions of their approved operations specifications. Answer (C) is incorrect. Pilots employed by an air carrier or in commercial operations must meet the appropriate provisions of their approved operations specifications in order to use GPS/WAAS instrument approaches. There is currently no requirement that the pilot be evaluated on GPS/WAAS approaches on each proficiency check to allow them the option of utilizing these approaches.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: GPS instrument approach operations, outside the United States, must be authorized by

choices.text: the FAA-approved aircraft flight manual (AFM) or flight manual supplement.
a sovereign country or governmental unit.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 미국 밖에서 GPS instrument approach를 수행하려면 해당 국가의 주권 당국이 승인해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: GPS instrument approach operations outside the U.S. must be authorized by the appropriate sovereign authority. Answer (A) is incorrect. The aircraft flight manual or the supplement explains how to operate the GPS system installed in the airplane; it does not authorize that GPS be used for any type of GPS operation. Answer (C) is incorrect. GPS instrument approach operations inside, not outside, the U.S. must be authorized by the FAA Administrator.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Pilots are not authorized to fly a published RNAV or RNP procedure unless it is retrievable by the procedure name from

choices.text: the aircraft navigation database, or manually loaded with each individual waypoint in the correct sequence.
the aircraft navigation database, or manually loaded with each individual waypoint and verified by the pilot(s).

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 공표 RNAV/RNP 출발·도착·접근절차는 aircraft navigation database에서 절차명으로 불러올 수 있고 공표 절차와 일치할 때만 비행할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Pilots are not authorized to fly a published RNAV or RNP procedure (instrument approach, departure, or arrival procedure) unless it is retrievable by the procedure name from the aircraft navigation database and conforms to the charter procedure. Answer (A) is incorrect. Pilots may not fly a published RNAV or RNP procedure unless it is retrievable by the procedure name from the aircraft navigation database. Manually loading each waypoint in the correct sequence is not an acceptable substitute for the established method of retrieving the procedure. Answer (B) is incorrect. Pilots may not fly a published RNAV or RNP procedure unless it is retrievable by the procedure name from the aircraft navigation database. Manually loading each waypoint and verifying them is not an acceptable substitute for the established method of retrieving the procedure.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: When using GPS for navigation and instrument approaches, a required alternate airport must have

choices.text: an approved instrument approach procedure, besides GPS, that is expected to be operational and available at the ETA.
a GPS approach that is expected to be operational and available at the ETA.
authorization to fly approaches under IFR using GPS avionics.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. GPS를 항법·계기접근에 사용하는 경우 필요한 alternate에는 GPS 이외의 승인 계기접근절차가 ETA에 이용 가능해야 하며, 항공기도 그 절차를 비행할 장비를 갖춰야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: When using GPS for navigation and instrument approaches, any required alternate airport must have an approved instrument approach procedure, other than GPS, that is expected to be operational and available at the ETA and that the airplane is equipped to fly. Answer (B) is incorrect. When using GPS for navigation and instrument approaches, any required alternate must have an approved instrument approach procedure, other than a GPS approach, that is expected to be operational and available at the ETA. Answer (C) is incorrect. When using GPS for navigation and instrument approaches, any required alternate airport must have an approved instrument approach procedure, other than GPS, that is expected to be operational and available at the ETA. The alternate airport is not required to have an approved GPS approach.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 251 on page 427.) You are cleared to HNL and plan to use the RNAV (RNP) RWY 26L approach. Assuming you have received the training, you

choices.text: should be prepared to program the FMS/GPS with the radio frequency to fly this approach.
can use the GPS and radio frequency communications to fly this approach to minimums.
know your FMS/GPS must have GPS and radius-to-fix capability.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. RNP 접근의 중요한 장점은 정밀하게 정의된 공역 안에서 곡선 track을 비행하는 능력이다. RF segment가 있는 절차에서는 FMS/GPS가 GPS 신호를 받고 RF leg를 비행할 수 있어야 하며 차트에 'RF and GPS REQUIRED'로 표시된다.
questions.explanation_en: A key component necessary to realize the benefits of RNP approaches is the ability to fly curved flight tracks within a precisely defined airspace area. Accordingly, RNP approach procedures require the FMS/GPS to have the capability to receive GPS signals and to fly radius-to-fix (RF) segments. This is indicated by the statement “RF and GPS REQUIRED” in the notes section of the approach chart. Answer (A) is incorrect. GNSS Landing System (GLS) approaches such as those using the Local Area Augmentation System (LAAS), not RNAV (RNP) approaches, require the pilot to select a five-digit channel number associated with the approach. RNAV (RNP) approaches use standard GPS signals and do not require tuning a specific radio frequency or channel. Answer (B) is incorrect. Precision Approach Radar (PAR) and ILS with Precision Runway Monitoring (ILS-PRM) approaches, not RNAV (RNP) approaches, require the use of radio communications. RNAV (RNP) approaches use standard GPS signals and do not require tuning a specific communication frequency other than the frequency assigned by ATC.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: If Receiver Autonomous Integrity Monitoring (RAIM) is not available prior to beginning a GPS approach, the pilot should

choices.text: continue to the MAP and hold until the satellites are recaptured.
continue the approach, expecting to recapture the satellites before reaching the IAF.
use a navigation or approach system other than GPS for an approach.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. GPS 접근 준비 중 RAIM을 사용할 수 없으면 ATC에 알리고 다른 항행시설을 사용하는 다른 종류의 접근을 선택해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: If RAIM is not available when setting up for a GPS approach, you should inform ATC and select another type of approach using another type of navigation aid. Answer (A) is incorrect. If a RAIM failure occurs prior to the final approach waypoint (FAWP), not when setting up for a GPS approach, proceed to the missed approach waypoint via the FAWP, perform the missed approach, and contact ATC as soon as possible, not hold until satellites are recaptured. Answer (B) is incorrect. If RAIM is not available when setting up for a GPS approach, advise ATC and select another type of approach using another type of navigation aid, not proceed to the IAF and hold until satellite reception is satisfactory.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: A GPS missed approach requires that the pilot take action to sequence the receiver
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. GPS missed approach에서는 MAWP를 지난 뒤 receiver가 missed approach portion으로 sequence되도록 조종사가 필요한 조작을 해야 한다. 탑재 GPS의 활성화 절차를 정확히 알고 있어야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: A GPS missed approach requires that you take action to sequence the receiver past the missed approach waypoint (MAWP) to the missed approach portion of the procedure. You must be thoroughly familiar with the activation procedure for the particular GPS receiver installed in the airplane and must initiate appropriate action after the MAWP. Answer (A) is incorrect. A GPS missed approach requires that you take action to sequence the receiver after, not over, the MAWP. Answer (C) is incorrect. Activating the missed approach prior to the MAWP will cause the CDI sensitivity to change to terminal (±1 NM) immediately, and the receiver will continue to navigate to the MAWP but not sequence past the MAWP. Thus, you should sequence the receiver after, not prior to, the MAWP.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: If the missed approach is not activated, the GPS receiver will display

choices.text: an extension of the outbound final approach course, and the ATD will increase from the MAWP.
an extension of the outbound final approach course.
an extension of the inbound final approach course.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Missed approach를 활성화하지 않으면 GPS는 inbound final approach course의 연장선을 계속 표시하고, MAWP 이후 수동 sequence할 때까지 ATD가 증가한다.
questions.explanation_en: If the missed approach is not activated, the GPS receiver will display an extension of the inbound final approach course, and the along track distance (ATD) will increase from the MAWP until it is manually sequenced after crossing the MAWP. Answer (A) is incorrect. If the missed approach is not activated, the GPS receiver will display an extension of the inbound, not outbound, final approach course, and the ATD will increase from the MAWP. Answer (B) is incorrect. If the missed approach is not activated, the GPS receiver will display an extension of the inbound, not outbound, final approach course, and the ATD will increase from the MAWP.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: If flying a published GPS departure,

choices.text: the data base will contain all of the transition or departures from all runways.
and if RAIM is available, manual intervention by the pilot should not be required.
the GPS receiver must be set to terminal course deviation indicator sensitivity.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 공표 IFR departure와 SID를 GPS로 비행하려면 receiver가 terminal CDI sensitivity(±1 NM)로 설정되어 있어야 하고 해당 항로가 database에 들어 있어야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: The GPS receiver must be set to terminal (±1 NM) CDI sensitivity, and the navigation routes must be contained in the database in order to fly published IFR charted departures and SIDs. Answer (A) is incorrect. The database may not contain all of the transitions or departures from all runways, and some GPS receivers do not contain SIDs in the database. Answer (B) is incorrect. Certain segments of a SID may require some manual intervention by the pilot, even if RAIM is available, especially when radar vectored to a course or required to intercept a specific course to a waypoint.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 252 on page 429.) In reviewing the RNAV (GPS) RWY 4 approach to LEW, you note the lack of a shaded fan from the 1.6 NM to RW04 point to the runway threshold. This indicates

choices.text: the visual segment below the MDA/DA is not clear of obstacles on a 34:1 slope.
you can descend on a 20:1 slope and remain clear of all obstacles.
the runway does not have a visual glideslope landing aid.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. U.S. Terminal Procedures legend의 작은 shaded fan은 MDA/DA 아래 visual segment가 34:1 slope 기준으로 장애물로부터 clear하다는 뜻이다. Shaded fan이 없으면 34:1 면이 clear하지 않음을 의미한다.
questions.explanation_en: In the legend at the front of a U.S. Terminal Procedures approach book, in the middle of the page, you will see a very small shaded area (a shaded fan) that indicates that the visual segment below MDA/DA is clear of obstacles on a 34:1 slope. If there is no shaded fan, this indicates a 34:1 slope is not clear of obstacles. For an example of this shaded area, refer to Fig. 251 on page 427. It is the small shaded area near the runway end in the profile view. Answer (B) is incorrect. A 20:1 slope would put obstacles very close to the glideslope and could be hazardous. Answer (C) is incorrect. A shaded fan would indicate that the visual segment below MDA/DA is clear of obstacles on a 34:1 slope, not that there is no visual glideslope landing aid.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Missed approach routing in which the first track is via a course rather than direct to the next waypoint requires

choices.text: that the GPS receiver be sequenced to the missed approach portion of the procedure.
manual intervention by the pilot, but will not be required, if RAIM is available.
additional action by the operator to set the course.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Missed approach의 첫 track이 다음 waypoint로 direct가 아니라 course를 따라가도록 되어 있으면 조종사가 course를 설정하는 추가 조작이 필요하다. 이 단계의 입력절차를 숙지하는 것이 매우 중요하다.
questions.explanation_en: Missed approach routings in which the first track is via a course rather than direct to the next waypoint require additional action by the pilot to set the course. Being familiar with all of the inputs required is especially critical during this phase of flight. Answer (A) is incorrect. Missed approach routings in which the first track is via a course rather than direct to the next waypoint requires that the pilot take additional action to set the course, not that the GPS receiver be sequenced to the missed approach portion of the procedure. Answer (B) is incorrect. Missed approach routings in which the first track is via a course rather than direct to a waypoint requires additional action by the pilot to set the course, even if RAIM is available.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Prior to conducting RNAV (GPS) approaches to localizer performance with vertical (LPV) guidance minimums, an air carrier pilot must

choices.text: not be prohibited by the FAA approved flight manual from conducting these approaches.
be authorized by operations specification to conduct those approaches.
have successfully flown an RNAV (GPS) approach during their last proficiency check.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Conventional NPA, RNAV, LNAV/VNAV 접근에서 VNAV 사용 권한은 운영자의 OpSpecs, AFM 또는 기타 FAA 승인문서에 정해진다. 탑재장비, redundancy, 장비 상태, 승무원 훈련 및 FAA 승인수준이 사용 가능 여부에 영향을 준다.
questions.explanation_en: Like any other authorization given to air carriers and Part 91 operators, the authorization to use VNAV on a conventional non-precision approach, RNAV approaches, or LNAV/VNAV approaches is found in that operator’s OpSpecs, Aircraft Flight Manual (AFM), or other FAA-approved documents. The type of equipment installed in the aircraft, the redundancy of that equipment and its operational status, the level of flight crew training, and the level of the operator’s FAA authorization are all factors that can affect a pilot’s ability to use VNAV information on an approach. Answer (A) is incorrect. The company’s OpSpecs, Flight Operations Manual (FOM), and the Aircraft Flight Manual (AFM) for the pilot’s aircraft would dictate the specific operational conditions and procedures by which this type of approach could be flown. Answer (C) is incorrect. Before an RNAV (GPS) approach can be done, authorization to do this approach must be given. This authorization is found in the OpSpecs, Aircraft Flight Manual (AFM), or other FAA-approved documents.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: When the use of RNAV equipment using GPS input is planned to be used for an instrument approach at a destination airport, any required alternate airport must have an available instrument approach procedure that does not

choices.text: require the use of GPS except when the RNAV system has an IRU input.
require the use of GPS except when dual, independent GPS receivers are installed.
require the use of GPS except when the RNAV system has a WAAS input.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 원칙적으로 required alternate에는 GPS가 필요하지 않은 계기접근절차가 있어야 한다. 다만 WAAS를 사용하는 RNAV system에는 예외가 적용된다.
questions.explanation_en: Any required alternate airport must have an available instrument approach procedure that does not require the use of GPS. The exception to that rule applies to RNAV systems using WAAS equipment. Answer (A) is incorrect. The restriction stipulates that the alternate airport must have an instrument approach procedure available that does not require GPS, unless the RNAV system utilizes WAAS equipment. There is no exception for RNAV systems with an IRU input. Answer (B) is incorrect. The restriction stipulates that the alternate airport must have an instrument approach procedure available that does not require GPS, unless the RNAV system utilizes WAAS equipment. Dual, independent GPS receivers that are not WAAS compliant would not meet the conditions for the exception.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 258 on page 431.) As you approach DEPEW on the RNAV (GPS) RWY 32 approach, your GPS changes from “armed” to “active,” and the CDI needle begins to show increasing deviation to the left with no increase in cross track. In this situation, you

choices.text: should immediately execute the missed approach.
know that the sensitivity of the CDI has increased.
would turn to the right to center the CDI needle.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. GPS receiver는 공항 reference point 30 NM 이내에서 approach armed 상태여야 한다. FAWP 2 NM 이내에서는 active approach mode로 전환되어 CDI sensitivity가 증가한다.
questions.explanation_en: The GPS receiver should always be approach armed within 30 NM from the airport reference point. Within 2 NM of the final approach waypoint, the unit will cycle to active approach mode, which increases the CDI sensitivity. Answer (A) is incorrect. This response is not merited at this time. Answer (C) is incorrect. Corrections should be minor at this point, and only subtle adjustments to meet the CDI sensitivity change are needed.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
