questions.question: At an indicated altitude of 1,000 feet with a temperature of 32°C, density altitude is
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Pressure altitude 1,000 ft와 온도 32°C를 E6B에 적용하면 density altitude는 약 3,400 ft이다.
questions.explanation_en: Density altitude is calculated using Celsius. In the pressure altitude scale, line up 32°C over 1,000 feet of pressure altitude. The density altitude arrow is pointing to about 3,400 feet. Answer (A) is incorrect. A density altitude of 1,400 feet would require a temperature of about 15°C. Answer (B) is incorrect. A density altitude of 2,400 feet would require a temperature of about 25°C.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the result when water vapor changes to the liquid state while being lifted in a thunderstorm?

choices.text: Latent heat is released to the atmosphere.
Latent heat is transformed into pure energy.
Latent heat is absorbed from the surrounding air by the water droplet.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 뇌우의 updraft에서 수증기가 응결하면 latent heat가 방출된다. 이 열은 포화 상승기류의 냉각을 일부 상쇄해 구름 내부 buoyancy를 증가시킨다.
questions.explanation_en: In a thunderstorm, the updrafts (lifting action) result in water vapor changing to liquid or condensation. Condensation releases latent heat to the atmosphere, which partially offsets cooling in the saturated updraft and increases buoyancy within the cloud. Answer (B) is incorrect. Latent heat cannot create pure energy. Latent heat is returned to the surrounding atmosphere. Answer (C) is incorrect. This is the process of latent heat of vaporization, which is changing liquid water to vapor.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What feature is normally associated with the cumulus stage of a thunderstorm?

choices.text: Beginning of rain at the surface.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 뇌우의 cumulus stage에서는 구름이 계속 발달하며 기류는 거의 전부 updraft이다.
questions.explanation_en: During the cumulus stage of a thunderstorm, the cumulus cloud is building, and there are continuous updrafts. Answer (A) is incorrect. The beginning of rain at a surface marks the beginning of the mature stage. Answer (B) is incorrect. Frequent lightning occurs after the downdrafts have developed, producing the static electricity that causes lightning.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Convective clouds which penetrate a stratus layer can produce which threat to instrument flight?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 약하게 안정한 층에 넓은 stratus가 있는 가운데 대류운이 그 층을 뚫고 뇌우로 발달할 수 있다. 이런 embedded thunderstorm은 외부에서 보이지 않아 IFR 비행에 특히 위험하다.
questions.explanation_en: A stratus layer may sometimes form in a mildly stable layer while convective clouds penetrate the layer and possibly form thunderstorms. These thunderstorms may be almost or entirely embedded in a massive stratus layer and pose an unseen threat to instrument flight. Answer (A) is incorrect. The formation of freezing rain is dependent on rain falling through colder air. Convective clouds that penetrate a stratus layer may or may not produce precipitation. Answer (B) is incorrect. Clear air turbulence is turbulence encountered in air where no clouds are present.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is indicated by the term “embedded thunderstorms”?

choices.text: Severe thunderstorms are embedded in a squall line.
Thunderstorms are predicted to develop in a stable air mass.
Thunderstorms are obscured by other types of clouds.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Embedded thunderstorm은 뇌우가 다른 구름이나 짙은 haze 속에 묻혀 육안으로 식별할 수 없는 상태를 말한다.
questions.explanation_en: The term “embedded thunderstorms” means that the thunderstorms are embedded in clouds or thick haze layers and cannot be seen. Answer (A) is incorrect. A squall line consists of severe thunderstorms, which can always be seen. Answer (B) is incorrect. Thunderstorms do not occur in stable air masses.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which weather phenomenon signals the beginning of the mature stage of a thunderstorm?

choices.text: The appearance of an anvil top.
The start of rain at the surface.
Growth rate of the cloud is at its maximum.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 뇌우의 mature stage는 지상에 비가 내리기 시작할 때 시작된다. 이는 downdraft가 구름 전체를 통과해 강수를 지면까지 운반할 만큼 발달했다는 뜻이다.
questions.explanation_en: The mature stage of a thunderstorm begins when rain begins falling at the surface. This means that downdrafts have developed sufficiently to carry water all the way through the thunderstorm. Answer (A) is incorrect. The appearance of an anvil top occurs during the dissipating stage. Answer (C) is incorrect. The growth rate of a thunderstorm is at its greatest during the cumulus stage.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Why are downdrafts in a mature thunderstorm hazardous?

choices.text: Downdrafts are kept cool by cold rain which tends to accelerate the downward velocity.
Downdrafts converge toward a central location under the storm after striking the surface.
Downdrafts become warmer than the surrounding air and reverse into an updraft before reaching the surface.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Mature stage의 downdraft에서는 차가운 비가 압축가열을 억제해 하강공기가 주변보다 차갑게 유지되므로 하강속도가 더욱 빨라져 2,500 fpm을 넘을 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: During the mature stage, cold rain in the downdraft slows compressional heating, and the downdraft remains colder than the surrounding air. Thus, its downward speed is accelerated and may exceed 2,500 fpm. Answer (B) is incorrect. After striking the ground, the downdrafts will move away from the storm’s center (not converge). Answer (C) is incorrect. Downdrafts remain colder, not warmer, than the surrounding air and accelerate downward, not reverse into an updraft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: During the life cycle of a thunderstorm, which stage is characterized predominately by downdrafts?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 뇌우의 생애는 cumulus, mature, dissipating 세 단계이다. Dissipating stage에서는 강수가 계속되면서 updraft가 사라지고 downdraft가 지배한다.
questions.explanation_en: Thunderstorms have three life cycles: cumulus, mature, and dissipating. In the dissipating stage, the storm is characterized by downdrafts as the storm rains itself out. Answer (A) is incorrect. The cumulus stage is the building stage characterized by updrafts. Answer (C) is incorrect. The mature stage has both updrafts and downdrafts, which create strong wind shears.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which type storms are most likely to produce funnel clouds or tornadoes?

choices.text: Cold front or squall line thunderstorms.
Storms associated with icing and supercooled water.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Funnel cloud나 tornado는 cold front 또는 squall line과 연관된 steady-state thunderstorm에서 잘 발생한다. 이런 뇌우의 mature-stage updraft는 air-mass thunderstorm보다 강하고 오래 지속될 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Funnel clouds or tornadoes normally form with steady-state thunderstorms associated with cold fronts or squall lines. The mature stage updrafts in a steady-state thunderstorm are stronger and last longer than those in air mass storms and may persist for several hours. Answer (A) is incorrect. Even though air mass thunderstorms may produce funnel clouds or tornadoes, they are most likely to occur with steady-state thunderstorms. Answer (C) is incorrect. All thunderstorms that have updrafts and carry water above the freezing level can produce icing and supercooled water. But thunderstorms associated with cold fronts and squall lines are most likely to produce funnel clouds or tornadoes.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is a difference between an air mass thunderstorm and a steady-state thunderstorm?

choices.text: Air mass thunderstorms produce precipitation which falls outside of the updraft.
Air mass thunderstorm downdrafts and precipitation retard and reverse the updrafts.
Steady-state thunderstorms are associated with local surface heating.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Air-mass thunderstorm에서는 강수가 updraft 안이나 바로 옆으로 떨어져 drag로 상승기류를 약화시키고 결국 downdraft로 바꾼다. Steady-state thunderstorm에서는 강수가 updraft 밖으로 떨어져 강한 상승기류가 계속 유지될 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The rain associated with an air mass thunderstorm falls through or immediately beside the updraft. Falling precipitation induces frictional drag, retards the updraft, and reverses it to a downdraft. During a steady-state thunderstorm, precipitation falls outside the updraft, allowing the updraft to continue unabated. Answer (A) is incorrect. Steady-state, not air mass, thunderstorms produce precipitation that falls outside the updraft. Answer (C) is incorrect. Air mass, not steady-state, thunderstorms are associated with local surface heating.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which type cloud is associated with violent turbulence and a tendency toward the production of funnel clouds?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Cumulonimbus mamma는 구름 밑면에 주머니·젖통 모양 돌기가 매달린 cumulonimbus로, 보통 severe turbulence를 시사하며 tornado를 만들 수도 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Cumulonimbus mamma is a cumulonimbus cloud having hanging protuberances like pouches or udders on the underside of the cloud, usually indicative of severe turbulence. This type of cloud can produce a tornado. Answer (B) is incorrect. Standing lenticular clouds mark mountain waves that are the product of stable air flowing over an obstruction. Answer (C) is incorrect. Stratocumulus clouds sometimes form from the breaking up of stratus or the spreading out of cumulus, and they are associated with some turbulence and possible icing at subfreezing levels.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Where do squall lines most often develop?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Squall line은 전선 자체가 아닌 좁은 active thunderstorm band로, 보통 습하고 불안정한 공기에서 cold front 앞쪽에 형성된다.
questions.explanation_en: A squall line is a nonfrontal, narrow band of active thunderstorms. Most often squall lines develop ahead of a cold front in moist, unstable air. Answer (A) is incorrect. Squall lines most often develop ahead of a cold front, not in an occluded front. Answer (C) is incorrect. Squall lines most often develop ahead of a cold front, not behind a stationary front.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Where can the maximum hazard zone caused by wind shear associated with a thunderstorm be found?

choices.text: In front of the thunderstorm cell (anvil side) and on the southwest side of the cell.
Ahead of the roll cloud or gust front and directly under the anvil cloud.
On all sides and directly under the thunderstorm cell.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 모든 뇌우에는 위험한 난류가 있다. 뇌우 wind shear의 최대 위험구역은 셀의 모든 방향과 바로 아래쪽이다.
questions.explanation_en: Hazardous turbulence is present in all thunderstorms. The maximum hazard zone caused by wind shear associated with a thunderstorm is found on all sides and directly under the thunderstorm cell. Answer (A) is incorrect. The wind shear associated with a thunderstorm is on all sides and directly under the cell, not just in the front and on the southwest side. Answer (B) is incorrect. The wind shear associated with a thunderstorm is on all sides and directly under the cell. A roll cloud is not present in all thunderstorms, and when present it marks the eddies of the shear zone between the plow wind and surrounding air.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Atmospheric pressure changes due to a thunderstorm will be at the lowest value

choices.text: during the downdraft and heavy rain showers.
immediately after the rain showers have stopped.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 뇌우 접근 시 기압은 빠르게 떨어지다가 첫 gust와 차가운 downdraft·강한 소나기가 도착하면 급상승하고, 뇌우가 지나가면 다시 정상으로 돌아간다.
questions.explanation_en: Pressure usually falls rapidly with the approach of a thunderstorm, then rises sharply with the onset of the first gust and arrival of the cold downdraft and heavy rain showers, falling back to normal as the storm moves on. Answer (A) is incorrect. During the downdraft and heavy rain showers, the pressure rises sharply. Answer (C) is incorrect. Immediately after the rain showers have stopped, the pressure will return to normal.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A clear area in a line of thunderstorm echoes on a radar scope indicates

choices.text: the absence of clouds in the area.
an area of no convective turbulence.
an area where precipitation drops are not detected.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Weather radar는 precipitation drop을 탐지한다. Radar scope에 깨끗한 구역이 보인다는 것은 강수입자가 탐지되지 않는다는 뜻이지 반드시 안전하다는 뜻은 아니다.
questions.explanation_en: Weather radar detects droplets of precipitation. If a radarscope displays a clear area, it indicates an area where no precipitation drops are detected. Answer (A) is incorrect. Weather radar detects only precipitation drops, not clouds. Answer (B) is incorrect. Convective turbulence, which would not be detected by radar, could be found under cumulus clouds. Radar does not detect turbulence.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When flying over the top of a severe thunderstorm, the cloud should be overflown by at least

choices.text: 500 feet above any moderate to severe turbulence layer.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Known 또는 suspected severe thunderstorm의 top은 구름 꼭대기 풍속 10 kt당 최소 1,000 ft 위로 통과해야 한다. 실제로는 이 고도가 항공기 성능한계를 넘을 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The top of a known or suspected severe thunderstorm should be cleared by at least 1,000 ft. of altitude for each 10 kt. of wind speed at the cloud top. In some severe thunderstorms, this clearance may exceed the altitude capability of most aircraft. Answer (B) is incorrect. The cloud should be overflown by at least 1,000 ft. for each 10 kt. wind speed, which would normally be greater than 2,500 ft. with a severe thunderstorm. Answer (C) is incorrect. The exact location of a turbulence layer will not usually be known.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Intense radar storm echos should be avoided by a margin of
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 가장 강한 radar echo는 severe thunderstorm일 가능성이 높다. Hail은 구름에서 수 NM 떨어져 내릴 수 있고 위험 난류는 최대 20 NM까지 확장될 수 있으므로 가장 강한 echo에서 최소 20 NM 떨어져 우회해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: The most intense echos are severe thunderstorms. Remember that hail may fall several miles from the cloud, and hazardous turbulence may extend as much as 20 NM from the cloud. Avoid the most intense echos by at least 20 NM. Answer (A) is incorrect. Avoid the most intense echos by at least 20 NM. Echos should be separated by 40 NM before flying between them. Answer (B) is incorrect. Avoid the most intense echos by at least 20 NM, though 25 NM would be a good “personal safety” item.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Downdrafts in thunderstorms can be expected to exceed
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Downdraft의 발달은 뇌우 mature stage의 신호이다. 차가운 비가 압축가열을 억제하므로 downdraft가 주변보다 차갑고 무거워져 2,500 fpm을 넘을 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The downdraft signals the mature stage of a thunderstorm. Cold rain in the downdraft retards compressional heating, and the downdraft remains cooler than surrounding air. Therefore, its downward speed is accelerated and may exceed 2,500 feet per minute. Answer (B) is incorrect. Thunderstorm downdrafts can be expected to exceed 2,500 feet per minute, not 3,500 feet per minute. Answer (C) is incorrect. Thunderstorm downdrafts can be expected to exceed 2,500 feet per minute, not 4,500 feet per minute.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Updrafts in the mature stage of a thunderstorm can exceed
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 서로 가까운 강한 updraft와 downdraft는 큰 vertical shear와 심한 난류를 만든다. Updraft는 6,000 fpm을 넘을 수도 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Updrafts and downdrafts in close proximity create strong vertical shear and a very turbulent environment. Updrafts reach a maximum with speeds possibly exceeding 6,000 feet per minute. Answer (A) is incorrect. Updrafts can reach speeds possibly exceeding 6,000 feet per minute, not 8,000 feet per minute. Answer (B) is incorrect. Updrafts can reach speeds possibly exceeding 6,000 feet per minute, not 7,000 feet per minute.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Steady-state thunderstorms are usually associated with
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Front, 수렴하는 바람, upper trough 같은 기상계가 강제 상승을 만들면 steady-state thunderstorm이 발달하며 종종 squall line으로 조직된다.
questions.explanation_en: Weather systems such as fronts, converging winds, and troughs aloft force upward motion spawning these storms that often form into squall lines. Steady-state thunderstorms usually are associated with weather systems. Answer (B) is incorrect. Afternoon heating intensifies the already active steady-state thunderstorm. Answer (C) is incorrect. In a steady-state thunderstorm, precipitation falls outside the updraft; therefore the mature stage updrafts become stronger and last much longer than air mass storms.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: All ATC facilities using radar weather processors with the ability to determine precipitation intensity will describe the intensity as

choices.text: light, moderate, heavy, intense, extreme, severe.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 강수강도를 판별할 수 있는 radar weather processor를 사용하는 ATC 시설은 강수강도를 light, moderate, heavy, extreme으로 조종사에게 설명한다.
questions.explanation_en: All ATC facilities using radar weather processors with the ability to determine precipitation intensity will describe the intensity to pilots as light, moderate, heavy, or extreme. Answer (A) is incorrect. The words “intense” or “severe” are not used by ATC facilities using radar weather processors with the ability to determine precipitation intensity. Answer (C) is incorrect. The word “severe” is not used by ATC facilities using radar weather processors with the ability to determine precipitation intensity.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Shear turbulence may be expected

choices.text: usually within 20 miles of a severe thunderstorm.
no more than 10 miles from a severe thunderstorm.
probably not more than 15 miles from a severe thunderstorm.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Severe thunderstorm 바깥에서도 구름 위 수천 ft 및 옆으로 약 20 NM까지 shear turbulence가 관측될 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Outside of the cloud, shear turbulence has been encountered several thousand feet above and 20 miles laterally from a severe storm. Answer (B) is incorrect. Shear turbulence has been encountered 20 miles laterally from a severe storm. Answer (C) is incorrect. Shear turbulence has been encountered 20 miles laterally from a severe storm.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Storm gust fronts often move as much as

choices.text: 10 miles ahead of the associated precipitation.
15 miles ahead of the associated precipitation.
20 miles ahead of the associated precipitation.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Gust front는 강수구역보다 최대 약 15 NM 앞서 이동할 수 있으며 접근하는 뇌우 전방의 지상풍을 매우 빠르고 크게 변화시킬 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Gust fronts often move far ahead (up to 15 miles) of associated precipitation. The gust front causes a rapid and sometimes drastic change in surface wind ahead of an approaching storm. Answer (A) is incorrect. Gust fronts often move up to 15 miles, not 10 miles, ahead of associated precipitation. Answer (C) is incorrect. Gust fronts often move up to 15 miles, not 20 miles, ahead of associated precipitation.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A thunderstorm first begins when

choices.text: lifting forces carry cooler air inward and upward.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Cumulus stage는 뇌우 생애의 시작으로 핵심은 updraft이다. 상승기류가 공기를 안쪽·위쪽으로 끌어올리며 구름 성장률이 3,000 fpm을 넘을 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The cumulus stage is the beginning of the life cycle of a thunderstorm. The key feature of this stage is the updraft. This updraft carries cooler air inward and upward. Growth rate of this stage may exceed 3,000 feet per minute. Answer (B) is incorrect. Rain begins at the second or mature stage of the life cycle of a thunderstorm, not the cumulus stage. Answer (C) is incorrect. The cumulus stage of a thunderstorm carries cooler air inward and upward. It is not a high temperature cycle.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Downdrafts in a thunderstorm may exceed
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Downdraft 2,500 fpm을 속도로 환산하면 시간당 150,000 ft이고 1 NM≈6,076 ft이므로 약 24.7 kt이다.
questions.explanation_en: Downdrafts can exceed 2,500 feet per minute (fpm). We convert that to knots by multiplying ● 2,500 fpm × 60 minutes = 150,000 feet per hour ● 1 nautical mile = 6,076 feet ● 150,000 feet per hour ÷ 6,076 feet = 24.69 knots Answer (A) is incorrect. The speed of 34 knots would require a downdraft of about 3,500 feet per minute. Answer (C) is incorrect. The speed of 14 knots would require a downdraft of only about 1,500 feet per minute.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Airborne weather radar is installed to help the crew
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Airborne weather radar는 항공기에 탑재되어 severe weather의 위치를 찾고 회피하는 데 사용한다.
questions.explanation_en: Airborne radar is equipment carried by aircraft to locate and avoid severe weather. Answer (A) is incorrect. Radar should not be used to penetrate storm cells. Instead, it should be used to locate and avoid dangerous weather. Answer (C) is incorrect. Radar shows the location and intensity of precipitation, but it does not directly detect turbulence.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Freezing rain encountered during climb is normally evidence that

choices.text: a climb can be made to a higher altitude without encountering more than light icing.
a layer of warmer air exists above.
ice pellets at higher altitudes have changed to rain in the warmer air below.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Freezing rain은 비가 더 차가운 공기층을 통과하며 supercooled된 뒤 충돌 시 얼어붙는 현상이다. 이를 만나면 상층에 0°C보다 따뜻한 공기층이 있음을 의미한다.
questions.explanation_en: Freezing rain is rain that falls through colder air and becomes supercooled, freezing on impact. If encountered, it means that there is a layer of warmer air above. Answer (A) is incorrect. Freezing rain means only that a layer of warmer air exists above. It does not indicate the amount of icing that may be encountered during a climb. Answer (C) is incorrect. Freezing rain is formed by rain falling through colder air, not from ice pellets melting through warmer air.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What condition is indicated when ice pellets are encountered during flight?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Ice pellet은 상층에서 freezing rain 조건이 있음을 나타낸다. 비가 하강하면서 얼어 얼음알갱이가 되기 때문이다.
questions.explanation_en: Ice pellets always indicate freezing rain at higher altitudes. Ice pellets are formed when rain freezes during descent. Answer (A) is incorrect. Ice pellets always indicate freezing rain, not thunderstorms, at higher altitudes. Answer (C) is incorrect. Freezing rain, not snow, is indicated at higher altitudes when ice pellets are encountered.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What temperature condition is indicated if precipitation in the form of wet snow occurs during flight?

choices.text: The temperature is above freezing at flight altitude.
The temperature is above freezing at higher altitudes.
There is an inversion with colder air below.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 내리던 눈이 더 따뜻한 공기층에서 녹을 수 있다. Wet snow를 만났다면 비행고도 기온이 0°C보다 높다는 의미이다.
questions.explanation_en: Falling snow may melt in warmer layers of air. When wet snow is encountered, it indicates that the temperature is above freezing at flight altitude. Answer (B) is incorrect. Wet snow indicates above-freezing temperature at flight level, not at higher altitudes. The temperature was below freezing at the altitudes where the snow formed. Answer (C) is incorrect. Wet snow indicates falling snow that has begun to melt due to above-freezing temperature at flight level. An inversion may or may not be the cause of the warmer air.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which conditions result in the formation of frost?

choices.text: The temperature of the collecting surface is at or below freezing and small droplets of moisture are falling.
Dew collects on the surface and then freezes because the surface temperature is lower than the air temperature.
Temperature of the collecting surface is below the dewpoint and the dewpoint is also below freezing.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Frost는 표면온도가 dew point보다 낮고 dew point 자체도 0°C 미만일 때 수증기가 바로 얼음결정으로 deposition되며 형성된다.
questions.explanation_en: Frost forms when both the temperature of the collecting surface is below the dew point and the dew point is also below freezing. Frost is the deposition of water vapor to ice crystals. Answer (A) is incorrect. Moisture that falls on a collecting surface that is at or below freezing will form ice. Answer (B) is incorrect. Frozen dew is hard and transparent, while frost is the deposition from vapor to ice and is white and opaque.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When will frost most likely form on aircraft surfaces?

choices.text: On clear nights with stable air and light winds.
On overcast nights with freezing drizzle precipitation.
On clear nights with convective action and a small temperature/dewpoint spread.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Frost는 맑고 안정하며 바람이 약한 밤에 항공기 표면에 가장 잘 형성된다. 다른 면에서는 비행하기 좋아 보이는 날씨여서 특히 주의가 필요하다.
questions.explanation_en: Frost will most likely form on aircraft surfaces on clear nights with stable air and light winds. These are conditions that in all other respects make weather ideal for flying. Answer (B) is incorrect. Freezing drizzle would produce ice, not frost, on the aircraft surfaces. Answer (C) is incorrect. Stable air is required. Convective action requires unstable conditions.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which type precipitation is an indication that supercooled water is present?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 비가 더 찬 공기층을 통과하면 supercooled되어 충돌 시 freezing rain으로 얼 수 있다. Supercooled water는 0°C 미만이지만 액체 상태인 물이다.
questions.explanation_en: Rain falling through colder air may become supercooled, freezing on impact as freezing rain. Supercooled water is liquid water that is colder than 0°C, and its impact on an object induces freezing. Answer (A) is incorrect. Wet snow is an indication that temperature is above freezing at present level. Answer (C) is incorrect. Ice pellets indicate that water has frozen, not become/ remained supercooled.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is a feature of supercooled water?

choices.text: The water drop deposits to an ice particle upon impact.
The unstable water drop freezes upon striking an exposed object.
The temperature of the water drop remains at 0°C until it impacts a part of the airframe, then clear ice accumulates.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 0°C보다 낮은 물방울은 supercooled droplet이다. 이런 물방울이 항공기 표면에 충돌하면 얼어 aircraft icing을 만든다.
questions.explanation_en: Water droplets that are colder than 0°C are considered supercooled. When they strike an exposed object, they freeze on impact. Aircraft icing results if supercooled water strikes an airplane. Answer (A) is incorrect. Deposition is the process of changing water vapor to ice crystals, not liquid water to ice (the latter is freezing). Answer (C) is incorrect. Supercooled water temperature is below, not at, 0°C.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The following weather condition may be conducive to severe in-flight icing:

choices.text: visible rain at temperatures below 0°C ambient air temperature.
visible moisture at temperatures below 5°C ambient temperature.
visible rain at temperatures below 10°C ambient temperature.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 주변기온이 0°C 이하인데 visible rain이 있다면 severe in-flight icing에 매우 유리한 조건이다.
questions.explanation_en: Visible rain at ambient temperatures below 0°C (32°F) indicates a condition that is conducive to severe in-flight icing. Answer (B) is incorrect. Visible moisture at ambient temperatures below 5°C (41°F) does not necessarily indicate a condition that is conducive to severe in-flight icing. Answer (C) is incorrect. Visible rain at ambient temperatures below 10°C (50°F) does not necessarily indicate a condition that is conducive to severe in-flight icing.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What condition is necessary for the formation of structural icing in flight?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 비행 중 structural icing에는 두 조건이 필요하다. 항공기가 비·구름방울 같은 visible moisture 안에 있어야 하고, 수분이 항공기에 닿는 지점의 온도가 0°C 이하이어야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Two conditions are necessary for structural icing in flight: (1) The aircraft must be flying through visible water, such as rain or cloud droplets, and (2) the temperature at the point where the moisture strikes the aircraft must be 0°C or colder. Answer (A) is incorrect. Supercooled water drops increase the rate of icing but are not a condition necessary for the formation of structural icing. Answer (B) is incorrect. Water must be visible, not in a gaseous (vapor) state.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which type of icing is associated with the smallest size of water droplet similar to that found in low-level stratus clouds?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Rime ice는 저층 stratus처럼 작은 물방울이 있을 때 잘 생긴다. 불규칙하고 거친 형상 때문에 airfoil의 공력효율을 크게 떨어뜨린다.
questions.explanation_en: Rime ice forms when drops are small, such as those found in low-level stratus clouds. Its irregular shape makes it very effective in decreasing aerodynamic efficiency of airfoils. Answer (A) is incorrect. Clear ice forms when drops are large, not small, as found in rain or cumuliform clouds. Answer (B) is incorrect. Frost is not a structural icing condition found in flight; it occurs to airplanes parked on the ground.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The following weather may be conducive to severe inflight icing

choices.text: droplets that splash or splatter on impact at temperatures below 0°C ambient temperature.
drops that impact at temperatures below -20°C ambient air temperature.
droplets that splash or splatter on impact at temperatures below 10°C and above 1°C ambient temperature.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 0°C 이하에서 물방울이 충돌하며 splash/splatter하는 조건에서는 severe icing이 가능하다.
questions.explanation_en: When water droplets splash or splatter on impact at temperatures at or below 0°C, severe icing is possible. Answer (B) is incorrect. At temperatures below -20°C precipitation is typically ice, not liquid that could freeze onto the airframe. Answer (C) is incorrect. The temperature range specified in this answer option is above freezing. Severe icing is not likely in temperatures that are consistently above freezing.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The following weather may be conducive to severe inflight icing
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Visible rain이 있고 static air temperature가 0°C 이하이면 severe icing 가능성에 특히 경계해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Pilots should be especially alert to for severe icing when there is visible rain and the static air temperature is 0°C or colder. Answer (A) is incorrect. Although visible moisture can cause icing, the weather that is most conducive to severe inflight icing includes visible rain and a static air temperature of 0°C or colder. Answer (C) is incorrect. While visible rain is a factor in the formation of severe inflight icing, the most conducive static air temperature is 0°C or colder, not 10°C.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What happens to residual ice that remains after deice boots are inflated and shed ice?

choices.text: Residual ice increases with a decrease in airspeed or temperature.
Residual ice remains the same until the aircraft exits icing conditions.
Residual ice decreases with a decrease in airspeed or temperature.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. FAA는 icing의 첫 징후에서 deicing system을 작동하도록 권고한다. Pneumatic boot는 cycle 사이에 residual ice가 남을 수 있고, 낮은 속도·낮은 온도에서는 축적이 쉬워 여러 번 cycle이 필요할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The FAA recommends that the deicing system be activated at the first indication of icing. Because some residual ice continues to adhere between pneumatic boot system cycles, the wing is never entirely “clean.” The amount of residual ice increases as airspeed and/or temperature decrease due to the more favorable conditions for ice accumulation associated with these conditions. At airspeeds typical of small airplanes, it may take many boot cycles to effectively shed the ice. Answer (B) is incorrect. Residual ice left behind between deicing system cycles will increase in magnitude if either airspeed or temperature decrease due to the more favorable conditions for ice accumulation associated with these conditions. Answer (C) is incorrect. The amount of residual ice increases, not decreases, as airspeed and/or temperature decrease due to the more favorable conditions for ice accumulation associated with these conditions.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: If you detect icing accumulation in flight, especially if the aircraft is not equipped with a deicing system, you should

choices.text: leave the area of precipitation, if able, or fly to an altitude where the temperature is above freezing.
fly to an area with liquid precipitation.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 항공기의 anti-ice/deice 능력과 관계없이 첫 조치는 visible moisture 구역을 벗어나는 것이다. 구름 아래로 강하, top 위로 상승, course 변경이 가능하며, 불가능하면 0°C보다 따뜻한 고도로 이동해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Regardless of the level of anti-ice or deice protection offered by the aircraft, the first course of action should be to leave the area of visible moisture. This might mean descending to an altitude below the cloud bases, climbing to an altitude that is above the cloud tops, or turning to a different course. If this is not possible, then the pilot must move to an altitude where the temperature is above freezing. Answer (A) is incorrect. The best action is to leave the area of precipitation, but, if that is not possible, the pilot should move to an altitude where the temperature is above freezing. Only during a temperature inversion would that be a higher altitude; usually it means descending to a lower altitude. Answer (C) is incorrect. Areas of liquid precipitation do not necessarily equate to areas where the temperature is above freezing. Freezing rain is an excellent example of liquid precipitation that is incredibly hazardous.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When conditions favoring the formation of ice are present, pilots should check for ice accumulation prior to flight. The best way to do this is by

choices.text: using a flashlight and watching for light reflection.
running your hand along all control surfaces.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 특히 clear ice는 표면에서 발견하기 어려우므로 flashlight를 항공기 표면에 비춰 반사를 확인하면 얼음 존재를 찾는 데 도움이 된다.
questions.explanation_en: Because ice, particularly clear ice, is difficult to detect on the aircraft’s surface, you can shine a flashlight along all visible surfaces of the aircraft and watch for light reflections. This would be an indication of ice on the aircraft’s surface. Answer (B) is incorrect. Physically inspecting the control surfaces is a good tactic, but you should not limit your scan merely to the aircraft’s control surfaces as the skin can and will collect ice as well. Additionally, T-tail designs may make a physical inspection of the related control surfaces difficult. Answer (C) is incorrect. Ice detection lights are useful for checking for ice accumulation at night, but they are used during flight, not during the preflight inspection.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: In an aircraft equipped with a pneumatic deicing system, the appropriate technique for removing ice is to

choices.text: operate the pneumatic deicing system several times.
operate the pneumatic deicing system once.
confirm that ice has accumulated prior to engaging the pneumatic boots.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 축적된 얼음과 cycle 사이 residual ice를 제거하려면 pneumatic deicing system을 여러 번 작동해야 할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: To clear accumulated ice as well as residual ice that may be left between cycles, you should operate a pneumatic deicing system several times. Answer (B) is incorrect. To clear accumulated ice as well as residual ice that may be left between cycles, you should operate a pneumatic deicing system several times, not just once. Answer (C) is incorrect. While this technique was formerly accepted as a rule of thumb, current advisory guidance recommends that deicing systems be activated at the first indication of icing rather than after any significant amount has accumulated.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Clear ice generally forms in outside temperature ranges of
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Clear ice는 일반적으로 외기온 0°C~-10°C 범위에서 잘 형성된다.
questions.explanation_en: Clear ice generally forms when outside temperatures range from 0°C to -10°C. Answer (A) is incorrect. The outside temperature range that is most conducive to clear ice formation is 0°C to -10°C, not colder than -25°C. Answer (B) is incorrect. The outside temperature range that is most conducive to clear ice formation is 0°C to -10°C, not -15° to -25°C.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Freezing drizzle often forms by the
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Freezing drizzle은 주로 collision-coalescence 과정으로 형성된다. 큰 물방울이 낙하하며 작은 물방울과 충돌·합쳐져 더 큰 supercooled drizzle drop으로 성장하며, 이런 큰 물방울은 보통 구름 상부에 많다.
questions.explanation_en: Freezing drizzle is more commonly formed by a process known as the collision-coalescence process. Some droplets in a cloud grow to approximately 30 micrometers in diameter. Then they begin to settle and fall fast enough so that they collide with some smaller droplets. If the droplets coalesce, the result is a larger droplet, which now has an even better chance of capturing smaller droplets. This process can produce drizzle-size drops in a supercooled cloud, usually near the top, where the larger droplets generally are found in any cloud. Answer (B) is incorrect. Freezing drizzle is more commonly formed by a process known as the collision-coalescence process. Answer (C) is incorrect. Freezing drizzle is more commonly formed by a process known as the collision-coalescence process.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: On initial climbout after takeoff with the autopilot engaged, you encounter icing conditions. In this situation you can expect

choices.text: ice to accumulate on the underside of the wings due to the higher AOA.
the autopilot to hold the vertical speed, only if the anti-icing boots are working.
increased airflow under the wings to prevent the accumulation of ice.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Icing 조건의 initial climb에서는 낮은 속도로 인해 AOA가 커지는 경우가 많아 항공기와 날개 아랫면이 icing에 더 노출되고, cruise보다 더 뒤쪽까지 얼음이 축적될 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Airplanes are vulnerable to ice accumulation during the initial climbout in icing conditions because lower speeds often translate into a higher Angle of Attack (AOA). This exposes the underside of the airplane and its wings to the icing conditions and allows ice to accumulate further aft than it would in cruise flight. Answer (B) is incorrect. The autopilot will hold the vertical speed if the anti-icing boots are working or not. Therefore, extreme vigilance should be exercised while climbing with the autopilot engaged. Climbing in Vertical Speed (VS) mode in icing conditions is highly discouraged. Answer (C) is incorrect. Lower speeds and a higher AOA will expose the underside of the airplane and its wings to the icing conditions and allows the accumulation of ice; it does not prevent the accumulation of ice.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is a characteristic of the troposphere?

choices.text: It contains all the moisture of the atmosphere.
There is an overall decrease of temperature with an increase of altitude.
The average altitude of the top of the troposphere is about 6 miles.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Troposphere는 지표에서 평균 약 7 mi까지의 층이며, 일반적으로 고도가 증가할수록 기온이 감소한다.
questions.explanation_en: The troposphere is the layer from the surface to an average altitude of 7 mi. It is characterized by an overall decrease of temperature with an increase in altitude. Answer (A) is incorrect. Moisture can be found in the stratosphere, as evidenced by some of the largest thunderstorms. Answer (C) is incorrect. The average altitude of the top of the troposphere is about 7 mi., not 6 mi.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Where is the normal location of the jetstream relative to surface lows and fronts?

choices.text: The jetstream is located north of the surface systems.
The jetstream is located south of the low and warm front.
The jetstream is located over the low and crosses both the warm front and the cold front.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 강하고 긴 경로의 jet stream은 보통 상층 trough/low 아래의 발달한 지상저기압과 전선계와 연관된다. 지상저기압은 처음 jet stream 남쪽에서 발달해 깊어질수록 jet 쪽으로 접근하고, occlusion이 진행되면 저기압은 jet 북쪽으로 이동하며 jet은 occlusion point 부근에서 전선계를 가로지른다.
questions.explanation_en: Strong, long-trajectory jet streams usually are associated with well-developed surface lows and frontal systems beneath upper troughs or lows. The jet stream is to the north as a surface low develops, and the low moves nearer the jet stream as the low deepens. The occluding low moves north of the jet stream, and the jet stream crosses the frontal system near the point of occlusion. Answer (B) is incorrect. The jet stream is located to the north, not south, of the low and warm front. Answer (C) is incorrect. The jet stream crosses the occlusion of the warm and the cold fronts at the point of occlusion.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which feature is associated with the tropopause?

choices.text: Absolute upper limit of cloud formation.
Abrupt change of temperature lapse rate.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Tropopause에서는 temperature lapse rate가 급격히 변한다. 열대 tropopause 위에서는 고도와 함께 기온이 상승하고, 극지 tropopause 위에서는 기온이 거의 일정하게 유지된다.
questions.explanation_en: The tropopause is characterized by an abrupt change in temperature lapse rate. The temperature above the tropical tropopause increases with height, and the temperature above the polar tropopause remains about constant with height. Answer (A) is incorrect. The jet stream (wind) and clear air turbulence are found extensively in the tropopause. Answer (B) is incorrect. Clouds can be present into the stratosphere, as in very large thunderstorms and cirrus clouds made up of ice crystals.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What weather feature occurs at altitude levels near the tropopause?

choices.text: Maximum winds and narrow wind shear zones.
Abrupt temperature increase above the tropopause.
Thin layers of cirrus (ice crystal) clouds at the tropopause level.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Tropopause 부근에서는 기온과 바람 변화가 크고 최대풍이 자주 나타난다. 이 강한 풍속차가 좁은 wind shear 구역을 만들어 위험한 turbulence를 발생시킬 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Temperature and wind vary greatly in the vicinity of the tropopause. Maximum winds generally occur near the tropopause. These winds create narrow zones of wind shear, which often generate hazardous turbulence. Answer (B) is incorrect. Abrupt temperature increase does not occur above the tropopause. Answer (C) is incorrect. Thin layers of cirrus (ice crystal) clouds can develop at altitudes below the tropopause level and extend into the lower stratosphere.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Where do the maximum winds associated with the jetstream usually occur?

choices.text: In the vicinity of breaks in the tropopause on the polar side of the jet core.
Below the jet core where a long straight stretch of the jetstream is located.
On the equatorial side of the jetstream where moisture has formed cirriform clouds.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Jet stream의 최대풍은 tropical tropopause와 polar tropopause 사이의 break 부근에서 나타나며, 강한 temperature gradient 때문에 jet core의 polar side에서 가장 강하다.
questions.explanation_en: Maximum winds associated with the jet stream occur in the vicinity of breaks between the tropical and polar tropopause. Maximum wind speed in the jet stream is found in the core on the polar side due to very strong temperature gradients. Answer (B) is incorrect. In the jet stream, the maximum winds are found in, not below, the core. Answer (C) is incorrect. When moisture is available, cirriform clouds will form on the upward motion of air of the jet stream on the equatorial side. This will occur in the slower winds of the jet stream.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Where are jetstreams normally located?

choices.text: In areas of strong low pressure systems in the stratosphere.
In a break in the tropopause where intensified temperature gradients are located.
In a single continuous band, encircling the Earth, where there is a break between the equatorial and polar tropopause.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Jet stream은 지구를 파동 형태로 둘러 흐르는 좁고 얕은 최대풍속대이다. 보통 temperature gradient가 강한 tropopause break 부근에 형성된다.
questions.explanation_en: The jet stream is a narrow, shallow, meandering river of maximum winds extending around the Earth in a wavelike pattern. The jet stream typically occurs in a break in the tropopause in an area of intensified temperature gradients characteristic of the break. Answer (A) is incorrect. A jet stream is located in a break in the tropopause, not in the stratosphere. Answer (C) is incorrect. There may be more than one jet stream at any time; up to three at one time are not uncommon.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A jet stream is a riverlike flow of high-altitude wind following the planetary atmospheric wave patterns with speeds of
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Jet stream으로 분류되려면 집중된 최대풍속이 최소 50 kt 이상이어야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: To be classified as a jet stream, the concentrated winds must be 50 knots or greater. Answer (B) is incorrect. The jet stream is classified as a riverlike flow of high-altitude wind with concentrated winds at a minimum of 50 knots, not 71 knots. Answer (C) is incorrect. The jet stream is classified as a riverlike flow of high-altitude wind with concentrated winds at a minimum of 50 knots, not 100 knots.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Clear air turbulence associated with a jet stream is

choices.text: similar to that associated with a tropical maritime front.
most commonly found in temperatures between -40° and -50°C.
most commonly found in the vicinity of the tropopause.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Jet stream과 관련된 CAT는 troposphere와 stratosphere 경계인 tropopause 부근에서 가장 흔하다.
questions.explanation_en: Clear air turbulence (CAT) associated with a jet stream is most often found in the vicinity of the tropopause, which is the boundary layer between the troposphere and the stratosphere. Answer (A) is incorrect. CAT associated with the jet stream is not most commonly associated with a tropical maritime front. Rather, it is most often found in the vicinity of the tropopause, which is the boundary between the troposphere and the stratosphere. Answer (B) is incorrect. Temperature is not a primary factor that affects CAT. However, CAT that occurs in the jet stream is often associated with proximity to the tropopause.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which type frontal system is normally crossed by the jetstream?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 지상저기압은 보통 jet stream 남쪽에서 발달해 깊어질수록 jet에 가까워지고, occlusion이 진행되면 jet 북쪽으로 이동하며 jet은 occlusion point 부근에서 전선계를 횡단한다.
questions.explanation_en: The development of a surface low usually is south of the jet stream and moves nearer as the low deepens. The occluding low moves north of the jet stream, and the jet stream crosses the frontal system near the point of occlusion. Answer (A) is incorrect. The jet stream crosses an occluded front, not both warm and cold fronts. Answer (B) is incorrect. The jet stream normally crosses an occluded, not a warm, front.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which type clouds may be associated with the jetstream?

choices.text: Cumulonimbus cloud line where the jetstream crosses the cold front.
Cirrus clouds on the equatorial side of the jetstream.
Cirrostratus cloud band on the polar side and under the jetstream.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 공기는 jet core 주위를 corkscrew 형태로 이동하며 equatorial side에서 상승한다. 상층 수분이 충분하면 jet stream의 equatorial side에 cirrus가 형성된다.
questions.explanation_en: Air travels in a “corkscrew” path around the jet stream with upward motion on the equatorial side. Thus, when high-level moisture is available, cirrus clouds form on the equatorial side of the jet stream. Answer (A) is incorrect. Cirriform, not cumulonimbus, clouds are associated with the jet stream. Answer (C) is incorrect. Cirrostratus clouds form on the equatorial, not polar, side of the jet stream.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A strong wind shear can be expected

choices.text: on the low pressure side of a 100-knot jetstream core.
where the horizontal wind shear is 15 knots, in a distance equal to 2.5° longitude.
if the 5°C isotherms are spaced 100 NM or closer together.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Jet core에서 바깥쪽으로 갈수록 풍속이 감소하며, 감소율은 equatorial side보다 polar(low-pressure) side에서 더 크다. 따라서 100-kt jet core의 저기압측에서 강한 wind shear를 예상할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Wind speed decreases outward from the jet stream core, and the rate of decrease is greater on the polar (low-pressure) side than on the equatorial (high-pressure) side. Thus, a strong wind shear can be expected on the low-pressure side of a 100-kt. jet stream core. Answer (B) is incorrect. On a tropopause data chart, a strong wind shear can be expected where the horizontal wind shear is greater than 18 kt., not 15 kt., in a distance equal to 2.5° longitude (or about 150 NM). Answer (C) is incorrect. On a tropopause data chart, a strong wind shear can be expected if the 20-kt. isotachs, not 5°C isotherms, are spaced 100 NM or closer.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The tropopause is generally found when the free air temperatures are
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 표준대기에서 tropopause는 약 -56.5°C, 고도 약 36,000 ft로 본다.
questions.explanation_en: In a standard atmosphere, the tropopause has a temperature of -56.5°C and a height of about 36,000 feet above the Earth. While both the temperature and altitude ranges of the tropopause are quite large, this answer choice is the best answer to the question given its inclusion of the standard temperature for the tropopause. Answer (B) is incorrect. In a standard atmosphere, the tropopause has a temperature of -56.5°C, which is outside of the range defined by this answer choice. Answer (C) is incorrect. In a standard atmosphere, the tropopause has a temperature of -56.5°C, which is warmer than the temperature defined by this answer choice.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The three jet streams are

choices.text: the polar front jetstream, the subtropical jetstream, and the polar night jetstream.
the polar front jetstream, the subtropical jetstream, and the polar jetstream.
the polar jetstream, the Tropic of Cancer jetstream, and the Maritime jetstream.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 주요 jet stream에는 polar front jet, subtropical jet, polar night jet이 있다. Polar front jet은 극기단과 열대기단의 경계, subtropical jet은 대략 북위 20~30° 부근, polar night jet은 겨울철 Arctic Circle 부근 stratosphere에서 나타난다.
questions.explanation_en: There are three jetstreams. The polar front jetstream is associated with the polar front or the division between the cold polar and warm tropical air masses. The subtropical jetstream is a very persistent circumpolar jetstream found on the northern periphery of the tropical latitudes between 20° and 30° north latitude. The polar night jetstream is found in the stratosphere in the vicinity of the Arctic Circle during the winter months. Answer (B) is incorrect. There is a polar front jetstream, but there is no polar jetstream. Answer (C) is incorrect. The Tropic of Cancer is the most northerly circle of latitude on Earth. At this location, the Sun may appear directly overhead at its highest or lowest point. There is no Maritime jetstream. There are maritime air masses which are moist air masses located over water.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: In the mid-latitudes, wind speed in the jet stream averages considerably less in the
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 중위도 jet stream의 평균 풍속은 여름보다 겨울에 훨씬 강하다.
questions.explanation_en: In mid-latitudes, wind speed in the jet stream averages considerably stronger in winter than in summer. Answer (A) is incorrect. The jet stream averages considerably less in summer. Answer (B) is incorrect. The jet stream averages considerably stronger in winter.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which type jet stream can be expected to cause the greater turbulence?

choices.text: A curving jet stream associated with a deep low pressure trough.
A straight jet stream associated with a high pressure ridge.
A jet stream associated with a wide isotherm spacing.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Jet stream cirrus shield는 turbulence와 연관된다. 지상·상층 저기압이 깊어질수록 광범위한 cirrus가 생기고 이런 발달계에서 난류도 가장 강해질 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The jet stream cirrus shield is its association with turbulence. Extensive cirrus cloudiness often occurs with deepening surface and upper lows. These deepening systems produce the greatest turbulence. Answer (B) is incorrect. Jet streams are normally boomerang shaped and not straight. Answer (C) is incorrect. Wide isotherm spacing indicates wind speeds are lower than the contour lines that are closer together.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The decrease in wind speed from the core of the jet stream is the greatest on

choices.text: the acute angle side of the jet stream.
the equatorial side of the jet stream.
the polar side of the jet stream.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Jet core에서 풍속이 감소하는 비율과 wind shear는 equatorial side보다 polar side에서 더 크다.
questions.explanation_en: The rate of decreased wind speed is considerably greater on the polar side than on the equatorial side. The magnitude of wind shear is greater on the polar side than on the equatorial side. Answer (A) is incorrect. The rate of decreased wind speed is considerably greater on the polar side. Answer (B) is incorrect. The rate of decreased wind speed is less on the equatorial side than on the polar side.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: An upper level wind cannot be considered a jet stream unless the wind speed is at least
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 정의상 jet stream은 집중된 풍속이 50 kt 이상이어야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: By definition, the concentrated winds must be 50 knots or greater to be classified as a jet stream. Answer (A) is incorrect. To be classified as a jet stream, concentrated winds must be 50 knots or greater, not 35 knots. Answer (C) is incorrect. Although 65 knots winds may be present within a jet stream, to be classified as a jet stream, the concentrated winds must be 50 knots or greater.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: With high altitude moisture present, cirrus clouds will form

choices.text: on the acute angle side of the jet stream.
on the equatorial side of the jet stream.
on the polar side of the jet stream.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Jet core 주위 공기는 corkscrew 경로를 따르며 equatorial side에서 상승한다. 상층 수분이 충분하면 그쪽에 cirriform cloud가 형성된다.
questions.explanation_en: Air travels in a corkscrew path around the jet core with upward motion on the equatorial side. When high level moisture is available, cirriform clouds form on the equatorial side of the jet stream. Answer (A) is incorrect. Cirriform clouds form on the equatorial side of the jet stream whenever high level moisture is present. Answer (C) is incorrect. Cirriform clouds form on the equatorial side of the jet stream.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The tropopause varies in height from

choices.text: 15,000 feet or below at the poles to 70,000 feet at the equator.
20,000 feet or below at the poles to 65,000 feet at the equator.
32,000 feet or below at the poles to 320,000 feet at the equator.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Tropopause 고도는 극지방 약 20,000 ft에서 적도 부근 약 65,000 ft까지 변하며, 일반적으로 겨울보다 여름에 높다.
questions.explanation_en: The height of the tropopause varies in height from about 20,000 feet over the poles to about 65,000 feet over the equator. It is higher in the summer than in winter. Answer (A) is incorrect. The stratosphere is beyond 65,000 feet over the equator. Answer (C) is incorrect. Above 65,000 feet lie the stratosphere, mesosphere, and thermosphere.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which area or areas of the Northern Hemisphere experience a generally east to west movement of weather systems?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 약 북위 30°의 고압대에서 지상 공기가 북·남으로 퍼지고, 남하하는 공기는 Coriolis force로 편향되어 subtropical northeast trade wind가 된다. 약 60°N 이상에서는 차갑고 무거운 공기가 남하하며 오른쪽으로 편향되어 polar easterly가 형성된다.
questions.explanation_en: The high-pressure belt at about 30° north latitude forces air outward at the surface to the north and to the south. The southward moving air is deflected by the Coriolis force, becoming the well-known subtropical northeast (moving northeast to southwest) trade winds. In the arctic region (60° north latitude and above), the heavier, denser air moves south at a low level toward the Equator but is turned to the right by the Coriolis force, causing the low-level polar easterlies (moving east to west). Answer (A) is incorrect. In the Northern Hemisphere, both the arctic and subtropical areas experience a general east-to-west movement of weather systems. Answer (C) is incorrect. In the Northern Hemisphere, both the arctic and subtropical areas experience a general east-to-west movement of weather systems.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Summer thunderstorms in the arctic region will generally move

choices.text: northeast to southwest in polar easterlies.
southwest to northeast with the jetstream flow.
directly north to south with the low-level polar airflow.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 북극 내륙의 여름 오후에는 scattered cumulus가 뇌우로 발달할 수 있다. 이 뇌우는 polar easterly를 따라 보통 북동에서 남서로 이동해 중위도의 일반적 이동방향과 반대가 될 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: During summer afternoons, scattered cumulus clouds forming over the interior of the arctic region occasionally grow into thunderstorms. These thunderstorms generally move from northeast to southwest in the polar easterlies, which is opposite the general movement in midlatitudes. Answer (B) is incorrect. Thunderstorms in the Arctic generally move northeast to southwest in the polar easterlies, not southwest to northeast with the jet stream flow. Answer (C) is incorrect. Thunderstorms in the Arctic generally move northeast to southwest in polar easterlies, not directly north to south.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which arctic flying hazard is caused when a cloud layer of uniform thickness overlies a snow or ice covered surface?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Whiteout은 균일한 구름층이 눈·얼음으로 덮인 지면 위에 있을 때 Arctic에서 발생하는 시정장애이다. 확산광 때문에 그림자와 깊이감이 사라져 지형·수평선 판단이 매우 어려워진다.
questions.explanation_en: Whiteout is a visibility-restricting phenomenon that occurs in the Arctic when a cloud layer of uniform thickness overlies a snow-or ice-covered surface. Parallel rays of the sun are broken up and diffused when passing through the cloud layer so that they strike the snow surface from many angles, resulting in a loss of depth perception. Answer (A) is incorrect. Ice fog forms in moist air during extremely cold conditions. It is not formed by a cloud layer overlying a snow-covered surface. Answer (C) is incorrect. Blowing snow is snow that is blown by light or greater winds, causing decreased visibility. It is not formed by a cloud layer overlying a snow-covered surface.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Whiteout conditions occur when

choices.text: light is reflected back and forth countless times between snow and clouds, eliminating all shadows.
the low angle of the sun’s rays strike the snow surface and eliminate shadows to the eye due to the “prism effect.”
snow eliminates the color contrast of the surface and clouds during daytime.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Whiteout에서는 구름층을 통과한 태양광이 확산되어 눈 표면과 구름 사이에서 반복 반사되면서 그림자가 사라지고 depth perception이 크게 저하된다.
questions.explanation_en: “Whiteout” is a visibility restricting phenomenon that occurs in the Arctic when a layer of cloudiness of uniform thickness overlies a snow or ice covered surface. Parallel rays of the sun are broken up and diffused when passing through the cloud layer so that they strike the snow surface from many angles. The diffused light then reflects back and forth countless times between the snow and the cloud, eliminating all shadows. Answer (B) is incorrect. In the phenomenon known as “whiteout,” parallel rays of the sun are broken up and diffused when passing through the cloud layer so that they strike the snow surface from many angles. The diffused light then reflects back and forth countless times between the snow and the cloud, eliminating all shadows. Answer (C) is incorrect. The result of “whiteout” is a loss of depth perception. Buildings, people, and dark colored objects appear to float in the air, and the horizon disappears.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A cyclone is

choices.text: a hurricane force storm in the Indian Ocean with highest sustained winds of 64 knots or higher.
a tropical depression in the Northwest Pacific with sustained winds of 63 knots.
a tropical storm in the Atlantic with highest sustained winds of 35 through 64 knots.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Tropical cyclone은 열대 해상에서 발생한 회전성 저기압의 총칭이다. 1분 평균 최대 지속풍속에 따라 Tropical Depression은 33 kt 이하, Tropical Storm은 34~63 kt, Hurricane/Cyclone/Typhoon은 64 kt 이상으로 분류한다. 지역에 따라 Atlantic/eastern Pacific은 hurricane, western Pacific은 typhoon, Indian Ocean·호주 부근은 cyclone이라 부른다.
questions.explanation_en: Tropical cyclone is a general term for any low that originates over tropical oceans. Tropical cyclones are classified according to their intensity based on average 1-minute wind speeds. Tropical cyclone international classifications are 1. Tropical Depression–highest sustained winds up to 33 knots; 2. Tropical Storm–highest sustained winds of 34 through 63 knots; and 3. Hurricane, Cyclone, or Typhoon–highest sustained winds 64 knots or more. Strong tropical cyclones are known by different names in different regions of the world. A tropical cyclone in the Atlantic and eastern Pacific is a “hurricane”; in the western Pacific, “typhoon”; near Australia and in the Indian Ocean, simply “cyclone.” Answer (B) is incorrect. A tropical depression is defined by having sustained winds up to 33 knots, not 63 knots. Answer (C) is incorrect. A tropical storm is classified according to intensity based on average 1-minute maximum sustained wind speed. At 64 knots, the cyclone will be designated as a hurricane.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which weather condition is present when the tropical storm is upgraded to a hurricane?

choices.text: A clear area or hurricane eye has formed.
Sustained winds of 64 knots or more.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Hurricane으로 분류되려면 최대 지속풍속이 64 kt 이상이어야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Tropical cyclones are classified by their intensity based on average 1-min. wind speeds. To be classified as a hurricane, the cyclone must have sustained winds of 64 kt. or more. Answer (A) is incorrect. Tropical cyclones are classified based on the sustained winds, not the highest wind speed. Answer (B) is incorrect. A clear area, or eye, usually forms in the tropical storm stage and continues through the hurricane stage.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the general direction of movement of a hurricane located in the Caribbean or Gulf of Mexico region?

choices.text: Westerly, until encountering land, then easterly.
Counterclockwise over open water, then dissipating outward over land.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Caribbean 또는 Gulf of Mexico의 hurricane은 저위도에서 보통 서~북서로 이동하다가 중위도로 올라가면 prevailing westerlies의 영향으로 북동쪽으로 recurvature한다.
questions.explanation_en: Hurricanes located in the Caribbean or Gulf of Mexico move in a direction between west and northwest while in low latitudes. As the hurricane moves toward the midlatitudes, the prevailing westerlies will gain control, and the hurricane will curve to the northeast. Answer (B) is incorrect. A hurricane will curve easterly because of prevailing winds, not because of land. Answer (C) is incorrect. The windflow in the hurricane is counterclockwise, not the general movement of the hurricane itself.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A cyclone is similar to a tropical storm in

choices.text: the northern Pacific with winds up to 64 knots.
the Indian Ocean with winds 65 knots or more.
the north Atlantic with winds 35 to 64 knots.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Indian Ocean에서 최대 지속풍속 약 64~65 kt 이상의 강한 tropical cyclone은 cyclone이라 부른다.
questions.explanation_en: A strong tropical cyclone (with winds of 65 knots or more) is known in the Indian Ocean as a “cyclone.” Answer (A) is incorrect. Systems with winds up to 64 knots are known as “tropical storms” and not “cyclones.” Also, this answer references the Pacific Ocean, but “cyclones” as referred to in this question exist in the Indian Ocean. Answer (C) is incorrect. Systems with winds from 35 to 64 knots are known as “tropical storms” and not “cyclones.” Also, this answer references the Atlantic Ocean, but “cyclones” as referred to in this question exist in the Indian Ocean.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A hurricane has formed when

choices.text: the highest sustained winds are 64 knots or more.
the winds around a pressure storm have averaged 48 knots for over 48 hours.
the barometric pressure in the center of the storm is 35 mb lower than pressure outside the weather feature.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Hurricane 또는 typhoon의 최대 지속풍속 기준은 64 kt 이상이다.
questions.explanation_en: A hurricane or typhoon has the highest sustained winds of 64 knots or more. Answer (B) is incorrect. A tropical storm has a highest sustained wind of 34 through 63 knots. The length of time is not an issue. Answer (C) is incorrect. The category of a storm is based on the sustained wind speed, not mb pressures.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Tropical storms form when

choices.text: a system of air surrounds an area with pressure of 48 mb.
a system has sustained winds of 34 to 63 knots.
a system has peak wind gusts that do not exceed 65 knots.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Tropical storm의 최대 지속풍속 기준은 34~63 kt이다.
questions.explanation_en: The classification of a tropical storm is based upon sustained winds of 34 through 63 knots. Answer (A) is incorrect. Classification of tropical cyclones are not based on areas of pressure. They are based on sustained wind speed. Answer (C) is incorrect. Each tropical storm classification is based upon the lowest sustained wind speed to the highest sustained wind speed, not peak gusts that do not exceed a certain speed.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A tropical cyclone is

choices.text: a tropical storm in the north Atlantic west of Newfoundland with highest sustained winds of 25 through 33 knots.
a tropical depression in the Northern Pacific near Dutch Harbor with sustained winds of 63 knots.
a hurricane force storm in the Pacific Ocean southwest of Hawaii with highest sustained winds of 65 knots or higher.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 최대 지속풍속 64 kt 이상의 회전성 열대 저기압은 hurricane/cyclone/typhoon 등으로 분류되는 강한 tropical cyclone이다. 국제 분류는 depression ≤33 kt, storm 34~63 kt, hurricane/cyclone/typhoon ≥64 kt이다.
questions.explanation_en: A hurricane force storm in the area stated, with sustained winds of 64 knots or higher, may be classified as a tropical cyclone. Tropical cyclone is a general term for a rotating, organized system of clouds and thunderstorms that originates over tropical or subtropical waters. The tropical cyclone international classifications include: 1. Tropical Depression – highest sustained winds up to 33 knots 2. Tropical Storm – highest sustained winds of 34 to 63 knots 3. Hurricane, Cyclone, or Typhoon – highest sustained winds 64 knots or more Answer (A) is incorrect. A tropical storm has highest sustained winds of 34 through 63 knots, not 25 through 34 knots. Answer (B) is incorrect. A tropical depression has sustained winds of up to 33 knots, not 63 knots.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Gusts in tropical cyclones can exceed the average one-minute wind speed by as much as
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Tropical cyclone은 1분 평균 풍속으로 강도를 분류하며, 순간 gust는 이 평균풍속보다 최대 약 50% 더 강할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Tropical cyclones are classified according to their intensity based on average one-minute wind speeds. Wind gusts in these storms may be as much as 50% higher than the average one-minute wind speeds. Answer (B) is incorrect. Wind gusts in these storms may be as much as 50% higher than the average one-minute wind speeds, not 75%. Answer (C) is incorrect. Wind gusts in these storms may be as much as 50% higher than the average one-minute wind speeds, not 100%.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which weather condition is present when a tropical storm is upgraded to a typhoon?

choices.text: Winds around the pressure center have averaged 48 knots or more for 48 continuous hours.
The storm has sustained winds of 64 knots or more.
Barometric pressure at the center is 35 mb lower than the surrounding pressure.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Hurricane 또는 typhoon으로 분류되려면 최대 지속풍속이 64 kt 이상이어야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: To be categorized as a hurricane or a typhoon, the storm must have highest sustained winds of 64 knots or more. Answer (A) is incorrect. With winds of 48 knots, this storm would be a tropical storm, not a typhoon. Answer (C) is incorrect. Storm classification is not based on barometric pressure but on sustained wind speed.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which type of weather can only be directly observed during flight and then reported in a PIREP?

choices.text: Level of the tropopause and turbulence.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 조종사는 직접 관측한 뇌우, structural icing, turbulence, wind shear, cloud base/top/layer, visibility, precipitation, 바람, 고도별 온도 등을 자발적으로 PIREP으로 보고하는 것이 권장된다.
questions.explanation_en: Pilots are urged to volunteer directly observed reports of thunderstorms, structural icing, turbulence, wind shear, cloud bases (tops and layers), visibility, precipitation, wind, and temperature at altitude. Answer (B) is incorrect. A pilot would not be able to determine from observation if jet stream-type winds were encountered. Answer (C) is incorrect. The level of the tropopause is determined by radiosondes released by ground weather observing stations. It is not a type of weather that can be directly observed by a pilot during flight.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What type turbulence should be reported when it momentarily causes slight, erratic changes in altitude and/or attitude, one-third to two-thirds of the time?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Light turbulence는 고도나 자세에 순간적이고 경미한 불규칙 변화가 생기는 정도이다. Intermittent는 전체 시간의 약 1/3~2/3 동안 발생함을 뜻한다.
questions.explanation_en: Light turbulence is defined as turbulence that momentarily causes slight, erratic changes in altitude and/or attitude. Intermittent is defined as occurring from one-third to two-thirds of the time. Answer (A) is incorrect. Light chop does not cause any appreciable changes in altitude and/or attitude, and occasional is less than one-third of the time. Answer (B) is incorrect. Moderate chop does not cause any appreciable changes in altitude and/or attitude.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What type turbulence should be reported when it causes slight, rapid, and somewhat rhythmic bumpiness without appreciable changes in attitude or altitude, less than one-third of the time?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Light chop은 고도·자세의 뚜렷한 변화 없이 작고 빠르며 비교적 규칙적인 흔들림이다. Occasional은 전체 시간의 1/3 미만 동안 발생한다는 뜻이다.
questions.explanation_en: Light chop is turbulence that causes slight, rapid, and somewhat rhythmic bumpiness without appreciable changes in attitude or altitude. Occasional is defined as occurring less than one-third of the time. Answer (B) is incorrect. Moderate turbulence causes a change in the aircraft’s attitude and/or altitude. Answer (C) is incorrect. Moderate chop causes rapid, not rhythmic, bumps or jolts, which are not “slight.”

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What type turbulence should be reported when it causes changes in altitude and/or attitude more than two-thirds of the time, with the aircraft remaining in positive control at all times?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Moderate turbulence는 고도나 자세 변화가 발생하지만 항공기는 항상 positive control 상태를 유지하는 정도이다. Continuous는 전체 시간의 2/3보다 많이 발생함을 뜻한다.
questions.explanation_en: Moderate turbulence is defined as turbulence that causes changes in altitude and/or attitude, but the aircraft remains in positive control at all times. Continuous is defined as occurring more than two-thirds of the time. Answer (A) is incorrect. Severe chop is not a turbulence reporting term. Answer (C) is incorrect. Intermittent means that turbulence is occurring from one-third to two-thirds of the time.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: KFTW UA/OV DFW/TM 1645/FL100/TP PA30/ SK SCT031- TOP043/BKN060-TOP085/OVC097- TOPUNKN/WX FV00SM RA/TA 07. This pilot report to Fort Worth (KFTW) indicates

choices.text: the ceiling at KDFW is 6,000 feet.
that the top of the ceiling is 4,300 feet.
the aircraft is in light rain.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Ceiling은 가장 낮은 BKN/OVC 층 또는 obscuration 속 vertical visibility의 높이이다. PIREP의 BKN060은 6,000 ft MSL을 뜻하며, PIREP 고도는 별도 표시가 없으면 MSL이다.
questions.explanation_en: A ceiling is defined as the height (AGL) of the lowest broken or overcast layer aloft or vertical visibility into an obscuration. The PIREP reports the lowest broken layer at 6,000 ft. MSL (BKN060). This indicates the ceiling is 6,000 ft. A ceiling is normally defined as the height above ground, but in a PIREP all altitudes are MSL unless otherwise indicated. Answer (B) is incorrect. The top of the scattered (SCT) layer, not the broken (BKN) layer is 4,300 ft. A ceiling is the lowest broken or overcast layer aloft. Answer (C) is incorrect. The flight visibility and weather (/WX) section of the PIREP is coded as /WX FV00SM RA, which means the flight visibility is 0 SM in rain. Light rain would be coded as -RA.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Maximum Turbulence Potential forecasts

choices.text: are only as accurate as the computer model.
exhibit the same accuracy during all 24 hours of the day.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 이 turbulence forecast 제품은 여러 turbulence indicator를 ensemble로 결합하므로 단일 지표보다 다양한 난류 원인을 반영할 수 있다. 정확도는 입력되는 computer model 자료의 정확도에 좌우된다.
questions.explanation_en: This product is based on an ensemble of turbulence indicators and, therefore, can capture more diverse sources of turbulence and provide a more reliable forecast than can be provided by a single indicator. The accuracy of the product depends on the accuracy of the computer model output used to create it. Answer (B) is incorrect. The accuracy of the analysis is dependent on PIREPs, which are fewer at night, causing the accuracy of the forecast to decrease. Answer (C) is incorrect. The product is only for turbulence associated with upper level fronts and jet streams while other known causes of turbulence are not forecast.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What determines how icing is reported on a PIREP?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Icing intensity는 얼음이 축적되는 속도에 따라 분류한다.
questions.explanation_en: Icing intensities are classified based on the rate of icing accumulation. Answer (A) is incorrect. The type of icing accumulation can be listed in the PIREP remarks, but not in the primary icing group. Answer (B) is incorrect. The thickness of ice would likely not be reported in a PIREP since that information does not provide direct information to pilots on what conditions to expect. Also, it is usually very difficult for a pilot to accurately estimate the thickness of the accumulated ice.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is indicated by the following report? TYR UUA/OV TYR180015/TM 1757/FL310/TP B737/TB MOD-SEV CAT 350-390

choices.text: An urgent pilot report for moderate to severe clear air turbulence.
A routine pilot report for overcast conditions from flight levels 350-390.
A special METAR issued on the 18th day of the month at 1757Z.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. PIREP의 UUA는 Urgent Upper Air report를 뜻하고, '/TB MOD-SEV CAT 350-390'은 FL350~390에서 moderate to severe clear-air turbulence가 있음을 의미한다.
questions.explanation_en: The UUA found in first section of the report indicates an “Urgent Upper Air” report. The /TB MOD-SEV CAT 350-390 in the last section of the report indicates moderate to severe clear air turbulence for flight levels 350 to 390. Answer (B) is incorrect. If the report is a routine report code UA would be used in the first section instead of UUA. Answer (C) is incorrect. The second section of the PIREP containing 1800 is the location section. In this example, /OV TYR 180015 indicates that the location of the weather-related phenomenon is on the 180 degree radial of the TYR VOR at 15 nautical miles. A METAR is an aviation routine weather report; however, METAR coding is used to describe weather and visibility phenomena in the PIREP.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The Hazardous Inflight Weather Advisory Service (HIWAS) is a continuous broadcast over selected VORs of

choices.text: SIGMETs, CONVECTIVE SIGMETs, AIRMETs, Severe Weather Forecast Alerts (AWW), and Center Weather Advisories (CWA).
SIGMETs, CONVECTIVE SIGMETs, AIRMETs, Wind Shear Advisories, and Severe Weather Forecast Alerts (AWW).
Wind Shear Advisories, Radar Weather Reports, SIGMETs, CONVECTIVE SIGMETs, AIRMETs, and Center Weather Advisories (CWA).

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. HIWAS는 선택된 VOR를 통해 SIGMET, Convective SIGMET, AIRMET, severe weather forecast alert, CWA 등 비행 중 기상 advisory를 지속 방송하는 서비스이다.
questions.explanation_en: The Hazardous Inflight Weather Advisory Service (HIWAS) is a continuous broadcast service over selected VORs of in-flight weather advisories, i.e., SIGMETs, convective SIGMETs, AIRMETs, severe weather forecast alerts (AWW), and center weather advisories (CWA). Answer (B) is incorrect. A runway wind shear advisory is given by a tower controller, not HIWAS, to arriving and departing aircraft. Answer (C) is incorrect. Radar weather reports are available from Flight Service Stations (FSSs), not HIWAS.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: En route weather advisories should be obtained from an FSS on
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. FSS는 항로비행 항공기와의 공통 통신 주파수로 122.2 MHz를 제공한다.
questions.explanation_en: Flight Service Stations (FSSs) provide communications capabilities for aircraft flying en route on a common frequency of 122.2 MHz. Answer (A) is incorrect. A remote frequency normally used by FSS at a NAVAID site is 122.1 MHz. A pilot transmits on 122.1 MHz, and the FSS receives on this frequency. The FSS transmits back to the pilot on the NAVAID frequency. Answer (C) is incorrect. The CTAF frequency used by an FSS located on an airport without an operating control tower is 123.6 MHz.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
